# Japan by Station: full text of every guide

> English Japan travel guides organised around train stations. Each guide shows the date its facts were checked. Source: https://japanbystation.com

## Depachika 101: How Japan's Department-Store Food Halls Work
URL: https://japanbystation.com/depachika-japan-food-halls-how-they-work
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-25

Key facts:
- Hours: Isetan Shinjuku food hall (B1) 10:00–20:00; Daimaru Tokyo B1F–11F 10:00–20:00; Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi B1 and 1F to 19:30 (checked 24 Nov 2026).
- Restaurant floors: Isetan Shinjuku Eat Paradise 7F 11:00–22:00; Daimaru Tokyo 12F 11:00–22:00 and 13F to 23:00.
- Tax-free: since 1 Nov 2026 you pay tax at the till and get it back after customs checks your goods at departure; minimum ¥5,000 before tax per store per day; food eaten in Japan doesn't count.

If you only do one food thing in a Japanese city that isn't a restaurant, make it the basement of a big department store. A depachika is dozens of separate counters under one roof: a famous yokan maker next to a bento kitchen next to a wine cellar. Walk it in the order below, go in the last hour if you want deals, and keep your receipts if anything is going home in your suitcase.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Floor by floor: what's actually down there
We'll use Isetan Shinjuku's B1 as the model, because its floor guide spells it out. Most big stores follow the same pattern.
Sweets first. Western pâtisseries on one side, wagashi and tea on the other. This is where the gift boxes live. At Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi, Toraya's bamboo-wrapped yokan "Yoru no Ume" is ¥3,024 and a Mon Cher Dojima Roll is ¥1,782.
Prepared food and bento. Isetan has about 50 deli and bento shops. Daimaru Tokyo, right on top of Tokyo Station, says its B1F brings in about 1,000 new bento a year, some made in front of you. It's the place to buy lunch for the Shinkansen.
Bakeries. Isetan alone has seven.
Fresh market. Fruit, fish and meat sold like a very good grocer. Mitsukoshi's buyers list Asakusa Imahan wagyu for sukiyaki at ¥10,800 for 600 g.
Sake, wine and craft beer. Isetan's wine and spirits corner holds about 1,900 bottles and has a sommelier.
Ready-to-eat counters like this are where the evening stickers appear first.
One counter that surprises first-timers is Mitsukoshi's Kayuan: it sells regional sweets from all over Japan, so you can taste a Kyushu or Tohoku speciality without leaving Tokyo.
Free tastings and the evening markdowns
Tastings. The Japan National Tourism Organization tells visitors to keep an eye out for free samples. Time Out Tokyo found tasting counters in Isetan's fresh market, from ham and sausage to oden. Not every tasting is free: some counters run paid tastings of their most expensive items. Take a sample, say thank you, and don't feel you have to buy.
Markdowns. No store publishes a time, and each counter decides its own cut. Time Out suggests going 30 to 60 minutes before closing, when most ready-to-eat food is discounted. A 2013 President report on Tobu Ikebukuro found ¥100-off and half-price stickers half an hour before its 21:00 close. Bento, sushi and deli go first. Sweets and gift boxes keep longer, so they rarely drop.
Sweets keep longer, so their prices rarely drop at closing time.
Our suggestion: sweets and gifts in the morning, when the shelves are full. Come back for dinner food in the last hour.
Eat it there, or take it away?
Mostly take-away, and eating by the display cases is frowned upon. In 2021, Tokyu Toyoko got so many complaints about shoppers eating by the counters that it added standing tables with bins. Look for the proper eat-in spots instead:
Isetan Shinjuku B1: a Kitchen Stage whose chef's menu changes every two to three weeks, a craft beer bar, wine tasting counters, Jean-Paul Hévin's chocolate bar and Toraya's café.
Daimaru Tokyo: some B1F bento shops have small counters for food made to order.
Mitsukoshi: HiO Ice Cream has an eat-in (¥495).
Paper bags on the Mitsukoshi Isetan food floors have cost a little extra since 2020 (¥30–50 when the fee started), so bring a foldable bag.
The restaurant floors upstairs
Take the lift to the top for proper sit-down meals with longer hours than the shops below:
Isetan Shinjuku
7F
Eat Paradise
11:00–22:00. Food hall B1 10:00–20:00.
Daimaru Tokyo
12–13F
Late by Tokyo Station
12F 11:00–22:00 (about 16 restaurants), 13F to 23:00. Food floors 10:00–20:00; closed 1–2 Jan.
Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi
7F + new bldg
Shop late, eat later
Main building 7F 11:00–19:00; new building B1, 9F, 10F to 22:00. B1 and 1F shops open to 19:30.
One perfect wagashi, the kind of thing you buy by the piece downstairs.
📅 Good to know: tax-free changed on 1 November 2026
You now pay tax at the till. Under the Japan Tourism Agency's refund system, the store registers your purchase. You get the tax back after customs confirms the goods are leaving Japan: scan your passport at the airport, before you check your bags, within 90 days of buying.
Minimum ¥5,000 before tax, same store, same day. Food and other items now count together, and the old sealed bags are gone (National Tax Agency).
Eat it here and the refund is gone. Food eaten in Japan doesn't qualify. If any item from a transaction is missing at customs, nothing on that transaction is refunded, so keep gift boxes together and unopened.
Stores can take a cut. Takashimaya, for example, registers purchases at its counter on the day of purchase and deducts a handling fee of 23% of the tax amount.
One more thing: the sweets that arrive on set days
Some cult sweets don't come in every day. Mitsukoshi's buyers note that Kamakura Benitaya's Kurumikko (walnut caramel cakes) is restocked on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays. Akasaka Kakiyama's Himeenza rice crackers aren't sold at all from November to January. If a box is on your list, check the store's restock days before you go. Kyoto's station store runs a whole schedule like this (see our Kyoto Station food hall guide).
Source: Nihonbashi Mitsukoshi "depachika meikan" buyer feature (mistore.jp), checked 24 November 2026.
We don't earn anything from the stores on this page. Prices, hours and tax rules change, so check the official sites before you go.

## Fukuoka Yatai: How They Work, and Nakasu, Tenjin or Nagahama?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-yatai-how-they-work
City: Fukuoka · Facts checked: 2026-11-25

Key facts:
- About 100 yatai (101 on 1 Apr 2026); most open 18:30–19:00 and close around midnight; no fixed holidays, many close in rain (Fukuoka City).
- Cash: most stalls take cash only; about 10% take cards; order at least one drink and one dish each (gofukuoka.jp).
- Rules: stalls may use the street only from 17:00 to 4:00, setup included, inside 3 m × 2.5 m (city operating rules).

For a first yatai night, we'd start in Tenjin: the most variety, a short walk from the station, and stalls like Kokinchan that are famous for yaki-ramen. Go to Nakasu if you want the classic picture of lanterns on the river, and to Nagahama if you want ramen with fewer people. Wherever you go, bring cash, arrive around 18:00 to 19:00, and plan to visit two or three stalls, not one.
About a 5-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who yatai suit, and who they don't
Good fit
Solo travellers and pairs: groups of two or three are ideal, and solo is fine
Anyone who likes talking to strangers: you sit elbow to elbow
Food hoppers who want three small meals, not one big one
Think twice
Groups of five or more: there are only about ten seats per stall
Rainy nights: many stalls simply don't open
If you need a toilet nearby: stalls have none (ask staff for the nearest)
How a yatai works
Fukuoka has about 100 yatai (101 on the city's count in April 2026). Since 2013 they have been run under a city ordinance, Japan's first of its kind. A stall may only use the street from 17:00 to 4:00 next morning, setting up and packing away included, and everything, seats too, has to fit inside 3 m × 2.5 m (city rules).
Hours: some stalls open at 18:00, most at 18:30 to 19:00, and most close around midnight. There are no fixed holidays. Each stall decides, and many close in rain or storms (official guide).
Getting a seat: ask "two people, OK?" If there's a queue, join the end.
Ordering: check the prices, then order at least one drink and one dish per person. That's the polite minimum. Most stalls have no cover charge, but some bar-style yatai do.
Paying: pay when you leave. Most stalls are cash only, and only about 10% take credit cards. Some newer ones take QR payments like PayPay.
Manners: travel light, sit close, don't take food away, don't linger once you've finished, then try another stall.
Ten seats, one cook and your neighbours' elbows: the whole point of a yatai.
Nakasu, Tenjin or Nagahama?
A · The classic scene
Nakasu
Lanterns on the Naka River
A row of about 20 stalls at the south end of Nakasu Island, about 5 to 8 minutes from Nakasu-Kawabata or Kushida Shrine station. Busiest 19:00 to 22:00. A newer cluster, Ura-Nakasu, has 10 stalls on Showa-dori, about 3 minutes north of the station.
B · Our first-timer pick
Tenjin
Most variety, near the trains
Stalls along Watanabe-dori and Showa-dori, right in the shopping district. Ramen, yaki-ramen and the occasional French stall. Kokinchan is about 2 minutes from Tenjin Station Exit 1.
C · The ramen row
Nagahama
Smaller, by the fish market
The old home of Nagahama tonkotsu ramen. It was down to two stalls by 2021, and seven new ones opened in June 2023. About a 9-minute walk from Akasaka Station.
Verdict: Tenjin for a first night, Nakasu for the photo and the buzz, Nagahama for ramen and a quieter seat. The answer changes if it's raining (stay where you can walk between several stalls quickly) or if you're four or more (go early, around 18:00, or split up).
What to order, and where
Tonkotsu ramen, yakitori and oden are the standards at almost every stall. Yaki-ramen, stir-fried ramen, is the one locals are talking about now. No yatai serves raw food.
Tonkotsu ramen: the yatai standard, best as your last stop.
Kokinchan (Tenjin): yaki-ramen ¥820, mentaiko tamagoyaki ¥750. Tabelog lists Mon–Wed 18:30–1:30, Fri–Sat to 2:00, closed Thursday and Sunday. No cards, but e-money is accepted.
Takechan fr Tsukasa (Seiryu Park, Nakasu): yaki-ramen and a mentaiko omelette made with tonkotsu stock. 18:00–1:00, irregular days off. Some menus are in several languages.
Tenjin Yatai Zonochan (Watanabe-dori): opened April 2025. Hakata ramen, bite-size gyoza and tonkotsu yaki-ramen. 18:15–24:00, cash only.
Mentai Chudoku (Nagahama): Fukuoka's first stall devoted to mentaiko (spicy cod roe). 18:00–24:00, PayPay only.
Yatai no Tamachan (Nagahama): yakitori, oden and Nagahama ramen. 18:30–24:00, weather permitting, QR payments OK.
Oden: point at what looks good in the pot.
An easy three-stall evening
18:00 Walk Watanabe-dori in Tenjin while the stalls finish setting up. It's the best time to get a seat.
18:30 Stall one: yaki-ramen and mentaiko tamagoyaki at Kokinchan (not Thursday or Sunday) or Zonochan, with one drink.
19:30 Walk about 15 minutes east to Nakasu and cross to the river.
20:00 Stall two: yakitori or oden on the riverside row, or try Ura-Nakasu on Showa-dori if the queues are long.
21:30 Stall three: a last bowl of tonkotsu ramen, then a short walk back to Nakasu-Kawabata.
Early evening: Tenjin as the stalls go up
Stall two: skewers and a drink
Late: one more bowl, then home
Where to stay for a yatai night
For the riverside stalls
Nakasu-Kawabata
Walk back in five minutes
Ura-Nakasu is about 3 minutes from the station. Downside: Nakasu is Fukuoka's nightlife district, so pick a room off the main strip.
Fall asleep a lantern-lit stroll from the river →
For the most choice
Tenjin
Stalls, shops and trains together
Watanabe-dori and Showa-dori stalls are on your doorstep, and the subway and Nishitetsu trains start here. Downside: the main streets stay busy day and night.
Base yourself where the yaki-ramen sizzles →
For trains and the airport
Hakata
Quiet nights, easy departures
The airport is about 5 minutes away by subway and Nakasu about 10. Downside: you'll ride back after the last stall instead of walking.
Eat late, still make the morning Shinkansen →
Comparing all three for a first trip? See Where to stay in Fukuoka: Hakata, Tenjin or Nakasu.
🏮 Nervous about ordering? Klook lists a two-hour private Nakasu yatai food tour, so a guide handles the "two people, OK?" and explains the menu.Let a guide get you your first stool by the river →
📅 Good to know before you book
Weather decides. Stalls have no fixed holidays and many close in rain or wind. With two nights in Fukuoka, you get a second chance.
Fridays and Saturdays have the longest waits (japan-guide.com). Arriving between 18:00 and 19:00 is the easiest way in.
New stalls are coming. The city is choosing operators for 23 more spaces across Nakasu, Tenjin and Nagahama, opening in April and May 2027.
Leave your luggage first. Stalls are tiny. Drop bags at the hotel (most hotels offer free cancellation, so booking early costs nothing).
One more thing: a light bulb tells you if a stall is open
Because yatai close for rain, wind or a day off at short notice, Fukuoka City fitted stalls with smart light bulbs. The official LINE account "FUKUOKA GUIDE" uses them to show which stalls are actually open tonight, and you can search the stalls in English by area or by food. Check it before you leave the hotel, not after a wet walk to a dark street. Landing at Fukuoka Airport's international terminal? There's a yatai concierge desk on 1F, open 8:00 to 21:30.
Source: Fukuoka City yatai DX page and gofukuoka.jp, checked 24 November 2026.
Some links on this page are affiliate links. If you book through them, Japan by Station may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. Stall hours and payment change, so check before you go.

## Kyoto Station Food Halls: The Classic Gift vs What Kyoto Buys
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-station-depachika-gifts
City: Kyoto · Facts checked: 2026-11-25

Key facts:
- JR Kyoto Isetan (inside Kyoto Station): 10:00–20:00; B1 sweets, sake and long-established shops, B2 fresh food, deli and bento; Eat Paradise 11F 11:00–22:00.
- Set-day sweets at Isetan B1 (Nov 2026): Imanishiken ohagi Saturdays from 11:00, 3 for ¥721; Nakamuraken mugite-mochi Thursdays and Sundays, 3 for ¥1,053.
- Takashimaya Kyoto 10:30–20:00, food on B1; Tsuruya Yoshinobu's Kyoto-only yokan 3 bars ¥1,274, keeps about a year.

If you only have half an hour before the Shinkansen, go down to JR Kyoto Isetan's B1. It's inside the station, and you'll find the famous yatsuhashi makers next to Kyoto sweet shops whose cakes only arrive on certain days. Go on a Saturday after 11:00 and you can carry home what Kyoto people actually line up for.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026 · new to depachika? Start with Depachika 101
Five pairs: the classic, and the local pick
1. Yatsuhashi vs Saturday ohagi
Classic: baked yatsuhashi, the crisp cinnamon cracker shaped like a koto harp. All three big makers, Izutsu, Shogoin and Honke Nishio, have counters on JR Kyoto Isetan B1. At Daimaru, Shogoin's box of 48 is ¥1,296. Local: Isetan's B1 lists set days for famous Kyoto shops. Imanishiken's ohagi (rice cakes wrapped in red-bean paste, made with the shop's own lightly sweet bean paste) come in on Saturdays from 11:00, ¥721 for three (store list, November 2026).
Fresh mochi sweets keep for a day or two. The baked boxes are the ones that fly home.
2. Matcha everything vs a yokan only Kyoto sells
Classic: matcha sweets. Local: Tsuruya Yoshinobu's Kyoto-only yokan, launched in February 2026. Three bars cost ¥1,274 and five cost ¥2,041. It keeps for about a year and is sold only in Kyoto, including at all three department stores (brand release). It's a sturdy gift for a long flight.
3. Pickles: the famous names
Kyoto tsukemono (pickles) is a whole counter row of its own. Isetan B1 has Kawakatsu, Doi Shibazuke and Daiyasu. Daimaru carries Doi, Nishiri and Daiyasu. At Takashimaya B1, Murakami Juhonten's shibazuke (aubergine pickled purple with red shiso) is ¥600 for 130 g, an easy one to try.
Kyoto pickles on display (this basket is at Nishiki Market). The station stores sell the big names vacuum-packed.
4. Station bento vs a Kyoto restaurant's box
Classic: any ekiben. Local: Isetan B2 carries bento from about 27 long-established restaurant brands, among them Hyotei and Nakamura-ro. Izuu, the Gion saba-zushi house, has a counter here too. A whole roll of its mackerel sushi is ¥4,860 at the main shop. Some say it tastes richer half a day later, which suits a train ride.
5. Ajari-mochi vs the 21st-of-the-month dorayaki
Classic: Mangetsu's ajari-mochi, a chewy bean-paste cake, ¥141 each at Daimaru or ten for ¥1,523 at Takashimaya. Local: Sasaya Iori's dorayaki (¥1,944) is sold at Daimaru Kyoto only on the 20th to 22nd of each month, around Toji's monthly Kobo-san market.
Matcha is the classic. The Kyoto-only boxes are what make the gift.
The three stores at a glance
Inside the station
JR Kyoto Isetan
B1 sweets · B2 deli & bento
10:00–20:00. Eat Paradise restaurants on 11F, 11:00–22:00; more on 7F–10F to 23:00.
Shijo-Karasuma
Daimaru Kyoto
"Gochiso Paradise" basement
About 10:00–20:00 for the food floors; restaurants on 8F to about 22:00 (third-party listing, check before you go).
Shijo-Kawaramachi
Takashimaya
B1 food · 7F dining
10:30–20:00; Dining Garden Kyo-kairo on 7F 11:00–21:30. Store-only boxes on B1.
Daimaru and Takashimaya are downtown, near Nishiki Market, and easy to fit into a sightseeing day. Isetan is the one for your last stop before the train.
Ten minutes before the train
Out of time? On the station's Hachijo side, ASTY Square (2F) is right in front of the Shinkansen central gate. It has 551 Horai, Kyoto dango and a deli-and-gift shop open 7:00–21:00. In Kyoto Porta, the underground mall, Kyo-komachi sits next to the JR central gate and opens 8:30–20:00. There are bento and souvenir shops inside the Shinkansen gates too.
Many of these makers still have their old shops across town. The station counters save you the trip.
Sleeping near the station makes the food hall an easy last stop. Our Kyoto where-to-stay guide compares it with Karasuma and Gion, or you can wake up five minutes from the sweets counters →
📅 Good to know before you shop
Tax-free works differently since 1 November 2026. You pay tax first and get it back after customs checks the goods at departure (minimum ¥5,000 before tax per store per day). Takashimaya Kyoto registers purchases at its 7F counter the same day and deducts a fee of 23% of the tax. Food eaten in Japan doesn't count.
Set days can move. Isetan warns that arrival days change and some items sell out. Demachi Futaba's mame-mochi (2 for ¥560) gives priority to reservations.
Fresh vs baked. Mochi and ohagi are best the same day. Choose baked yatsuhashi or yokan if the box has to survive a week of travel.
One more thing: plan your day around the mochi calendar
Isetan's B1 runs a weekly calendar of Kyoto mochi. Nakamuraken's mugite-mochi (freshly pounded rice cake with kinako to sprinkle on, 3 for ¥1,053) comes in on Thursdays from 11:00 and Sundays from 10:00. Mitamaya's black-syrup dango arrive Thursday to Sunday. Fuka's fu-manju, wrapped in a bamboo leaf, comes six days a week. Time your last station visit to the right day and you'll eat what Kyoto keeps for itself.
Source: JR Kyoto Isetan B1 set-day wagashi list, 1 to 30 November 2026 (mistore.jp), checked 24 November 2026.
One link on this page is an affiliate link. If you book through it, Japan by Station may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. Prices, hours and arrival days change, so check the stores' own pages before you go.

## Shin-Osaka vs Osaka Station: Which One, and Where to Stay
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shin-osaka-vs-osaka-station
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-25

Key facts:
- Two different stations: the Tokaido and Sanyo Shinkansen stop only at Shin-Osaka (platforms 20–27); Osaka Station (Umeda) has no Shinkansen platforms. They are one JR stop apart, about 4 minutes.
- Kyoto from either one: the JR Special Rapid starts at Osaka Station, calls at Shin-Osaka and reaches Kyoto in about 24 minutes from Shin-Osaka; the regular fare is ¥580 from both (JR West, checked 25 Nov 2026).
- Transfer time: JR West advises allowing 11 minutes to change from JR to the Osaka Metro Midosuji Line at Shin-Osaka (Umeda about 6 min, Namba about 16 min).
- Stay by traveller: early Shinkansen → remm Shin-Osaka (directly connected to the Shinkansen Central gate); families → Courtyard by Marriott Shin-Osaka Station (1 min, rooms from 30 m²); budget with a bath → Via Inn Shin-Osaka (3 min from the JR East Exit).

They are not the same station. Shin-Osaka is where every Shinkansen stops; Osaka Station, in Umeda, has no bullet trains at all. They are one JR stop apart, about 4 minutes. Our rule: sleep at Shin-Osaka for one night and an early Shinkansen; sleep at Osaka Station (Umeda) for three nights or more, when your evenings and day trips matter more than the bullet train.
About a 5-minute read · facts checked 25 November 2026
Who a base at Shin-Osaka suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
One night in Osaka between Tokyo and Hiroshima, or the night before an early Shinkansen
Travellers with big suitcases: the station hotels sit at the Shinkansen gates
Day trips on the Shinkansen (Hiroshima, Okayama, Nagoya) with a JR Pass
Anyone who wants a calmer, business-district night
Think twice
First-timers who want to walk out to dinner and nightlife: the area is offices and hotels
Kyoto, Nara or Kobe day trips without a pass: Osaka Station has the same fares and more trains to choose from
Anyone who will ride into the city every evening: 6 to 16 minutes each way on the subway adds up
Shin-Osaka or Osaka Station: which one do you need?
Start from the train you are taking.
Shinkansen (Nozomi, Hikari, Kodama to Tokyo or Nagoya; Mizuho, Sakura to Hiroshima or Hakata): Shin-Osaka only. Tokaido trains (towards Tokyo) use platforms 23 to 27; Sanyo trains (towards Hiroshima) use 20 to 22. The fastest Nozomi from Tokyo takes 2 hours 21 minutes.
Kyoto by JR Special Rapid: both. The train starts at Osaka Station and calls at Shin-Osaka; Kyoto is about 24 minutes from Shin-Osaka and about 29 from Osaka, and the fare is ¥580 from either.
Kyoto by Shinkansen: Shin-Osaka, 13 to 14 minutes on a Hikari, about ¥1,450 in a non-reserved car. Worth it with a JR Pass; without one, you save about 10 minutes for nearly ¥900 more.
Kansai Airport on the HARUKA: both. Since March 2023 the HARUKA also stops at the underground Osaka (Umekita) platforms; JR West puts Osaka to the airport at about 47 minutes.
Namba, Shinsaibashi, Tennoji: Osaka Metro Midosuji Line, which runs through both areas (Shin-Osaka station and Umeda station). From Shin-Osaka it is about 6 minutes to Umeda and about 16 to Namba.
Hankyu, Hanshin, the Loop Line: Osaka Station / Umeda only. See Osaka Station vs Umeda.
Every Shinkansen in Osaka stops at Shin-Osaka, never at Osaka Station.
Our suggestion: type "Shin-Osaka" into your map app whenever a Shinkansen is involved. "Osaka Station" sends you to Umeda, about 4 km away, and walking between the two takes well over half an hour.
Which gate? Start from where you are going
Shin-Osaka's main concourse is on the 3rd floor, with the Shinkansen and JR gates side by side. Go by destination:
Going to Namba, Umeda or Tennoji by subway? Follow the signs for the Midosuji Line at the west end of the concourse. JR West tells you to allow 11 minutes from the JR gates to the subway, so don't plan a 5-minute connection.
Going to remm Shin-Osaka? Leave by the Shinkansen Central gate: the hotel is directly connected to it.
Going to Courtyard by Marriott Shin-Osaka Station? From the Shinkansen Central gate, go out the North Exit and follow the pedestrian deck (about a minute). Off a local JR train, use the East gate.
Going to Via Inn Shin-Osaka or the east-side hotels? Use the JR East Exit; Via Inn is about 3 minutes away. The extra-large coin lockers are on the south side of this exit.
Going to Shin Osaka Washington Hotel Plaza or Via Inn Shomenguchi? Go down to the JR Front Exit on the 1st floor (Via Inn Shomenguchi is also 1 minute from subway Exit 7).
Going on to Osaka Station? Any JR Kyoto Line train towards Osaka, one stop, about 4 minutes.
Tokaido trains leave from platforms 23 to 27, Sanyo trains from 20 to 22: check the direction before you ride up.
Where to stay near Shin-Osaka: one pick per traveller
First Shinkansen of the day
remm Shin-Osaka
Directly on the Shinkansen gate
A Hankyu Hotels property directly connected to the Shinkansen Central gate, 1 minute from the JR East gate and 3 from the Midosuji Line. You can be on the platform minutes after checkout. Downside: compact rooms built for business travellers.
Out of the room and onto the platform in minutes →
Families and big suitcases
Courtyard by Marriott Shin-Osaka Station
Room to open two cases
About a minute from the North Exit over the deck, with rooms from 30 m² (up to 90 m²) and a breakfast buffet from 6:00, per the Osaka Convention and Tourism Bureau. Downside: the price of an international chain.
Spread out before the long ride →
Budget, with a bath
Via Inn Shin-Osaka
A soak after a day of trains
JR West's own hotel brand, about 3 minutes from the JR East Exit, with a public bath, rooms for families and groups and a Japanese breakfast buffet (¥1,430). Downside: 7 minutes from the Midosuji Line, so a little further for city evenings.
End the day in a big bath, not a tub →
Light bags, free breakfast
Toyoko Inn Shin-osaka-eki Higashi-guchi
Free breakfast, short walk
About 8 minutes from the JR East Exit, with free breakfast from 6:30 to 9:00. Downside: the walk is long with heavy luggage, and breakfast starts too late for the very first trains.
Breakfast included, Shinkansen at 9 →
Staying three nights or more? Compare the Umeda side in Osaka Station vs Umeda and prices in Osaka hotels by budget.
Eat around Shin-Osaka: the famous bite and the local one
What most visitors go for: 551 Horai pork buns for the train. Note that Ekimarché, the shopping street inside the JR gates, is closing in stages for a full renovation in 2026, and its 551 Horai counter shut in August. The Arde Shin-Osaka building (2nd floor) has the station's sit-down 551 Horai restaurant, and the Osaka Norenmeguri shops inside the Shinkansen gates still sell bento and gifts.
Dig a little deeper: besides the station, consider the Higashi-Mikuni side, about 10 minutes' walk north. Jukusei Udon Nakaya, 2 minutes from Higashi-Mikuni subway Exit 5, is on Tabelog's Udon Hyakumeiten (top 100) list for 2024. Order the tori-chikuten bukkake (chicken tempura with a cold pour-over broth) or the duck noodles. It opens 11:00 to 14:30 and 17:30 to 22:30, closes on Sundays, and takes cash only; weekday lunch fills up after 12:00, and at dinner each person orders one dish and one drink.
Station food is for the train; for a sit-down bowl of udon, walk ten minutes north.
📅 Good to know before you book
Big suitcase on the Shinkansen? Bags over 160 cm (length + width + height) and up to 250 cm need a "seat with oversized baggage area", free to reserve when you book; without one, JR charges ¥1,000 on board. Over 250 cm is not allowed.
One night or three? For one night before an early train, the gate hotels save the most. For longer stays, Umeda gives you the same Kyoto fare and more evening choices.
Free cancellation: many listings around Shin-Osaka offer it on Booking.com (check each one), so you can hold a room while you settle your train times.
See what's free around Shin-Osaka on your dates →
Nearby, if you have more time
Umeda, one stop south: department-store food halls, the Sky Building and the old food alleys under the tracks. See Osaka Station vs Umeda.
Namba, 16 minutes on the Midosuji Line: which of its four stations you need is in Namba Station: which Namba.
Tenma: Osaka's long covered shopping street and standing bars; see Tenma: where Osaka locals eat.
Osaka Station in Umeda, one JR stop from Shin-Osaka: the place for evenings out.
One more thing: send the suitcase ahead and arrive empty-handed
Arriving by Shinkansen in the morning, long before check-in? At Crosta Shin-Osaka in the station you can hand over your bags and have them delivered to your Osaka hotel the same day for ¥2,000 a bag (or stored for ¥1,000). It runs from 9:00 to 20:00 and needs a reservation. You ride into the city with nothing but a day bag and find the suitcase waiting in the lobby.
Source: Hands-free travel, Sightseeing from Shin-Osaka Station, osaka-info.jp (Osaka Convention and Tourism Bureau). Checked 25 November 2026.

## Where to Stay in Osaka by Budget: 8 Easy Hotels With Real Perks
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-hotels-by-budget
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

For about ¥12,000 a night for two, you can sleep in Osaka with a free hot-spring bath and a free bowl of ramen at 9:30 pm, or a free breakfast every morning, or a lounge that pours free drinks until 9 pm. Spend about ¥18,000 and you get a rooftop bath or a hotel three minutes from JR Osaka Station. Below are the eight we'd book, what makes each one different, and what we saw them cost on a real night.

Same city, very different nights: the bracket decides the view and the extras.
Around ¥12,000 a night: the three that give you the most
≈ ¥10,000–15,000 a night for two
At this price most Osaka hotels give you a clean, small room and nothing else. These three throw in something you'd otherwise pay for every day.
1 · Free lounge≈ ¥9,600
Hotel Elcient Osaka Umeda
Umeda · 5 min to JR Kitashinchi, 7 min to Higashi-Umeda (Tanimachi Line), 12 min to JR Osaka
☕ Free lounge 11:00–21:00
🍸 Free drinks from 17:30
♨️ Public bath + sauna
🧴 Lobby amenity buffet
This is the one that feels like more than you paid for. The guest lounge is free and runs most of the day: coffee, tea and soft drinks from 11:00, sweets with afternoon tea from 15:00, then snacks and alcoholic drinks from 17:30 to 21:00. Come back from Osaka Castle, have a drink on the house, then soak in the second-floor bath (open 16:00 to 1:00 and again 6:00 to 9:00) before dinner in Kitashinchi.
Cleanser, face wash and toner sit in a lobby amenity buffet, so you can pack lighter.
Good to know: breakfast is extra (listed at ¥1,980 per person). JR Osaka is 12 minutes on foot, so with big suitcases use JR Kitashinchi (5 minutes) or a short taxi.

2 · Free breakfastfrom ≈ ¥10,400
Comfort Hotel Osaka Shinsaibashi
Shinsaibashi · 5 min from Shinsaibashi Station exits 5 and 6 (Midosuji Line), 5 min to Dotonbori
🍳 Free breakfast 6:30–9:30
☕ Free coffee & lemon water
🚭 Fully non-smoking
🧺 Laundry + ice machine
Breakfast is included in the room price, every morning: fresh bread and Japanese rice balls (onigiri) from 6:30 to 9:30. Hot coffee and lemon water are free in the Library Café, and guests say the coffee and tea flow all day. You're five minutes from Dotonbori, so you can eat your way through Osaka at night and still have breakfast sorted.

Dormy Inn's famous habit: every night from about 21:30 to 23:00, a free bowl of yonaki soba, a light soy-sauce ramen, in the restaurant. Before it, the natural hot-spring bath and sauna; after it, guests mention free ice pops and cold drinks like Yakult. It's the closest thing to a ryokan evening you'll get three minutes from Dotonbori.

Bath in the sky≈ ¥18,300*
Candeo Hotels Osaka The Tower

Its Sky Spa is on the 31st floor, 135 m above the street, and holds the Guinness World Record as the highest open-air infinity-edge public bath. Every guest room is between the 18th and 31st floors, so there's no such thing as a bad view here. Go at dusk, when the city lights come on below you.

You can't sleep closer to Dotonbori: the Glico Running Man is a minute's walk, and you can book a Dotonbori View room and watch the canal light up from bed. Guests mention a lounge with snacks and an all-you-can-drink hour in the afternoon, and reviewers keep saying the staff speak English well.

Wake up above the canal →
For one special night, the view is part of what you pay for.
How we picked
Every hotel here is within a short walk of a station, works without Japanese at check-in (you show your passport, which Japanese law requires of foreign visitors), and has one thing that makes the stay easier or more fun: free food or drinks, a big bath, or a station at the door. We don't take payment from hotels. Facts come from the hotels' own pages and the big booking sites; where something comes from guest reviews, we say so.
Twin or double? Japanese "double" beds are often 140 cm wide. Two adults with suitcases usually sleep better in a twin.
Not sure whether you want Namba or Umeda? Namba is for food and nights out; Umeda is for trains and day trips. Our Osaka area guide goes through both with walking times.
One more thing: if you have a tattoo, pick the bath before the hotel
Many Japanese public baths still turn away tattoos, and hotel baths follow their own rules. Candeo states that tattooed guests are welcome at the Namba SkySpa, and The Tower's Sky Spa doesn't restrict entry for tattoos. Dormy Inn explains its rules at check-in. If the bath is the reason you're booking, check the policy before you pay, not at the bath door.

## New Chitose Airport to Sapporo: Train, Bus or Car?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/new-chitose-airport-to-sapporo
City: Hokkaido · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Take the JR Rapid Airport train: it's 33 to 43 minutes to Sapporo Station for ¥1,230, runs six times an hour in the daytime, and you just tap Suica at the gate. The airport bus (¥1,500) is the better pick when it stops outside your hotel in Odori or Susukino and you'd rather not drag a suitcase through a station. A car or taxi only makes sense if Sapporo isn't your final stop, or on a snow day when trains stop.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who the train suits, and who it doesn't
Train is right for
Hotels near Sapporo Station, Shin-Sapporo or along the subway
Anyone with Suica or another IC card: no ticket queue
Travellers heading on to Otaru: some trains run straight through
Think about the bus or a car if
Your hotel is a named bus stop in Odori or Susukino
You have more than two big bags each (the train limit)
You're driving on to Niseko, Furano or the countryside anyway
Three ways into the city
A · JR Rapid Airport
33 min · ¥1,230
Fastest, and no booking needed
From 9:00 to 16:00 there's one Special Rapid (33 min), three Rapids (37 min) and two Semi-Rapids (43 min) an hour. Cars 1–3 and 5–6 are unreserved; car 4 is the reserved u-seat car, ¥1,000 extra (¥800 as a ticketless booking), worth it at busy times when you want a guaranteed seat and space for a big case. The station is directly under the Domestic Terminal.
B · Airport bus
¥1,500 · 65 min+
Door to your hotel
Hokuto Kotsu's buses stop at Sapporo Station (about 65 minutes on direct runs), Susukino and hotels including Keio Plaza Hotel Sapporo, Grand Mercure Sapporo Odori Koen, Sapporo Prince Hotel and ANA Crowne Plaza. No reservation; pay as you get off by cash, contactless card or PayPay. Suica doesn't work, and it's one suitcase per person in the hold.
C · Car or taxi
60 min · ¥17,000+
Only for onward trips
JR Hokkaido puts a taxi at about 60 minutes and from about ¥17,000 per vehicle. A rental car is for travellers continuing into the countryside, not for Sapporo itself, where trains and the subway do the job. Groups with lots of luggage may prefer a pre-booked transfer.
Pre-book a driver for a door-to-door winter arrival →
Our verdict: take the train unless your hotel is on the bus route. The answer changes in two cases: more luggage than two pieces each, or a winter storm warning on your arrival day, when it's worth checking JR Hokkaido's service status before you leave baggage claim.
New Chitose Airport in winter, where most Hokkaido trips begin.
How the train works on arrival
Follow signs down to the JR station under the Domestic Terminal. With Suica, ICOCA, PASMO or Kitaca, tap through and take any non-reserved car. Without one, buy a ticket at the machines, which take cash only; the orange reserved-seat machines and the JR counter take cards. Luggage is limited to two items each, up to 250 cm in total size and 30 kg. The Special Rapid stops at Minami-Chitose, Shin-Sapporo and Sapporo, then continues to Teine, Minami-Otaru and Otaru. Heading for Otaru? Check the destination: trains marked Teine or Hoshimi end before Otaru.
Sapporo trains run in deep snow most days, but big storms can stop them.
Eat before you leave the airport
The third floor of the Domestic Terminal is lined with ramen counters from all over Hokkaido, a good first meal if you land hungry.
Baikoken: Asahikawa soy-sauce ramen from a shop founded in 1969. 9:30 to 21:00, last order 20:00.
Ajisai: Hakodate salt ramen with clear soup, from a shop with an 80-year history. 9:00 to 21:00, last order 20:00.
Ebisoba Ichigen: ramen made with sweet-shrimp heads, served in its red bowls. 9:00 to 21:00, last order 20:00.
Eat first, then head down to the trains: the station is right under the terminal.
Winter: when the plan changes
Heavy snow is the one thing that beats the train. On 25 and 26 January 2026, JR Hokkaido cancelled 1,145 trains and about 7,000 people were stranded at New Chitose; for two days afterwards, the last Rapid Airport from Sapporo left at 20:04 instead of late evening. On a disrupted day, JR Hokkaido points travellers to the airport bus (about 70 to 90 minutes) or a taxi (about 60 minutes), and warns that both get very crowded and slower on bad roads.
Unused paper tickets are refunded in full if you cancel the trip, and a reserved u-seat bought online and not yet collected is cancelled automatically if its train is cancelled.
Heavy snow days are when the train plan changes.
Where to stay: three good bases
For train arrivals
Sapporo Station
Off the train, into bed
The airport train arrives here, and early departures are a short walk away. Downside: further from Susukino's dinners.
Roll your case straight from the platform to your room →
For bus arrivals
Odori
Hotels that are bus stops
Several big Odori hotels are stops on the airport bus, so you can skip the station entirely. Downside: the bus is slower than the train, and Suica won't work.
Let the airport bus drop you at your door →
For a quieter base
Shin-Sapporo
The first city stop
Every Rapid Airport train, Special Rapid included, stops here before Sapporo. Downside: it's away from the centre, so dinner in Susukino means a ride back in.
Get off one stop early and sleep somewhere calmer →
Still choosing an area? Our first-trip Sapporo guide compares Sapporo Station, Odori and Susukino.
📅 Good to know before you book
Arriving December to February? Pick a hotel close to the train or a bus stop, so a snow day doesn't leave you dragging a case across ice.
u-seats can be booked ahead online with JR-EAST Train Reservation (¥800 ticketless). Use an IC card or paper ticket for the gate; the e-ticket alone won't open it.
Peak times: the airport bus doesn't take reservations, so when it's full you wait for the next one.
Most hotels on booking sites show a free-cancellation date, handy when winter flights move.
Line up a snowy Sapporo stay with room to change plans →
Nearby, if you have more time
Otaru: some Rapid Airport trains run straight through from the airport, 73 minutes at the fastest.
Noboribetsu or Hakodate: change at Minami-Chitose for limited expresses, where all seats are reserved.
Odori Park and the TV Tower: the centre of the city you're heading for.
One more thing: a Hakodate seafood bowl without going to Hakodate
Kikuyo Shokudo started in 1956 at Hakodate's morning market and is known there for its seafood rice bowls, especially the build-your-own "Okonomi-Don". Its New Chitose branch is on the third floor of the Domestic Terminal, open 11:00 to 20:00, so it works as a first lunch on arrival or a last one before your flight home.
Source: New Chitose Airport official shop page, checked 24 November 2026.

## First Trip to Fukuoka: Hakata, Tenjin or Nakasu?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-where-to-stay-first-trip
City: Fukuoka · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

For most first trips we'd stay in Hakata: the airport is 5 minutes away by subway and Kyushu's biggest station is downstairs for day trips. Pick Tenjin if shopping and Dazaifu are the plan, and Nakasu-Kawabata, between the two, if your evenings will be spent at the yatai food stalls by the river. All three sit on one subway line, so the choice is about your mornings and nights, not about being stuck.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who Fukuoka suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Short trips: almost no time lost between plane and hotel
Food-first travellers: ramen, markets and about 100 yatai stalls
Kyushu explorers using Hakata as a hub for day trips
Travellers flying in from Seoul, Busan, Taipei or Shanghai on short direct flights
Think twice
Travellers after big temple sights: those are a train ride away, in Dazaifu
Big groups at the yatai: most stalls seat no more than about 10
Light sleepers right in Nakasu's bar streets, which stay busy late
Getting there from the airport
The subway station is inside the Domestic Terminal. Kuko Line trains reach Hakata in 5 minutes and Tenjin in 11, every 3 to 6 minutes at rush hour and every 6 to 8 minutes during the day, with Nakasu-Kawabata in between. Landing at the International Terminal? Take the free shuttle bus to the Domestic Terminal first, about 10 minutes. Once in town, Hakata to Tenjin is 6 minutes and ¥210.
Hakata Station: Kyushu's largest station, five minutes from the runway.
Where to stay: three good bases
For trains and day trips
Hakata
Shinkansen downstairs
JR Hakata City is one of Japan's biggest station buildings, with limited expresses and shinkansen across Kyushu. Behind the offices are quiet temple streets and Sumiyoshi Shrine, about 10 minutes' walk. Downside: the station side feels like a business district at night.
Step off the plane and into bed in Hakata →
For shopping and Dazaifu
Tenjin
Downtown Kyushu
Department stores, the underground Tenjin Chikagai mall, and Nishitetsu trains straight to Dazaifu. Downside: 11 minutes from the airport instead of 5, and no shinkansen.
Base yourself where Fukuoka shops and strolls →
For yatai nights
Nakasu -Kawabata
Walk home from the stalls
The river yatai, Kushida Shrine and Kawabata, Hakata's oldest shopping arcade, are on your doorstep, one stop from both Hakata and Tenjin. Downside: the bar streets nearest the river are loud late, so pick a hotel on the Kawabata side.
Fall asleep a short stroll from the river stalls →
Eat like a local
A yatai seats about ten. You'll be sharing elbows, and that's the point.
Yatai (from about 6 pm): Fukuoka has about 100 street stalls, mainly in Nakasu and Tenjin. Tonkotsu ramen, yakitori and oden are on almost every menu, and yaki-ramen (stir-fried ramen) is the newer favourite. The house rules are simple: order at least one thing each, leave room for the next person, and drop your luggage at the hotel first because there's nowhere to put it.
Nagahama yatai: the stalls by the fish market came back in 2023. Nagahama no Hiroshi starts many evenings there with a pork-wrapped lettuce roll at ¥900.
Hakata Ramen Shin-Shin, Tenjin main shop: open since October 2003, 30 seats, about 5 minutes on foot from Tenjin Station. Its hours and closed days are on the shop's own calendar, so check before you go. There's also a branch at Fukuoka Airport for a last bowl before you fly.
Rain or wind? A yatai may simply not open in stormy weather. Keep a ramen shop like Shin-Shin as your plan B for that evening.
🏮 Nervous about your first yatai? Small-group and private food walks around the Nakasu stalls take about two hours, and some add a night cruise on the Naka River, so someone shows you how ordering and sharing a counter works.Let a local seat you at the river stalls →
A simple first afternoon and evening
14:00 Land, ride the subway 5 minutes to Hakata, drop your bags.
15:00 Walk to Sumiyoshi Shrine, the oldest of Japan's Sumiyoshi shrines, and the Rakusui-en garden next to it.
16:30 Over to Kushida Shrine and the Kawabata arcade in Nakasu-Kawabata.
18:00 The yatai open. Start by the river in Nakasu, then try a second stall rather than staying at one.
21:00 Still hungry? Hop to Tenjin's stalls, one subway stop away.
📅 Good to know before you book
Yatai are weather-dependent: on a stormy night, stalls may stay shut. If yatai are the reason for your trip, give yourself two evenings.
Markets close on Sundays: Yanagibashi Rengo Market, "Hakata's kitchen", is closed on Sundays and public holidays. Plan a weekday or Saturday morning for it.
Flying in from abroad: the International Terminal has no subway, so allow about 10 minutes for the free shuttle before your 5-minute train.
Most hotels on booking sites show a free-cancellation date, so booking early costs nothing if your dates move.
Hold a Fukuoka room while your flights settle →
Fukuoka after dark: compact, lit up and easy to walk.
Nearby, if you have more time
Dazaifu: Nishitetsu trains run straight from Tenjin; fares start at ¥170 for short hops.
Uminonakamichi and Shikanoshima: reachable by road, but the 15-minute ferry from Bayside Place Hakata or Marizon is the nicer way.
One more thing: breakfast in Hakata's kitchen
Yanagibashi Rengo Market is where Fukuoka's chefs and home cooks shop: fishmongers packed along lanes about a metre wide, plus mentaiko, pickles and sweets, and a few shops with eat-in counters. It opens at 8:00 (shop hours vary) and is about 3 minutes from Watanabe-dori Station on the Nanakuma Line, or about 5 minutes by car from Hakata. Go early on a weekday or Saturday; it's closed on Sundays and holidays.
Source: Crossroad Fukuoka (Fukuoka Prefecture official tourism site), checked 24 November 2026.

## Hakone 'Private Onsen': Which Booking Actually Gets You One?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/hakone-private-onsen-which-booking
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

If what you want is hot-spring water with nobody else in it, don't assume the "room with open-air bath" is the answer. At one Gora ryokan we checked, that room costs ¥12,600 more for two and its bath is heated tap water, while the inn's real onsen private bath is ¥3,600 for 50 minutes. Our pick for most couples: a standard ryokan room plus a booked private bath, or a two-hour private bath room in Yumoto if the bath matters more than the room.
About a 5-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026 · sample prices for Wednesday 16 December 2026, 2 adults
Who this suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Couples or families who want to bathe together (shared baths are split by gender)
Anyone with tattoos who wants a bath without asking permission
First-timers nervous about bathing with strangers
Travellers who care whether the water is really from a hot spring
Think twice
Solo travellers happy in a shared bath: you'd pay for privacy you don't need
Late arrivals: private-bath slots at small inns go to whoever checks in first
Anyone who needs to pay by card at the inn: some ryokan take cash only on site
The three ways to get a private bath
A · In-room bath
+¥12,600 for two
Read the room description, not the photo
On 16 December 2026, Kiritani Hakoneso in Gora sold its standard two-meal plan at ¥27,000 for two on Ikyu and its Annex room with open-air bath at ¥39,600. The plan page says plainly that the in-room baths "are not onsen water", with a reheating function instead. Pay for this when you want a bath any time of night, not when you want the hot spring.
B · Reservable private bath
¥3,600 / 50 min
The real onsen, by the slot
Kiritani's private open-air bath uses the inn's milky sulphur water from Owakudani. It's ¥3,600 for two for 50 minutes, limited to five groups a day. You request it when you book, and time slots are given out in check-in order, so it is not guaranteed. The inn also lists free family baths.
C · Day-use private bath
¥10,400 / 120 min
A guaranteed booking, any hotel
Hakone Yuryo, a 3-minute free shuttle from Hakone-Yumoto Station, has 19 private open-air bath rooms. The smallest (18 m², up to two people) cost ¥10,400 for 120 minutes on weekdays, booked online with a card. Pair it with a simple room-only stay and the bath is the highlight, booked to the minute.
Our verdict: for a couple staying one night, book a standard ryokan room and add its private bath (B), and check in early. Choose C if your hotel has no private onsen or you arrive after 17:00 and don't want to gamble on a slot. Choose A only when the room page itself says hot spring, onsen or gensen, or when an in-room tub at midnight is the whole point.
Getting there
Odakyu trains run from Shinjuku to Hakone-Yumoto; for Gora, change to the Hakone Tozan Railway. Hakone Yuryo's free shuttle bus leaves from near Hakone-Yumoto Station and takes about 3 minutes. Kiritani Hakoneso is on the hill in Gora and offers a free pick-up; ask when you book, especially if you have big bags or it's raining. Our Freepass guide works out whether the pass pays off for a one-night stay.
Hakone's onsen towns are small: most evenings revolve around the bath and dinner.
Timing that makes the difference
Booking Add the private-bath request in the notes when you reserve (option B). For Yuryo (option C), booking opens one month before your date and closes at 15:00 the day before.
15:30 Kiritani's check-in opens. The earlier you check in, the better your choice of private-bath slots.
18:00 Last check-in at Kiritani, and last entry to Yuryo's private baths on weekdays (19:00 at weekends and on holidays).
After dinner Kiritani's baths run until 09:30, so a late soak or an early-morning one both work.
Eat around your bath
Private baths in Hakone are booked by the slot, so plan dinner around yours.
Irori Saryo Hachiri (inside Hakone Yuryo): fish and irori-hearth dishes after your bath, weekdays 11:30 to 20:00 (last order 19:00), weekends and holidays to 21:00 (last order 20:00). It saves a second trip when you've booked a late private room.
Ryokan dinner: Kiritani serves dinner and breakfast in private dining rooms in its main building, about a 2-minute walk outdoors with stairs and slopes from the Annex. Worth knowing if anyone in your group has trouble with steps.
Where to stay: three good bases

Ryokan with their own springs
Milky water and private baths on site, and the Tozan Railway at the door. Downside: the best slots go to early arrivals.

The first stop from Odawara and a short shuttle to Yuryo. Downside: room-only hotels here rarely have their own private onsen.

Lake Ashi
Quiet nights by the water
Lakeside hotels for the morning boat and Hakone Shrine. Downside: further from Yumoto's day onsen, with fewer late buses.

Not sure which part of Hakone suits you? Our Yumoto, Gora or Lake Ashi guide compares the three with prices and last buses.
📅 Good to know before you book
Cancellation: Kiritani's Ikyu plan for 16 December was free to cancel until 9 December; after that 30% from six days before, 50% the day before and 100% on the day. Payment at the inn is cash only.
Yuryo closes for maintenance 1 to 3 December 2026, and charges holiday rates from 26 December 2026 to 3 January 2027.
Want the big baths too? Yuryo's public baths cost extra on top of a private room: ¥1,000 on weekdays, ¥1,300 at weekends.
Running late? Yuryo cannot move your slot if you arrive late. Extensions are ¥2,600 per 30 minutes, if the room is free.
Line up a Hakone night with a free-cancellation window →
Nearby, if you have more time
Leaving Tokyo after lunch? Make a ryokan dinner from Tokyo works out the latest train that still gets you to the table.
Big suitcase? Forward it, carry it or store it before you head up the mountain.
One more thing: the private bath is a race to check-in
At small ryokan with one private bath, slots are often handed out at the front desk. Kiritani says so plainly: five groups a day, allocated in check-in order. Arrive at 15:30, the moment check-in opens, and you choose your time; arrive at 17:45 and you take what's left. If an early check-in isn't possible, book Yuryo's private room for the afternoon instead and treat the inn's bath as a bonus.

## Enoshima Without the Stairs: Escalator, Boat or Stay on the Shore?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/enoshima-without-the-stairs
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Key facts:
- Escar: three escalator sections to the Samuel Cocking Garden, ¥500 adult, 8:50–19:05, up only; the way down is stairs (checked 24 Nov 2026).
- Benten-maru boat: about 10 minutes between Chigogafuchi and the foot of Benten Bridge, about ¥400, weather-dependent; phone 0466-22-4141 before 10:00.
- From Shinjuku: Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass ¥1,640; Romancecar to Katase-Enoshima about 61–69 minutes plus a ¥750 seat charge.
- Benten Bridge: a flat 389 m walk from the shore to the island.

Yes, Enoshima works for someone who walks happily but hates long stair climbs, as long as you plan it in one direction. Our pick: ride the Escar escalators up (¥500), walk on across the top and down to the rocks at Chigogafuchi, then take the little Benten-maru boat back to the bridge, so you never climb back over the island. If the sea is rough and the boat isn't running, keep it to the lower island and the shore instead.
About a 6-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who this plan suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Parents or partners who can walk an hour on the flat but tire on long stairways
A half day from Tokyo with sea views and a seafood lunch
Clear winter days, when Mount Fuji shows best from the coast
Think twice
Wheelchairs and strollers on the island itself: the Escar asks you to fold strollers, and the way down is stairs
Anyone who can't manage stairs going down either: stick to the shore plan
Stormy days: the boat stops and the island's back side is all on foot
Getting there from Tokyo
Take Odakyu from Shinjuku to Katase-Enoshima. The Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass (¥1,640 for adults from Shinjuku) covers the round trip plus a day of Odakyu local-area and Enoden rides. Add the Romancecar for a reserved seat (¥750 each way; sample trains take about 61–69 minutes). From Katase-Enoshima it is about a 5-minute walk to the start of Benten Bridge, a flat 389 m walkway to the island. Katase-Enoshima Station is all on one level, which helps. The Enoden's Enoshima Station and the Shonan Monorail are each about 10 minutes further away.
The Enoden is covered by the Freepass, so you can head on to Kamakura afterwards.
Three ways to do Enoshima with fewer stairs
A. Lower island only: the bridge, the shops, a long lunch
Walk the bridge and stroll the shop street at the bottom of the island. This is where most of the seafood restaurants are. Make lunch the goal, then turn back at the foot of the shrine steps. You get the sea on both sides, Fuji on clear days from the bridge, and no climbing at all. The downside: you miss the views from the top and the caves on the far side.
B. Upper island with the Escar (and the boat back)
The Escar is a set of three paid escalators: the first stops near Hetsunomiya shrine, the second near Nakatsunomiya, the third at the Samuel Cocking Garden and the Sea Candle lookout tower. All three cost ¥500 for adults (¥250 children), 8:50 to 19:05, and replace stone steps that take about 20 minutes to climb. The catch the signs don't shout about: the Escar only goes up. Coming down is by stairs.
The shrine gate where the steps begin.
So plan it one way. From the garden, the path on to Okutsunomiya and down to the rocks at Chigogafuchi is on foot, with stone steps and no escalator; the Iwaya Caves (¥500) are close by. From Chigogafuchi the Benten-maru boat runs back to the foot of Benten Bridge in about 10 minutes, about ¥400 for adults, cash. Kanagawa Prefecture's own tourism page suggests it for the way back to save energy. It has no timetable and stops in rough seas, so phone 0466-22-4141 before 10:00 on the day.
C. Stay on the shore: flat, with the island in view
Kanagawa's tourism board checked the route from Katase-Enoshima Station to Enoshima Aquarium and found it usable by powered wheelchair, with only slight curbs and slopes. Pair the aquarium (¥2,800 adults, 9:00 or 10:00 to 17:00 depending on the season, ¥200 off with your rail ticket) with a walk along Katase West Beach, one of the official Fuji viewpoints.
Our verdict: plan B with the boat, on a calm day, for most people who simply dislike climbing. Choose A if going down long stairways is also hard on the knees. Choose C for wheelchairs, strollers, or a rough-sea day.
Eat like a local: shirasu, near the bridge
Shirasu, tiny whitebait, is the local catch here, served on rice raw or boiled.
Tobicchi Honten (lower island, right after the bridge): 11:00–21:00 (last order 20:00), no fixed closing day, about ¥1,000–3,000 a head. Tabelog reviewers order the shirasu-don set (about ¥1,490). On weekends and holidays it hands out numbered tickets before opening. No credit cards. Reviewers note raw shirasu is off the menu from about January to mid-March.
Enoshima-tei (upper island): sea-view tables, cards accepted, no reservations, open to 17:30 on weekdays and 19:00 at weekends. A good reason to sit down after the Escar.
Enoshima Koya (mainland, 3 minutes from Katase-Enoshima): 8:00–20:00 (last order 19:00), cards accepted. Listings name the makanai-don, fish namero with sesame sauce, as the dish to order. Handy for plan C, and for an early lunch.
The Sea Candle: the Escar's last section drops you at its garden.
A stair-light half day (plan B)
9:30 Phone the Benten-maru (0466-22-4141) to check it is running today. If not, switch to plan A or C.
10:30 Arrive at Katase-Enoshima, walk the 389 m bridge, browse the shop street.
11:15 Escar up all three sections (¥500). The garden is free until 17:00; the Sea Candle is ¥800.
12:30 Lunch with a view at the top.
13:30 On foot to Okutsunomiya and down to Chigogafuchi; the Iwaya Caves if you have the energy.
14:30 Benten-maru back to the bridge, then the train home, or the Enoden to Kamakura.
Morning: the flat walk over
Midday: the top, by escalator
Afternoon: Fuji from the water on a clear day
Where to stay if you make it two days
For sunsets and an early start
Katase-Enoshima
The bridge at your door
Walk to the island first thing in the morning. Fewer, smaller hotels, so choice is limited.
Watch the island go gold from your own doorstep →
For temples too
Kamakura
Enoshima one day, Kamakura the next
The Enoden links the two. Kamakura is busier and pricier at weekends.
Fall asleep a short ride from the Great Buddha →
For value and trains
Fujisawa
The junction town
Odakyu, JR and the Enoden meet here, so you're in reach of both Tokyo and the coast. Less scenery around the hotel.
Base yourself where three railways meet →
🎟️ Skip the ticket machines: the Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass and an Enoshima Sky View Ticket (Escar, garden and Sea Candle together) are both sold online as phone tickets.Have your island tickets ready on your phone →
📅 Good to know before you book
Winter is Fuji season: Fujisawa's tourism site calls winter the clearest time for Fuji from Enoshima, and lists "Diamond Fuji" sunsets around early April and early September.
Winter illumination: the Sea Candle garden's "Shonan no Hoseki" lights ran 22 November 2025 to 28 February 2026; the garden charges ¥500 after 17:00. Check this season's dates.
Romancecar front seats: the panoramic seats on GSE trains sell out first. Most hotels offer free cancellation if you want to lock in a weekend.
Nearby, if you have more time
Kamakura: the Enoden runs on to the Great Buddha and Hasedera. Our Kamakura from noon guide times it.
Hakone: the other classic Odakyu trip. See Gora to Lake Ashi: bus or ropeway?
One more thing: the flat Fuji view most people walk past
Fujisawa's tourism office lists the breakwater promenade at Katase Fishing Port, on the mainland just west of the bridge, as a Fuji viewpoint. It is flat and away from the island crowds, and it looks across the water toward the mountain on clear winter afternoons. It's a good last stop for anyone whose legs are done for the day.
Source: Discover Fujisawa, Mount Fuji viewpoints page, checked 24 November 2026.

## Fushimi Inari: Dawn, Afternoon or After Dark? How Far Up Is Worth It
URL: https://japanbystation.com/fushimi-inari-dawn-day-or-after-dark
City: Kyoto · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Key facts:
- Hours: the grounds are open around the clock and free; the amulet office keeps roughly 8:30–16:30 hours (checked 24 Nov 2026).
- Mountain: Inariyama is 233 m; Yotsutsuji, the viewpoint junction, is about 30–45 minutes up; the full summit loop takes about 2–3 hours.
- First train: JR Nara Line locals leave Kyoto Station from 5:33 on weekdays; Inari Station is right in front of the shrine.
- Light: sunrise in Kyoto is about 6:40 in late November and about 7:05 at the end of December; sunset about 16:45–16:55.

Go at dawn. The grounds never close and entry is free, the first JR local leaves Kyoto Station at 5:33 on weekdays, and the gates are far quieter before the day crowds build from around nine. Climb to Yotsutsuji, about 30–45 minutes up, for the view over southern Kyoto, then come down for breakfast at the gate. The afternoon works only if you're willing to climb past the crowds, and after dark is for the lit lower torii, not the mountain.
About a 6-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who a dawn visit suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Photographers who want torii without people in them
Anyone staying near Kyoto Station or on the Keihan line
Walkers happy with steady stone steps for 30–45 minutes
Think twice
Late risers staying in the north or west of Kyoto: the first trains won't help you
Young kids at night: the upper path is dark and wooded
New Year week: one of Japan's busiest shrines, around 2.5 million visitors in a typical year
Getting there
JR Nara Line local trains run from Kyoto Station to Inari Station in a few minutes, and the shrine's big torii stands right outside the station. On weekdays the first locals leave Kyoto at 5:33 and 5:51; the last train back from Inari to Kyoto is at 0:04. From Gion or Sanjo, take the Keihan Line to Fushimi-Inari and walk about 5 minutes east (limited expresses don't stop there). Kyoto City Tourism advises skipping the bus: journey times swing by more than 20 minutes.
The main gate, a few steps from JR Inari Station. By mid-morning this square is full.
Dawn, afternoon or after dark: the three answers
A. Dawn: our pick
Sunrise in Kyoto is about 6:40 in late November and about 7:05 at the end of December. Be at the gate as it gets light and the famous Senbon Torii, the double row of gates built up by donations since the Edo period, is yours. Behind the Okusha worship hall, try the omokaru stones: make a wish and lift; if the stone feels lighter than you expected, the shrine says your wish is likely to come true.
B. Afternoon: only if you climb
Travel guides put the busy stretch at roughly 9:00 to 18:00, and the jam is at the bottom: many visitors see the main hall and the first gates, then leave. The crowd thins the higher you go. So the afternoon works if you walk on to Yotsutsuji, the junction about halfway up with teahouses and a view over southern Kyoto. The full loop over the 233 m summit, Ichinomine, takes about 2–3 hours in total. Kyoto City Tourism also publishes a crowd forecast for the area by time slot, worth a look on the day.
After dark the lower gates glow. The mountain above them doesn't.
C. After dark: the lower torii only
Lights cover the busier lower areas, and the mood is very different from the daytime rush. But most of the loop beyond them has no lights, and guides mention monkeys and wild boar in the woods. At night, stay on the lit lower section for 30–45 minutes and keep the climb for daylight. Last trains back to Kyoto run past midnight, so time isn't the problem; the dark path is.
Our verdict: dawn, up to Yotsutsuji and back, about two hours with photo stops. It changes if you can't get there early: then go mid-afternoon and climb past the bottom section. If it's your only free evening, a night walk on the lower torii is worth it, the summit isn't.
Eat like a local: inari sushi at the gate
Inari sushi, rice packed in sweet fried tofu, is the classic snack of the shrine approach, and the old shops near the station still make it.
Inafuku (3 min from JR Inari): inari sushi with sesame and burdock, plus udon sets. 9:00–17:00 (last order 16:30), closed Tuesdays, cash or PayPay only. The earliest sit-down option after a dawn climb.
Nezameya (2 min from JR Inari): grilled quail skewers (¥900) and inari sushi, 10:00–16:00 or until sold out; irregular closing days.
Kendonya: handmade kitsune udon, about ¥900 on average. 11:00–20:30 with a 14:30–17:00 break, closed Wednesdays: the one to remember for an evening visit.
Nishimura-tei, at Yotsutsuji: a teahouse on the mountain with udon and sweets, from 10:00 on weekdays (9:00 weekends and holidays), last orders around 14:00. Tabelog reviewers mention the view.
Inari sushi: the snack this shrine gave its name to.
A dawn route with times (late November)
5:51 JR local from Kyoto Station (or the 5:33 if you want to be first).
6:05 Through the main gate to the Senbon Torii while it's still blue light.
6:40 Around sunrise: Okusha hall and the omokaru stones, then keep climbing.
7:15 Yotsutsuji: the view over southern Kyoto. Turn back here, or carry on round the summit loop.
8:15 Back at the bottom, before the busy hours start.
9:00 Breakfast-lunch at Inafuku, then one stop to Tofuku-ji, which opens at 9:00.
Early: the gates to yourself
The fox messengers watch the path
After dark: the lit lower shrine
Where to stay for a dawn start
Easiest for first trains
Kyoto Station
South (Hachijo) side
JR Nara Line trains leave from here, and day trips to Nara and Osaka start here too. The area is busy and less atmospheric.
Be at the torii before the city wakes →
Closest to the shrine
Fushimi
Inari and the sake district
Walk to the gate in the dark, and the Fushimi sake breweries are a few stops south. Fewer restaurants open late.
Sleep where the fox shrines and sake breweries are →
For evenings out
Gion-Shijo
On the Keihan line
Keihan trains run straight to Fushimi-Inari, and Gion's old streets are outside the door. Prices run higher.
Lantern-lit evenings, one train from the torii →
Still choosing a base for the whole trip? See where to stay in Kyoto on a first trip.
🥾 Want the quiet back trails? Small-group hikes take a less-used route up the mountain in about three hours, starting near Tofuku-ji.Walk the side of Inari most visitors never find →
📅 Good to know before you book
New Year (1–3 January): about 2.5 million people come for the first shrine visit of the year. If your dates include it, go on another day.
Autumn leaves next door: Tofuku-ji, one stop away, holds an autumn special viewing (14 November to 6 December in 2026), when the Tsutenkyo bridge fee rises from ¥600 to ¥1,000 and gates open at 8:30.
Kyoto Station hotels fill early in autumn and spring; most offer free cancellation, so holding a room costs nothing.
Nearby, if you have more time
Tofuku-ji: one stop on either JR or Keihan; reception from 9:00, the gardens are ¥500.
Fushimi sake district: Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum, 9:30–16:30, about ¥600 with a tasting, about 5 minutes from Keihan Chushojima.
Nara: the JR Nara Line continues there. See Nara: day trip or one night?
One more thing: clap at the echo pond
Partway up, at Kumataka-sha, is Shin-ike, which the shrine calls the "echo pond". The old custom: if someone is missing, you clap your hands towards the pond, and the direction the echo comes back from shows where to look. On an empty dawn path you can actually hear it, which you can't at noon.
Source: Fushimi Inari Taisha official map page for Kumataka-sha / Shin-ike, checked 24 November 2026.

## Gora to Lake Ashi: Bus or Ropeway?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/gora-to-lake-ashi-bus-or-ropeway
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Ride the Hakone Ropeway once, for the views over Owakudani's steam vents, and use the bus for everything else. From Gora Station, two short Tozan bus rides reach Moto-Hakone on Lake Ashi in 20 to 30 minutes for ¥910, a short walk from Hakone Shrine's lakeside torii, and the Freepass covers them. Most visitors only know the cable car, ropeway and boat loop; knowing the bus lets you do the views one way and come back fast.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who the ropeway suits, and who should just take the bus
Ride the ropeway if
It's your first Hakone visit and you want Owakudani's steam and the high views
You have a Freepass: the ropeway and boat are already paid for
The day is clear and calm: the views are the whole point
Take the bus if
You mainly want the lake, Hakone Shrine and lunch by the water
Time is short: the bus goes straight to Moto-Hakone
It's windy or misty, or the ropeway is closed for maintenance
The Tozan buses: the quiet shortcut between Gora and the lake.
Three ways from Gora to Lake Ashi
A · The ropeway loop
Views · ¥2,000 ropeway
Cable car, ropeway, boat
Cable car up to Sounzan, then the ropeway over Owakudani to Togendai, about 30 minutes end to end with gondolas roughly every minute (¥2,000 one way, covered by the Freepass), then the sightseeing boat across the lake to Moto-Hakone. Allow most of a morning with stops. The ropeway runs until 16:45, or 16:15 in December and January.
B · The bus
20–30 min · ¥910
Gora to Moto-Hakone
The "S" sightseeing-facility bus from Gora to Kowakien (about 4 minutes, ¥250), then the H-line bus to Moto-Hakone-ko (about 14 minutes, ¥660). From Hakone-Yumoto the direct bus from stop 2 takes about 30 minutes for ¥1,210 and runs about every 15 minutes in the daytime. Heading for Togendai instead? Gora to Togendai by bus is about 55 minutes, ¥880.
C · Mix the two
Our pick
Views out, bus back
Ropeway and boat out in the morning, then the H-line bus from Moto-Hakone back down to Yumoto or up towards Gora. You get Owakudani and the lake without sitting through the slow loop twice.
Our verdict: on a first visit with a Freepass, do C: ropeway out, bus back. The answer changes on a windy or misty day, or when the ropeway is shut for maintenance: then take the bus both ways (B) and spend the saved time at the shrine or in an onsen. If you've ridden the ropeway before, the bus alone is the smarter way to the lake.
Moto-Hakone and the shrine torii: 20 to 30 minutes from Gora by bus.
Eat like a local: lunch at either end
Bakery & Table Hakone (Moto-Hakone): right by the Moto-Hakone-ko bus stop, open every day, with a bakery downstairs and a café with lake views upstairs (last café order 16:30). GOOD LUCK TRIP lists the rice-flour curry doughnut as the best-seller. Cards accepted.
Tamura Ginkatsutei (Gora): about 2 minutes from Gora Station, and where tofu katsuni, a tofu cutlet simmered with egg, originated. Lunch last order 14:30; closed Wednesdays and Tuesday evenings. Cards accepted.
Hakone Gyoza Center (Gora): small and popular for gyoza sets at lunch, last order 14:30. Closed Thursdays and Wednesday afternoons, cash only. A reviewer on its listing suggests writing your name in the notebook by the door.
Two stops below Gora: the stained-glass tower at the Open-Air Museum, open every day.
Our half-day route: views out, bus back
9:30 From Gora, cable car up to Sounzan and check Hakone Navi's live status once more.
10:00 Ropeway over Owakudani to Togendai (about 30 minutes), with a stop for the steam vents.
11:00 Boat across Lake Ashi to Moto-Hakone.
11:45 Walk about 10 minutes to Hakone Shrine (free) and its lakeside torii.
12:45 Lunch and a lake view at Bakery & Table, by the bus stop.
14:00 H-line bus down to Hakone-Yumoto (about 30 minutes) for a bath before the train home.
Late morning: off the boat at Moto-Hakone
Midday: shrine, lake, lunch
Afternoon: back down to Yumoto for a bath
Making it a night: three bases
For flexibility
Hakone-Yumoto
Every bus starts here
Direct buses to Moto-Hakone and Togendai, and the Romancecar home. Downside: you're at the bottom of the mountain, so mornings at the lake mean a 30-minute ride.
Keep every road out of Hakone at your door →
For a second try at the ropeway
Gora
First in line at Sounzan
Stay up here and you can be on the first gondolas of the morning, before the day-trippers arrive. Downside: quieter evenings and fewer dinner choices.
Sleep one cable car away from Owakudani →
For the lake at its calmest
Moto-Hakone
The lake before the crowds
Wake up by the water and catch the first boat when the wind drops. Downside: the furthest base from the train.
Wake to Lake Ashi and take the first boat out →
Comparing bases in more detail? See our Yumoto vs Gora vs Lake Ashi guide.
📅 Good to know before you book
Planned ropeway maintenance: Owakudani–Sounzan is shut 7–24 December 2026 and Togendai–Owakudani 12 January–26 February 2027 (replacement buses for ticket holders). If the gondola matters, book outside those dates.
Wind can stop the ropeway and boats on any day of the year: check Hakone Navi's Transportation Info page before you leave Tokyo, and switch to the bus if they're down.
Most Hakone hotels on booking sites show a free-cancellation date: useful when the forecast turns.
Hold a Hakone room you can still cancel if plans change →
Nearby, if you have more time
Owakudani: the ropeway stop with the steam vents and a new observation area; worth getting off on the way across. Our Freepass guide shows when the pass pays off.
A private onsen: rain is the best excuse. See how to book one that's really onsen water.
Arriving with a big case? Send it ahead or store it so the bus rides are easy.
One more thing: a ropeway you couldn't ride is money back
Wind stops the ropeway and the lake boats more often than most visitors expect. If that happens on your Freepass days and you never rode it, the unused part is refunded at the station where you finish: on the digital Freepass that's ¥1,640 for an adult 2-day pass, ¥820 if only one section was down, and ¥1,180 more if the boat didn't run either. Ask before you go through the gate home.
Source: Hakone Navi Freepass page and EMot Digital Hakone Freepass terms, checked 24 November 2026.
