## Hiroshima and Miyajima in One Day: Where to Base, Tram or Train, and the Tides
URL: https://japanbystation.com/hiroshima-miyajima-one-day
City: Hiroshima · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Base yourself near Hiroshima Station, see the Peace Memorial Museum first thing (it opens at 7:30 if you book online), then take the JR Sanyo Line and the JR ferry to Miyajima: about 45 minutes station to island, all covered by the JR Pass. Skip the tram for this trip; it's ¥240 but takes over an hour. Before you fix the day, open the Miyajima tide table: below about 100 cm you can walk to the torii, above about 250 cm it floats.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who the one-day plan suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
First visits on a Kansai–Kyushu trip with one day to spare
JR Pass holders: train and JR ferry are both covered
Early risers: the museum is quietest before 8:30
Think twice
You want both a walk to the torii and the floating view: that needs the right tide day, or a night on the island
You plan to hike Mount Misen too: give Miyajima a full day
You hate early starts: the plan works best from 7:30
Getting to Miyajima: three ways
A · JR train + JR ferry
≈45 min · ≈¥620
Our pick
JR Sanyo Line from Hiroshima to Miyajimaguchi takes about 25–30 minutes (about ¥420), then a 5-minute walk to the pier and a 10-minute ferry (¥200) that runs about every 15 minutes. Both are covered by the JR Pass; pass holders just buy the ¥100 visitor tax at the terminal.
B · Hiroden tram, line 2
70–75 min · ¥240
Cheap, slow
A flat ¥240 fare, paid when you get off, but the trip through the city takes about 70–75 minutes. Worth it only if your hotel is near the tram line and you'd rather watch the city go by than save time.
C · Boat from Peace Park
45 min · ¥2,400
Straight from the A-Bomb Dome
The World Heritage Sea Route leaves Motoyasu Pier, 150 m south of the dome: 17 sailings a day, ¥4,400 return, with the last boat back from Miyajima at 17:30. Book by the day before; IC cards aren't accepted and the ¥100 tax is extra.
Our verdict: JR train plus JR ferry for almost everyone. The boat from Peace Park (C) wins only when you want to go straight from the museum to the island without backtracking and don't mind ¥4,400 return. The tram (B) is for slow days, not one-day plans.
Ten minutes on the JR ferry, and the island fills the windows.
The tide check that decides your afternoon
The Miyajima Tourist Association publishes a yearly tide table and puts it simply: below 100 cm you can walk out to the Great Torii, and above 250 cm the shrine and torii look like they're floating. Low tide alone isn't enough; some days it never drops below 100 cm. The table uses Hiroshima Port levels, and Miyajima runs slightly earlier. Pick the day that has both a sub-100 and an over-250 window in daylight, and plan the island around those times rather than the clock.
The shrine is open from 6:30; in late autumn it closes at 17:30, in December at 17:00, and entry is ¥300. After sunset it's lit until 23:00, but you can't go inside.
Above about 250 cm, this is the view. Below 100 cm, you can walk to its feet.
Eat like a local
Okonomi-mura (Hiroshima city): 23 okonomiyaki counters stacked on floors 2 to 4 of one building in Shintenchi, about 3 minutes from Hatchobori tram stop. It grew from the post-war food stalls on this square. Each counter keeps its own hours, so it suits a late dinner after the island.
Anagomeshi Ueno (Miyajimaguchi): conger eel over rice, the dish this coast is known for, a minute from JR Miyajimaguchi Station. The diner runs from about 10:00 to 19:00 (last order 18:30) and the bento counter from 9:00; it closes when sold out, so take a bento for the ferry if the line is long. Budget about ¥2,000–3,000.
On Omotesando the deer shop too. Eat your snacks inside, not on the street.
A one-day route
7:30 Peace Memorial Museum, booked online for the early slot, then the Peace Park and A-Bomb Dome.
10:00 Tram or taxi back to Hiroshima Station, JR to Miyajimaguchi (about 25–30 minutes).
11:00 Anagomeshi bento, then a JR ferry between 9:10 and 16:10 for the route past the torii.
12:00 Itsukushima Shrine and the torii, timed to your tide window.
15:00 Omotesando shopping street and the deer.
18:30 Back in town for okonomiyaki at Okonomi-mura.
Early morning: Peace Park before the crowds
Midday: the shrine corridors over the water
After dark: back in the city for dinner
Where to stay: three good bases
For a one-day plan
Hiroshima Station
Shinkansen, JR and trams
Arrive by bullet train, take the JR to Miyajimaguchi, and trams leave for Peace Park from the same building. Downside: less atmosphere at night than downtown.
Step off the Shinkansen and into your room →
For evenings out
Hatchobori / Hondori
Okonomi-mura on foot
The covered shopping streets, bars and okonomiyaki, and a short walk or tram ride to Peace Park. Downside: one extra ride to the JR line for Miyajima.
Stay where Hiroshima goes out for okonomiyaki →
For both tides
Miyajima
The island after the boats
Sleep on the island and you can catch a low tide in the morning and the lit torii at night. Downside: fewer dinner options; the last JR ferry back leaves at 22:14.
Have the torii to yourself after the last day-trippers →
⛩️ Rather not juggle trams, trains and ferries? Several small-group day tours cover the Peace Park and Miyajima in one go, with transport sorted and a guide to explain what you're looking at.See Hiroshima and the island with a guide beside you →
📅 Good to know before you book
The tide table comes first: choose your Miyajima date from the Tourist Association's table, then book the hotel around it.
The 7:30 museum slot needs an online reservation, as does the last hour of the day. The museum closes 30–31 December and for a period in mid-February.
The Peace Park boat sells out ahead: it can be booked up to the day before, not on the day online.
Most Hiroshima hotels on booking sites show a free-cancellation date, useful if you move the day to catch a better tide.
Line up a Hiroshima stay around the perfect tide →
Nearby, if you have more time
Mount Misen: Miyajima's summit, by ropeway and a hike; give the island a full day if you want it.
Heading on to Kyushu? Our first-trip Fukuoka guide picks a base by the station.
Coming from Kansai? See Kansai Airport to Kyoto and where to stay in Osaka.
One more thing: the ferry that sails past the torii
Both ferries take 10 minutes and cost ¥200, but JR runs its sailings from Miyajimaguchi between 9:10 and 16:10 on a route that passes close to the Great Torii before docking. Sit or stand on the right-hand side facing forward for the view; it's the first, and often best, look at the torii, and it costs nothing extra.
Source: JR Miyajima Ferry official route and timetable pages, checked 24 November 2026.

## Kamakura From Noon: Temples, Sunset or Both?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

You can see Kamakura properly from a noon start if you stay in one area and follow the closing times. Take the 11:36 from Tokyo (Kamakura at 12:33, no change), do the Great Buddha and Hasedera first, because both stop letting people in around 16:30–16:45, then ride the Enoden to Inamuragasaki for sunset. Finish at Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, which keeps its gates open until 20:00. Trying to fit in Kita-Kamakura's temples as well is what turns a relaxed afternoon into a rush.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who a noon start suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
A slow morning in Tokyo, then one well-paced afternoon
First visits: the Great Buddha, Hasedera and the coast are all on one short train line
Couples who'd rather watch a sunset than tick off six temples
Winter trips: the light and the closing times line up neatly
Think twice
You want Kita-Kamakura's Zen temples and Hase: that needs a morning start
Weekend lunch at the busiest places: expect queues on the Enoden and at Hase
You need step-free routes everywhere: Hasedera's upper terrace and the cape path have slopes and steps
Getting there and around
From Tokyo Station, the JR Yokosuka Line runs straight to Kamakura: the 11:36 arrives at 12:33 (57 minutes, ¥1,040 ticket or ¥1,034 by IC card, on our weekday check). From Shinjuku, the Shonan-Shinjuku Line with a change at Ofuna takes about 54 minutes. A JR Pass covers both.
In Kamakura, the little green Enoden does the rest. It's ¥200 from Kamakura to Hase, ¥200 from Hase to Inamuragasaki and ¥220 from Inamuragasaki back to Kamakura. Tap your IC card and you don't need to think about tickets.
The Enoden: three short rides cover the whole afternoon.
Three ways to spend the afternoon
A · Temples first
Hase · arrive by 15:30
Great Buddha + Hasedera
Pick Hase and give it time. The Great Buddha (¥300) lets people in until 16:45 from October to March and 17:15 from April to September. Hasedera (¥400) takes last entry at 16:30 from July to March and 17:00 from April to June. They're 5 minutes apart on foot, 7 minutes from Hase Station. Get there by 15:30 at the latest to enjoy both.
B · Coast first
Sunset · ~16:30 in winter
Beach, cape, dinner by the sea
Walk Yuigahama, ride the Enoden to Inamuragasaki for sunset, then go one stop on to Shichirigahama for dinner at bills (dinner from 17:00, open to 21:00, bookable online). Back to Kamakura or on to Fujisawa by Enoden.
C · One of each
Our pick
Hase, then the cape, then Hachimangu
Temples while they're open, sunset when they close, and Tsurugaoka Hachimangu after dark, since its gates stay open until 20:00. Every move is one Enoden ride or a short walk.
Our verdict: from a noon start, do C. In winter the sun sets around 16:30, just as Hase closes, so the day flows on its own. The answer changes in summer: in late June the sun sets around 19:00, so you have time for B's beach walk too, and dinner by the sea makes sense. On a grey or rainy day, skip the sunset and do A slowly, then Hachimangu and an early dinner.
The Great Buddha at Kotoku-in: last entry 16:45 in winter.
Our noon route (winter timings)
11:36 Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station, no change.
12:33 Kamakura. Change to the Enoden for Hase (about 7 minutes).
13:00 Walk 7 minutes to the Great Buddha. Add ¥50 to step inside the statue (until 16:30).
13:45 Walk 5 minutes to Hasedera. Late lunch at Kaikoan, the temple's own restaurant, looking over Yuigahama (open until 16:00).
15:45 Enoden two stops to Inamuragasaki, then an 8-minute walk to the cape.
16:30 Sunset over Shichirigahama and Enoshima.
17:15 Enoden back to Kamakura, then 10 minutes on foot to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu (open until 20:00), and dinner near the station.
Early afternoon: the Great Buddha
Sunset: the coast below Inamuragasaki
After dark: back to Kamakura by Enoden
Lunch and dinner on this route
Kaikoan (inside Hasedera): the temple's restaurant has wide windows over Yuigahama beach and serves vegetarian curry, vegan pasta and desserts. It's open 10:00 to 16:00, so it works as a late lunch. You need a Hasedera ticket to get in.
bills Shichirigahama: one Enoden stop past Inamuragasaki, open every day 7:00 to 21:00, with the dinner menu from 17:00 and terrace seats above the sea. Book on the official site if you want a table straight after sunset.
Around Kamakura Station: after Hachimangu, the streets between the shrine and the station are the easiest place to find dinner without another train ride.
Tsurugaoka Hachimangu: the one big sight still open after sunset.
Making it a night: three bases
For trains and dinner
Kamakura Station
Hachimangu at 6 a.m.
JR and the Enoden in one place, dinner on your doorstep, and the shrine opens at 6:00 for a walk before anyone else arrives. Downside: the busiest streets in town during the day.
Sleep a short walk from the shrine steps →
For the sea
Yuigahama / Hase
The Buddha at 8:00
Be at Kotoku-in when it opens and on the beach before breakfast. Downside: fewer places to eat late, and smaller guesthouses rather than big hotels.
Hear the waves from your room in Hase →
For value and Enoshima
Fujisawa
The other end of the Enoden
A bigger city with more business hotels, the Tokaido Line to Tokyo, and the Enoden all the way to Kamakura for ¥310, passing Enoshima on the way. Downside: you're not in Kamakura itself.
Start tomorrow at the Enoshima end of the line →
🧭 Want someone else to handle the timing? Enoden itself sells a one-day Kamakura tour with an English-speaking guide that covers Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, the Great Buddha, Hasedera and Enoshima, and guided Kamakura day trips from Tokyo are listed on Klook too.Let a guide pace your Kamakura day →
📅 Good to know before you book
Closing times change with the season: Kotoku-in closes at 17:30 from April to September and 17:00 from October to March. Hasedera's later hours run only April to June. Spring and early summer give you the longest afternoons.
Mount Fuji from the cape: the government's "Kanto Fujimi 100" list notes Fuji shows best from Inamuragasaki on windy days from early December to late February. That's the season when a noon start pays off most.
A night by the sea: if you want the 8:00 Great Buddha without the crowds, stay over. Most hotels on the big booking sites offer free cancellation, so you can hold a room and decide once you've seen the forecast.
Turn the sunset into a sunrise too →
Winter sunsets come around 16:30, right after the temples close.
Nearby, if you have more time
Zeniarai Benten: the shrine where people wash coins in spring water, about 30 minutes on foot from the Great Buddha.
Daibutsu hiking trail: the Daibutsu-zaka entrance is about 10 minutes from Kotoku-in, a woodland ridge walk if you start earlier.
Enoshima: stay on the Enoden past Shichirigahama for the island itself. Travelling with someone who dislikes stairs? See Enoshima without the stairs.
One more thing: save the big shrine for last
Most day-trippers start at Tsurugaoka Hachimangu because it's closest to the station, then rush to Hase before it closes. Do it the other way round. The temples in Hase stop admitting people around 16:30, but Hachimangu's gates are open from 6:00 to 20:00 every day of the year, and it's free. Walk up the main steps after sunset, when most of the afternoon crowd is on the train home, and you have Kamakura's biggest shrine at a quieter hour.
Source: Tsurugaoka Hachimangu, Kotoku-in and Hasedera official sites, checked 24 November 2026.

## Kansai Airport to Kyoto: Haruka, Limousine Bus or via Osaka?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kansai-airport-to-kyoto
City: Kyoto · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

For most first-time arrivals we'd take the JR Haruka: about 75 to 80 minutes from the airport to Kyoto Station with no change, and ¥2,700 on the visitor one-way ticket. Pick the limousine bus (¥2,800) if you land late, because it runs until 23:20 while the last Haruka leaves at 22:16, or if you want your suitcases in the hold. Go via Osaka on ordinary trains only if your hotel is near Shijo or Kawaramachi and you travel light: it's the cheapest, but it means changes.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who the Haruka suits, and who it doesn't
Haruka is right for
Hotels around Kyoto Station, or anywhere you'll reach by taxi or subway from there
Daytime and early-evening landings
Foreign visitors who can use the discounted HARUKA One-way Ticket
Think about the bus or Hankyu if
Your flight lands after about 21:30 and immigration is slow
You have more cases than hands: the bus takes them in the hold
Your hotel is on Shijo-dori and you'd rather not change at Kyoto Station
The three ways in
A · JR Haruka
75–80 min · ¥2,700
Fastest, no change
About every 30 minutes; the first weekday train leaves the airport at 06:31 and the last at 22:16. The HARUKA One-way Ticket for foreign visitors on a temporary-visitor stay costs ¥2,700 to Kyoto (¥1,350 child) if bought from 1 November 2026, and covers ordinary reserved or unreserved seats. Without it, the regular unreserved fare is about ¥3,100.
B · Limousine bus
85–90 min · ¥2,800
Late landings, big bags
From Terminal 1 (and most from Terminal 2) to Kyoto Station Hachijo Exit, roughly every 20 minutes. The last bus leaves T1 at 23:20 and arrives at 0:45. No reservations towards Kyoto: first come, first seated. Pay cash or tap ICOCA; suitcases go in the hold.
C · Ordinary trains via Osaka
¥1,670 · about 1 h 50
Cheapest, for light packers
Nankai to the Sakaisuji subway, then the Hankyu Kyoto Line straight to Karasuma or Kyoto-kawaramachi: about ¥1,670 and about 1 hour 50 minutes. JR local and rapid trains via Osaka to Kyoto Station are about ¥1,900. Every change means stairs and crowds with your bags.
Our verdict: Haruka for most arrivals, on the ¥2,700 visitor ticket if you qualify. The answer changes when you land late (take the bus: it runs over an hour after the last Haruka), when you have heavy luggage and a hotel near the Hachijo side (bus), or when you travel light to a Shijo hotel and want the cheapest ride (Hankyu via Osaka).
The JR and Nankai platforms are right outside arrivals at Kansai Airport.
Choose by where your hotel is
Kyoto Station, south side (Hachijo): the limousine bus stops right outside, in front of the Avanti building opposite the Hachijo Exit, so you skip the station crowds entirely.
Kyoto Station, north side or Kyoto Tower area: the Haruka is simplest; walk out through the central gates.
Shijo-Karasuma or Kawaramachi: either the Haruka plus a short subway or taxi ride, or the Hankyu route via Osaka that ends right under Shijo-dori.
Arashiyama: GOOD LUCK TRIP lists Haruka plus the JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama at about 1 hour 45 minutes from ¥3,300.
Kyoto Station: the Haruka arrives inside, the bus stops on the south side.
Eat like a local on arrival night
Landed hungry? Go up, not out. Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of the Kyoto Station building has nine ramen shops from around Japan, open 11:00 to 22:00 (last order 21:30), and Navitime puts a meal at about ¥1,000 to ¥3,000. It's the easy first dinner for anyone off a daytime Haruka. If you arrive on the last train or bus, the convenience stores around the station are your friend; save the real Kyoto dinner for tomorrow.
A first bowl of ramen without leaving the station building.
Where to stay: three good bases
For late arrivals
Kyoto Station
Off the bus, into bed
Both the Haruka and the limousine bus end here, and so does your trip home. Downside: evenings are quieter than downtown, and temples are a bus ride away.
Sleep under Kyoto Tower, minutes from your train →
For a first trip
Shijo-Karasuma
The centre of everything
Subway and Hankyu at the door, Nishiki Market a short walk. Downside: one extra ride from the airport train. Our first-trip Kyoto guide explains why we pick it.
Base yourself where Kyoto's lines all meet →
For evenings out
Kawaramachi
Pontocho at your door
Restaurants, bars and Gion over the river, and the Hankyu line from Osaka ends here. Downside: busy and pricier on weekends.
Stroll home from Pontocho's lantern-lit lanes →
🚄 Want the Haruka sorted before you fly? The discounted visitor ticket is sold outside Japan, through JR West's own site and overseas agencies, and an agency voucher is exchanged for the ticket in Japan after you land. Booking it before departure means one less queue after a long flight.Land, collect, and be on the Haruka in minutes →
📅 Good to know before you book
The visitor ticket went up on 1 November 2026, from ¥2,200 to ¥2,700 to Kyoto. Tickets bought on or before 31 October stay valid with nothing extra to pay. It's one per person, and Japanese nationals can't use it.
Going home by bus? The Kyoto-to-airport limousine needs a reservation (up to a month ahead); the airport-to-Kyoto direction doesn't take them.
Door to door: Yasaka's shared airport shuttle is ¥4,300 per person, but must be booked by 12:00 two days before. A taxi is about ¥40,000.
Most Kyoto hotels on booking sites show a free-cancellation date, handy if your flight time moves.
Find a Kyoto room that suits your landing time →
If you're splitting the trip with Osaka
Staying in Osaka first? Our Kansai Airport to Osaka guide compares Nankai and JR by hotel area.
The HARUKA One-way Ticket also has an Osaka price (¥1,900 to the Osaka city zone), so check which city you land into first.
Still deciding where to sleep in Kyoto? Start with our first-trip guide.
One more thing: Kyoto's first view is free, above the platforms
Before you head to the hotel, take the escalators beside the station's Great Stairs, 171 steps lit by about 15,000 LEDs, and walk the Skyway, a glass corridor 45 metres above the central hall that starts from the 11th floor. It's free and open 10:00 to 22:00, and it's the easiest way to see Kyoto Tower and the city at night without paying for an observatory.
Source: japan-guide.com and GOOD LUCK TRIP, Kyoto Station Building, checked 24 November 2026.

## Naha First Trip: Where to Stay and Do You Need a Car?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/naha-where-to-stay-do-you-need-a-car
City: Okinawa · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

For most first trips we'd stay near Kokusai-dori, between Prefectural Office and Makishi stations, and skip the car while you're in Naha. The Yui Rail monorail gets you from the airport in 13 to 16 minutes (¥290–¥320) and on to Shuri Castle in 11 more. Rent a car only for the days you head north. Churaumi Aquarium is about two hours by car from the airport, against about three by express bus.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who a car-free Naha base suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Short trips of 2–4 nights centred on Naha, Shuri and the markets
Travellers who want a drink with dinner: Japan's drink-driving rules are very strict
Anyone arriving late: the monorail starts right at the airport terminal
Rainy days: the market streets off Kokusai-dori are covered
Think twice
Your trip is mostly beaches and the north: base yourself up there with a car
Families with several suitcases changing hotels often: a car is easier
Light sleepers right on Kokusai-dori: pick a side street
Getting around: the monorail
The Yui Rail runs from Naha Airport through the city to Shuri and on to Tedako-Uranishi. Single fares start at ¥250. From the airport it's 11 minutes to Asahibashi (¥290), 13 to Prefectural Office (¥290), 16 to Makishi (¥320), 19 to Omoromachi (¥320) and 27 to Shuri (¥360).
Tap in with Suica, ICOCA, PASMO or any of Japan's national IC cards. You can top them up at Yui Rail stations, but you can't buy a Suica there. The 1-day ticket costs ¥1,000 and the 2-day ¥1,800. Both count 24 or 48 hours from purchase, not calendar days.
Pass maths: airport to Makishi (¥320) plus a Shuri round trip from Makishi (¥290 each way) comes to ¥900, so a 1-day ticket only pays off once you add a fourth ride, such as Omoromachi (¥250). Because it runs for 24 hours, buy it on arrival in the afternoon and it still covers the next morning.
Naha is compact: most of what you'll want is along one monorail line.
Three bases, three kinds of trip
A · Kokusai-dori · Our pick
13–16 min · ¥290–¥320
Walk to dinner and the market
Prefectural Office or Makishi station. Kokusai-dori's covered side streets lead to the Makishi Public Market, and Shuri is 11 minutes from Makishi. Downside: the main street is busy and loud at night, so ask for a room off it.
Wake up a few steps from the market lanes →
B · Asahibashi
11 min · ¥290
Bus trips and the first stop from the airport
The closest base to the airport, with Naha Bus Terminal next to the station for buses north. Kokusai-dori is two stops away. Downside: quieter in the evening, with fewer places to eat on the doorstep.
Stay where Okinawa's day-trip buses leave →
C · Omoromachi
19 min · ¥320
Newer, calmer, malls next door
T Galleria by DFS is right by exit 1, with big malls nearby and wider streets. Easy for families, and Makishi is 3 minutes away (¥250). Downside: less old-Naha character after dark.
Choose a calm base with room for the kids →
Our verdict: for a first trip of a few nights, stay near Kokusai-dori (A). It changes if most of your days are bus trips north or you land late and fly out early: pick Asahibashi (B). With children, lots of shopping or a car parked at the hotel, Omoromachi (C) is easier.
Do you need a car?
In Naha: no. The monorail covers the airport, Kokusai-dori, Omoromachi and Shuri. For the north: usually yes. The official Churaumi Aquarium site puts it at about two hours from Naha Airport by car (via the Okinawa Expressway) and about three hours by express bus. Beaches and capes further up the island are slower still without a car.
The neat answer for most trips is to split it: spend your Naha nights car-free, then pick up a rental for the days you go north, or stay up there a night or two and keep the car.
Naha has its own small beach; the famous ones are further north, where a car pays off.
Eat like a local: the Makishi Public Market
Turn off Kokusai-dori halfway along and follow the covered market street to the Makishi Public Market, Naha's kitchen since 1950, rebuilt on the same spot and reopened in March 2023. It's about 10 minutes on foot from Makishi or Miebashi station, open roughly 8:00 to 22:00 (hours vary by shop).
Downstairs: 75 shops selling fish from local waters, Okinawan pork and beef, island vegetables, sea grapes and shima rakkyo (small island shallots).
Upstairs: 12 eateries serving Okinawan dishes such as soki soba, champuru and rafute (slow-braised pork belly), plus sata andagi doughnuts. The city notes the upstairs restaurants stay open fairly late, so it works for dinner too.
Ask for "shiibun": the Okinawan word for the little extra a stallholder sometimes adds to your bag.
🐋 Going north without a car? Round-trip highway bus tickets from Naha to Churaumi Aquarium are sold on Klook, so you can lock in seats for the roughly three-hour ride each way instead of working out the bus routes on the day.See the whale sharks without renting a car →
Shureimon, the gate below Shuri Castle: 11 minutes from Makishi by monorail.
📅 Good to know before you book
Shuri Castle has just reopened: the interior of the rebuilt main hall was due to reopen on 23 November 2026, seven years after the 2019 fire. Expect it to be busy for a while; the halls around it are still being rebuilt.
Sundays on Kokusai-dori: about 1.3 km of the street becomes a car-free "transit mall" from 12:00 to 18:00 (cancelled in rain). If your hotel is on the street itself, arrive by monorail and walk, or check in before noon.
Car days: if you're renting for the north, book the hotel and the car for the same dates. Most hotels on the big booking sites offer free cancellation, so you can firm up the plan later.
Line up your Naha nights before the car days →
Nearby, if you have more time
Shuri Castle: Shuri Station, 11 minutes from Makishi (¥290). The grounds outside the paid area are free to walk.
Naminoue Shrine: Naha's seaside shrine, on the coast west of Kokusai-dori.
The north by car: Churaumi Aquarium is about two hours' drive; make it a night up there rather than a rushed round trip.
One more thing: have your market fish cooked upstairs
The market's best trick is "mochiage", running since 1990. Buy fish, lobster or meat at a stall on the ground floor, and one of the eateries upstairs will cook it for you as sashimi, grilled or as a steak. You pay for the ingredients at the stall and a cooking fee at the restaurant. Ask the stallholder which upstairs place suits what you bought. They'll point you to the right counter, and many people add a drink or a bowl of noodles while they wait.
Source: Highlighting Japan (Government of Japan), November 2025, interview with Naha City's market office; checked 24 November 2026.

## Namba Station: Which Namba, Which Exit for Your Hotel
URL: https://japanbystation.com/namba-station-which-namba
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Key facts:
- Four stations called Namba: Osaka Metro Namba (Midosuji M20, Yotsubashi Y15, Sennichimae S16), Nankai Namba (trains to Kansai Airport and Koyasan), Osaka-Namba (Kintetsu to Nara and Hanshin to Kobe, one shared station) and JR Namba (Yamatoji Line). All are linked on foot, mostly underground.
- To Kansai Airport: Nankai rapi:t from Nankai Namba, 34 min at the fastest; Airport Express about 45 min for the ¥970 base fare. Limousine bus from OCAT (JR Namba building) about 48 min to Terminal 1, ¥1,400 adult (checked 24 Nov 2026).
- Destination-first exits: Dotonbori → Osaka Metro Exit 14; Namba Parks and Nankai trains → Exit 4; Namba HIPS → Exit 15-B walkway; Kintetsu/Hanshin and Namba Walk → Exit 27 direction.
- Stay by traveller: airport by train → Swissotel Nankai Osaka (on top of Nankai Namba); airport bus, Nara or Kobe → Hotel Monterey Grasmere Osaka (1 min from JR Namba); nights out → Cross Hotel Osaka (3 min from Exit 14); rainy days and laundry → Namba Oriental Hotel (30 s from Namba Walk B21).

"Namba Station" is really four stations: Osaka Metro Namba (the subway), Nankai Namba (trains to Kansai Airport), Osaka-Namba (Kintetsu to Nara and Hanshin to Kobe) and JR Namba. They are linked on foot, mostly underground, so pick by your train line, then by the exit for where you are going. For your hotel, match it to how you will reach the airport: rapi:t people sleep near Nankai, bus people near JR Namba.
About a 5-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who a base at Namba Station suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Travellers flying in and out of Kansai Airport: direct trains and a direct bus start here
Food-first trips: Dotonbori, Hozenji and Kuromon Market are a walk away
Day trips to Nara or Kobe: Kintetsu and Hanshin trains leave from Osaka-Namba
Night owls: you can walk back to the hotel after the last train
Think twice
JR Pass holders doing Kyoto day trips: Osaka Station in Umeda is easier (see Osaka Station vs Umeda)
Light sleepers who want quiet streets: the Dotonbori side stays loud late
Anyone hoping to catch the shinkansen in a hurry: Shin-Osaka is 16 minutes away on the Midosuji Line
Which Namba station do you need?
Look at the line on your ticket or map app, then use this list.
Going to Kansai Airport by train, or to Koyasan? Nankai Namba. Its platforms are on the 3rd floor of the Nankai building, under the Swissotel.
Going to Nara or Kobe? Osaka-Namba, one station shared by Kintetsu and Hanshin, three levels underground. Platforms 1 and 2 are for Nara, platform 3 for Kobe-Sannomiya. Until 2009 it was called Kintetsu Namba, so older maps differ.
Going to Umeda, Shin-Osaka or Tennoji? Osaka Metro Namba on the Midosuji Line (M20). The same station also has the Yotsubashi (Y15) and Sennichimae (S16) lines.
Going east on JR towards Tennoji, Nara or Horyuji? JR Namba, the end of the Yamatoji Line, directly connected to the OCAT building. It sits a little west of the others; the hotel above it lists the Nankai trains as about 7 minutes' walk.
The rapi:t, Nankai's airport train, leaves from Nankai Namba.
Our suggestion: type the operator into your map app ("Nankai Namba", "Kintetsu Osaka-Namba"), not just "Namba". The four stations are a few minutes apart, and the wrong one costs you a walk with your bags.
Which exit? Start from where you are going
Exit numbers below are on the Osaka Metro Namba station map, the one most signs follow.
Going to Dotonbori, Hozenji Temple or the Shinsaibashisuji arcade? Use Exit 14, on the east side of Midosuji. Exit 25 also reaches Dotonbori from the west side.
Going to Namba Parks, Takashimaya or the Nankai airport trains? Use Exit 4. Namba Parks is directly connected to Nankai Namba.
Going to Namba HIPS? Take Exit 15-B, a covered walkway straight into the building.
Going to Kintetsu or Hanshin trains? Follow signs for Exit 27 and Namba Walk; the Osaka-Namba gates are along that passage.
Going to the airport bus at OCAT or to JR Namba? From the Yotsubashi Line, take the connecting passage at Exit 30. The airport buses leave from the 2nd floor of the OCAT bus terminal.
Going to Kuromon Market or Nippombashi? Stay underground and walk east along Namba Walk, a 715 m shopping street that ends at Nippombashi station; the market is right outside.
Above ground in Namba: pick your exit first and you surface on the right block.
Namba to Kansai Airport: rapi:t, Airport Express or bus?
rapi:t (Nankai Namba): 34 minutes at the fastest, every seat reserved. Since 1 April 2026 the seat surcharge is ¥700 at the counter or ¥550 with Nankai's ticketless app, on top of the ¥970 fare. Many guides still quote the old, lower surcharge.
Airport Express (Nankai Namba): about 45 minutes, no surcharge, so just the ¥970 fare. Good if you travel light outside rush hour.
Limousine bus (OCAT, by JR Namba): about 48 minutes to Terminal 1 and 11 more to Terminal 2, ¥1,400 adult (¥700 child), departures from 06:10 to 22:40, no reservation. Best with big suitcases: you load them once and sit down.
Coming the other way? Our Kansai Airport to Osaka guide matches the train to your hotel area.
Where to stay near Namba Station: one pick per traveller
Airport by train
Swissotel Nankai Osaka
The airport train is downstairs
Directly connected to Nankai Namba, so the rapi:t and Airport Express leave from under your room; the Osaka Convention and Tourism Bureau puts it 3 minutes from Metro Exit 4. 546 rooms, a spa and a gym. Downside: big-hotel prices.
Take the lift down to the airport train →
Airport bus, Nara or Kobe days

Above JR Namba and the airport bus
Rooms on floors 24 to 31: JR Namba is a 1-minute walk and the Kintetsu and Hanshin trains to Nara and Kobe about 1 minute. The OCAT airport bus terminal is directly connected to JR Namba. Downside: the Midosuji Line is about 5 minutes away and the Nankai trains about 7.
Ride the lift down to the airport bus →
Nights out, first trip
Cross Hotel Osaka
One minute from the canal
3 minutes from Exit 14 and 1 minute from Dotonbori, with a separate bath and toilet in every room and 24-hour reception. Downside: you are in the busiest, loudest block of Namba. Compare areas in Osaka for night owls.
Walk home from the neon in a minute →
Rainy days, longer stays
Namba Oriental Hotel
The Sennichimae side, under cover
Besides the Dotonbori side, consider the Sennichimae side towards Nippombashi: calmer, and Kuromon Market is close. This hotel is 30 seconds from Namba Walk exit B21, so you reach the trains underground; it has free guest lounges including a laundry lounge, handy after a week on the road. Downside: no direct airport link.
Stay dry from the lobby to the platform →
Walking times from the Osaka Convention and Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp) and the hotels' own pages, checked 24 November 2026. More prices in Osaka hotels by budget.
Eat around Namba Station: the famous plate and the local one
What most visitors go for: Jiyuken, open since 1910, about 3 minutes from the station opposite Bic Camera. Order the meibutsu (signature) curry, listed at ¥650 on Hot Pepper Gourmet. Cash only, closed Mondays (Tuesday when Monday is a holiday).
Dig a little deeper: Marufuku Coffee Sennichimae Honten, a coffee house roasting its own beans since 1934, about 5 minutes from Metro Namba. Regulars come for the thick hotcakes cooked on a copper griddle and the homemade coffee jelly; Retty and Rurubu put a set at about ¥1,300 to ¥1,450. It opens 8:00 to 23:00 (last order 22:30), so it works for an early breakfast before the airport train.
The lion-head stage of Namba Yasaka Shrine, in the Namba district.
📅 Good to know before you book
"Namba" in a hotel name can mean anywhere from Nippombashi to Sakuragawa. Check the minutes to the station you will use (Nankai for the rapi:t, OCAT for the bus) before you book.
The last airport bus from OCAT leaves at 22:40 and the bus takes no reservations, so plan a late departure around the train instead.
Free cancellation: many Namba listings offer it on Booking.com (check each one), so you can hold a room while you compare sides.
See which side of Namba fits your dates →
Nearby, if you have more time
Walks from the station: our things to do around Namba lists the canal, the food streets and the arcades with walking times.
Namba or Tennoji on a budget? We priced the same nights in Namba or Tennoji for ¥30,000.
Just need a cheap private room? See a private room in Namba for about ¥5,000.
Dotonbori is a 3–5 minute walk from Exit 14.
One more thing: drop your bags on the 2nd floor, not in a locker
On your last day, the coin lockers at Namba fill up and the Kintetsu ones take only ¥100 coins. Nankai Namba has a staffed n·e·s·t counter on the 2nd floor, in front of the Central Ticket Gate and outside the gates, open 9:00 to 21:00. It keeps a bag for ¥800 a day, or sends it to Kansai Airport for ¥2,500 a piece, so you can spend the day in Namba with empty hands and pick it up at the airport.
Source: n·e·s·t counter page (airporter.co.jp); Osaka Convention and Tourism Bureau Hands-free Travel page (information as of 1 October 2025); Kintetsu coin locker page. Checked 24 November 2026.

## Nara: Day Trip or One Night? Deer, Trains and a Quiet Evening
URL: https://japanbystation.com/nara-day-trip-or-one-night
City: Nara · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Key facts:
- Trains: Kintetsu Osaka-Namba to Kintetsu-Nara about 40 min, ¥680; Kyoto to Kintetsu-Nara about 35 min by limited express; JR Kyoto–Nara about 45 min (checked 24 Nov 2026).
- Closing times (Nov–Mar): Todaiji Great Buddha Hall 8:00–17:00 (¥800); Kasuga Taisha 7:00–17:00, inner area 9:00–16:00 (¥700).
- Deer: about 1,465 in the July 2025 count; crackers ¥200; stags can get aggressive in autumn.
- Evening: Nara's official evening course goes Nigatsudo for sunset → Sarusawa Pond → The Bar at Nara Hotel (18:00–23:00).

A day trip is enough for Nara's big three: Todaiji's Great Buddha, Kasuga Taisha and the deer park are all a walk from Kintetsu-Nara Station, and in winter they close around 17:00. Stay one night if you want what a day trip misses: sunset from the free hillside veranda of Nigatsudo, Naramachi's old streets in the evening, and the park again the next morning, unhurried. Our pick for a first visit: Kintetsu from Osaka or Kyoto, out early, and one night if you're moving between the two cities anyway.
About a 6-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who a night in Nara suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Travellers moving Kyoto → Osaka (or back): Nara sits between them on Kintetsu
Photographers who want sunset and early-morning light in the park
Anyone who'd rather walk slowly than rush four temples into one afternoon
Think twice
Night owls: the temples close by about 17:00 and evenings are quiet
Short trips with one base: a day trip from Osaka or Kyoto covers the highlights
Rail Pass holders on a tight budget: Kintetsu isn't covered
Getting there: Kintetsu or JR?
From Osaka-Namba (Kintetsu): about 40 minutes to Kintetsu-Nara, ¥680. Trains also stop at Tsuruhashi, which makes Osaka's Korean food district an easy base (see living like a local in Osaka).
From Osaka Station (JR): about 50 minutes on the Yamatoji Rapid to JR Nara. The new JR limited express "Mahorobago" has also linked Osaka and Nara since March 2025.
From Kyoto (Kintetsu): about 35 minutes by limited express (about ¥1,280 with the seat charge) or about 46 minutes by express (about ¥760). The sightseeing train Aoniyoshi takes about 33–36 minutes for ¥1,490 per person in pairs, but generally doesn't run on Thursdays.
From Kyoto (JR): about 45 minutes on the Miyakoji Rapid, covered by the Japan Rail Pass.
Why Kintetsu wins for most: Kintetsu-Nara is about 7 minutes' walk from Kofukuji and about 15 from Todaiji. JR Nara is a longer walk west of the park, roughly 15–20 minutes further.
Todaiji's Great Buddha Hall: 8:00 to 17:00 from November to March.
Three ways to do Nara
A. Day trip: the big three, done by five
Arrive by 9:00, walk Kofukuji → the deer park → Todaiji (¥800) → Kasuga Taisha, lunch in between. From November to March the Great Buddha Hall runs 8:00–17:00 (7:30–17:30 from April to October), Kasuga Taisha's grounds 7:00–17:00 and its paid inner area 9:00–16:00 (¥700). Kofukuji's five-storey pagoda is under a long repair and covered, so don't plan your photos around it.
B. One night: sunset, Naramachi, an easy second morning
Do the day as above, but end it at Nigatsudo, the hall on the hillside above Todaiji, for sunset. Nara's own evening walking course goes from there down to Sarusawa Pond and ends at The Bar at Nara Hotel (18:00–23:00). Next morning: Isuien Garden (9:30–16:30, ¥1,200, closed Tuesdays) and Naramachi's old townhouses, then a train on to Osaka or Kyoto.
Kasuga Taisha's stone lanterns. Its grounds open at 7:00 in winter.
C. Nara between Kyoto and Osaka
If you're changing bases anyway, send big luggage ahead or use lockers, ride Kintetsu from Kyoto, spend the day in Nara, and carry on to Osaka-Namba in the evening on the same railway. You see Nara without an extra night or a round trip.
Our verdict: one night if you're moving between Kyoto and Osaka anyway or love photography; a day trip if you have one base and three or four nights. It changes for Rail Pass holders: then JR, and a day trip is the better use of the pass.
The deer: timing and the rules
The July 2025 count found about 1,465 deer, the most since 1953. They are wild and protected, not pets. Nara's visitor bureau asks you to feed them only the deer crackers sold in the park (¥200), one at a time, to keep bags and maps out of reach, and to open your hands to show you've run out. Stags can be aggressive, especially in autumn, and about 200 fawns are born each year at the Rokuen enclosure, where mothers and fawns stay until about mid-July; give any mother deer extra space in early summer. The bureau also runs early-morning deer-calling events at Tobihino in some seasons.
In Nara the deer wander well beyond the park.
Eat like a local
Kakinoha-zushi at Izasa-chaya (near Todaiji): pressed sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves, Nara's signature. 11:00–17:00 (last order 16:00), irregular closing days. A good lunch between Todaiji and Kasuga.
Nakatanidou (5 minutes from Kintetsu-Nara): famous for its high-speed mochi pounding; a yomogi (mugwort) mochi is ¥200, cash only. Listings disagree on hours and closing days, so treat it as a daytime stop.
An evening drink at The Bar at Nara Hotel: 18:00–23:00 (last order 22:30), the final stop of the city's own evening walk. The hotel opened in 1909.
The one-night version, with times (winter)
9:00 Kintetsu-Nara. Kofukuji (9:00–17:00), then into the park.
10:30 Todaiji's Great Buddha Hall (¥800).
12:00 Kakinoha-zushi at Izasa-chaya.
13:30 Kasuga Taisha and its lantern paths; the inner area closes at 16:00.
16:00 Check in, then up to Nigatsudo for sunset (about 16:45–17:00 in winter).
18:00 Down past Sarusawa Pond, dinner, a nightcap at The Bar at Nara Hotel.
Morning: the park and its deer
Late morning: the Great Buddha
Dusk: what day-trippers miss

Kofukuji is about 7 minutes away, and the trains to Osaka-Namba and Kyoto leave from here.

For Rail Pass holders

Pass-covered trains in both directions. The park is a longer walk or a short bus ride.

About 10–15 minutes' walk south of Kintetsu-Nara, with small inns and guesthouses. Most attractions close at 17:00.

🚆 Doing Nara and more on Kintetsu? The Kintetsu Rail Pass for visitors covers Osaka, Nara and Kyoto lines, and limited express tickets can be booked in English.Ride Kyoto, Nara and Osaka on one pass →
📅 Good to know before you book
Lantern nights: Kasuga Taisha lights about 3,000 lanterns on 14 and 15 August and on Setsubun in February every year, and the city runs evening light-ups of Ukimido and Sarusawa Pond from July to September. Worth knowing if your dates fall on them.
No Aoniyoshi on Thursdays: plan the sightseeing train for another day.
Free cancellation: most Nara hotels offer it, so holding a room while you decide costs nothing.
Nearby, if you have more time
Naramachi Koshi-no-ie: a free traditional townhouse, 9:00–17:00, closed Mondays.
Fushimi Inari: on the JR line back to Kyoto. See Fushimi Inari: dawn, afternoon or after dark?
Kyoto as a base: where to stay in Kyoto on a first trip.
One more thing: sunset from Nigatsudo's veranda
Nigatsudo, the hall on the hillside above the Great Buddha, looks out over the whole city. Listings say it is open at all hours with no ticket, and the city's official evening walk starts here for the sunset and the night view. It's the reason we'd stay the night.
Sources: Nara Visitor Bureau evening course, Rurubu (open 24 hours, free), checked 24 November 2026.

## Osaka Station vs Umeda: Same Place? Which Side for Your Hotel
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-station-vs-umeda
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

Key facts:
- Same hub, different stations: JR uses the name Osaka Station; Hankyu and Hanshin use Osaka-umeda (renamed from Umeda on 1 October 2019); Osaka Metro has Umeda, Higashi-Umeda and Nishi-Umeda. All are linked on foot.
- HARUKA to Kansai Airport: underground track 21 (track 24 towards Kyoto), nearest gate the West Gate.
- Airport bus to Kansai Airport: from Hankyu Sanbangai, about 60 min to Terminal 1, ¥1,800 adult one way, no reservation (Kansai Airport Transportation Enterprise, checked 24 Nov 2026).
- Stay by traveller: HARUKA arrivals → Osaka Station Hotel (West Gate); early trains → Hotel Granvia Osaka (Central Gate); families → Hotel Hankyu RESPIRE (3 min from the 3rd-floor bridge gate); budget → Nakazakicho, 800 m east.

Yes, it is the same place. JR calls its station Osaka Station; the private railways and the subway call theirs Umeda or Osaka-umeda. They form one hub you can walk across, so the station you need depends only on your train line. For your hotel, the side matters more than the name: pick the side your trains and airport bus use, and you skip the maze with your luggage.
About a 5-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who a base at Osaka Station suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
JR Pass holders and anyone doing day trips: JR, Hankyu and Hanshin all start here
Travellers arriving on the HARUKA or the airport limousine bus
Rainy days: much of the area is linked by covered decks and underground walkways
Families who want big department stores and food halls next to the hotel
Think twice
Travellers who want to walk out of the hotel into old streets and small bars: that is Tenma or Nakazakicho, a short walk away
Tight budgets: hotels on top of the station cost more (see the prices below)
Anyone who hates crowds at rush hour: the main concourses are busy
Osaka Station or Umeda: which one do you need?
Look at the line on your ticket or app, then use this list. All of these stations sit inside the same few blocks.
JR lines (Loop Line, Kyoto and Kobe lines, the HARUKA, the Kuroshio): JR Osaka Station. A JR Pass works here.
Hankyu (to Kyoto-Kawaramachi, Kobe-Sannomiya, Takarazuka): Hankyu Osaka-umeda, platforms on the 3rd floor of its own terminal. It was renamed from "Umeda" on 1 October 2019, which is why older maps still show the old name.
Hanshin (to Kobe and Koshien): Hanshin Osaka-Umeda, underground next to the Hanshin Department Store. Renamed on the same day.
Osaka Metro: Umeda for the Midosuji Line (Namba, Tennoji, Shin-Osaka), Higashi-Umeda for the Tanimachi Line, Nishi-Umeda for the Yotsubashi Line. Three names, three stations, all reached on foot underground.
JR Tozai Line: Kitashinchi, a separate JR station south of Osaka Station, within walking distance.
Osaka Station's atrium: the JR side of the hub, with decks linking it to the buildings around it.
Our suggestion: type the line name, not just "Umeda", into your map app. "Umeda" alone can send you to the wrong one of six stations.
Which side? Start from where you are going
Going to Kansai Airport on the HARUKA? Use the underground platforms on the Umekita side: track 21 for the airport, track 24 for Shin-Osaka and Kyoto. The nearest gate is the West Gate. These platforms opened in March 2023, so older guides miss them.
Going to Kansai Airport by bus? Walk to Hankyu Sanbangai, the bus terminal under the Hankyu buildings. The limousine takes about 60 minutes to Terminal 1 and costs ¥1,800 (child ¥900), with no reservation.
Going to Hotel Granvia Osaka? Leave JR by the Central Gate and turn right: the hotel is part of the station building.
Going to Grand Front Osaka or Hotel Hankyu RESPIRE? Use the 3rd-floor bridge gate and walk north over the deck: RESPIRE says 3 minutes.
Going to Kyoto or Kobe on Hankyu? Head for the Hankyu Department Store side, follow the 1st-floor passage, then ride up to the 3rd-floor Hankyu gates.
Going to Namba or Shin-Osaka by subway? Same direction, towards the Hankyu Department Store, then take the escalator down to Midosuji Line Umeda.
Going to Hilton Osaka or Herbis Osaka? They are across the road on the south side; the Osaka Convention and Tourism Bureau puts the Hilton 2 minutes from JR Osaka.
Hankyu's maroon trains leave from their own terminal at Osaka-umeda, a short walk from JR.
Where to stay near Osaka Station: one pick per traveller
Arriving on the HARUKA
Osaka Station Hotel
Straight off the airport train
A luxury hotel (Marriott's Autograph Collection) directly connected to the West Gate, the gate closest to the underground HARUKA platforms. From the platform you stay inside the gates and follow the walkway towards the West Gate. Downside: you pay for that convenience.
Step off the HARUKA and into the lobby →
Early trains most mornings
Hotel Granvia Osaka
On top of the platforms
Out of the Central Gate and turn right. On our December dates a Comfort Single cost ¥49,243 for three nights, about ¥16,400 a night. Downside: worth it only if you really catch early trains on most days.
Be on the platform five minutes after breakfast →
Families
Hotel Hankyu RESPIRE
The airport bus stops at the tower
Inside Yodobashi Umeda Tower, 3 minutes from the JR 3rd-floor bridge gate. It has triple and quad rooms and luggage storage, and some limousine buses from Kansai Airport stop at the building. Downside: breakfast costs extra. More in our Osaka hotels by budget.
Roll the kids from the bus to the room →
Budget, light bags
Nakazakicho
Twelve minutes' walk, lower prices
Besides the station towers, consider Nakazakicho, east of Umeda: old houses turned into cafés, and a well-rated double was ¥24,920 for three nights against ¥34,394 at Hotel Monterey Osaka by the station. Downside: an 800 m walk with your bags. The numbers are in Nakazakicho vs Umeda.
Trade the towers for a café street →
Prices: Booking.com, 1 adult, Mon 14 to Thu 17 December 2026, taxes included, checked 23 November 2026. They change daily.
Eat around Osaka Station: the famous bite and the local one
What most visitors go for: the ikayaki (pressed squid pancake) from the Snack Park on B1 of the Hanshin Umeda Main Store. It is the store's speciality, sold by the thousand every day, and the line moves fast. It is a quick stand-up snack, not a meal.
Dig a little deeper: under the JR tracks, the old Shin-Umeda Shokudogai food alley is where office workers eat. On its ground floor, Kushikatsu Matsuba Sohonten has served deep-fried skewers standing-only for about 70 years. JTB's GLTJP says to start with the beef; most skewers cost in the ¥100s and none is over ¥300. The rules: never dip twice in the shared sauce (use the free cabbage to scoop more), and no credit cards. It opens weekdays 14:00 to 22:00 and weekends 11:00 to 21:30, and closes on Mondays.
Osaka Station City from above: the hub is big, so choose your side before you book.
📅 Good to know before you book
Landing late at Kansai Airport? The limousine to Osaka Station runs a late-night bus: the last one leaves Terminal 1 at 0:15 and takes cashless payment only (timetable checked 24 November 2026). A hotel on the bus side of the station saves the walk at 1 a.m.
Hotel names can mislead: "Umeda" in a hotel name can mean anywhere from Osaka Station to Nakazakicho or Dojima. Check the walking time to the gate you'll use before you book.
Free cancellation: many listings around the station offer it on Booking.com (check each one), so you can hold a room while you compare the other side.
Compare both sides of the station on your dates →
Nearby, if you have more time
Umeda Sky Building Kuchu Teien Observatory: the rooftop ring west of the station; adults ¥2,000, open 9:30 to 22:30 (last entry 22:00).
Tenma and Tenjinbashisuji: one stop on the Loop Line, Osaka's long covered shopping street and its standing bars. See Tenma: where Osaka locals eat.
Out late? Our Osaka for night owls compares the areas that stay up.
The Umeda Sky Building: the rooftop ring is open until 22:30.
One more thing: let the airport bus do the station for you
Coming in from Kansai Airport with big suitcases, the limousine bus beats the train for one reason: it ends at the street, not deep inside the station. Besides Hankyu Sanbangai, buses from the airport stop at Herbis Osaka (for the Hilton side and Osaka Station Hotel, 2 minutes away), and some also stop at Hotel Hankyu RESPIRE in Yodobashi Umeda Tower and at Candeo Hotels Osaka The Tower in Dojima. Check which stops your bus makes on the timetable and pick your hotel to match. No escalators, no gates.
Source: Kansai Airport Transportation Enterprise timetable for Osaka Sta. (Umeda); Osaka Station Hotel access page. Checked 24 November 2026.

## Where Sapporo Locals Eat: Markets, Soup Curry and Ramen
URL: https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-locals-eat
City: Hokkaido · Facts checked: 2026-11-24

For a seafood breakfast, we'd go to the Curb Market, next to Sapporo's central wholesale market and about 20 minutes from Odori, rather than the better-known Nijo Market downtown. For soup curry, head to a basement off Odori (Garaku) or ride out to Kotoni, where people actually live. For ramen, do what Susukino does: finish the night with a bowl, in the famous alley or at Keyaki around the corner, open until 2 a.m.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 24 November 2026
Who this food plan suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Food-first travellers with two or three days in Sapporo
Early risers: market stock is best from 8:00 to 11:00
Winter visitors: soup curry and ramen are built for cold nights
Anyone happy to ride the subway two or three stops for a better meal
Think twice
Very tight budgets: market crab and seafood bowls aren't cheap
Late sleepers: the Curb Market is quieter and emptier by the afternoon
Spice-averse eaters: start soup curry at the mildest level
Nijo Market or Curb Market?
A · Curb Market · Our pick
60 shops · 6:00–17:00
Where the city's kitchen is
Next to Sapporo's central wholesale market, Hokkaido's biggest. About 60 stores selling fish, crab, vegetables, fruit and Hokkaido sweets, and about 20 restaurants (open from 7:00), most attached to fish shops, so you can eat what you pick. Tozai Line from Odori to Nijuyonken (about 10 minutes), then 7 minutes on foot.
B · Nijo Market
Downtown · 7:00–18:00
History on your way
Dating from the early Meiji period, with some shops over 100 years old, right by Bus Center-mae Station and a short walk from Odori. Restaurants open 6:00 to 21:00, so it also works for a late breakfast or an early dinner. Both markets are open every day.
C · Both, different days
2+ days
Breakfast at one, lunch at the other
Curb Market for an early seafood breakfast on a free morning, Nijo for a seafood lunch between sights downtown. Neither needs more than an hour or two.
Our verdict: if you can be on the subway by 8:00 one morning, go to the Curb Market. The city's tourism office says stock thins out after the busy 8:00–11:00 window, and the restaurants fill with local workers at lunchtime. Choose Nijo if you only have a spare hour downtown or you're going after 15:00. Nijo's restaurants stay open until 21:00, while the Curb Market closes at 17:00.
How to shop: almost every stall offers tastings, so try a few kinds of salmon roe before you buy. Live crabs can be boiled on the spot or shipped, and heavier crabs have more meat.
Downtown Sapporo: Nijo Market is a short walk from the Tanukikoji arcade.
Soup curry: where Sapporo goes
Soup curry is Sapporo's own dish: a thin, spiced broth with big pieces of Hokkaido vegetables and chicken or pork, served with rice on the side. You choose the spice level, the rice size and a topping or two. Two toppings is plenty.
Garaku (central): in a basement at Minami 2-jo Nishi 2-chome, near Odori. The pork-bone and herb broth simmers for two days, with kelp and bonito added, and the shop closes when it runs out, so go early.
Okushiba Shoten (by Sapporo Station): in the basement of the Hokuren Building, Kita 4-jo Nishi 1-chome. Known for a rich shrimp broth, and the easiest pick with luggage or an early train.
Kotoni (residential): a few stops west of Sapporo Station on JR, or on the Tozai Line. Picante sits under the elevated JR Kotoni Station and cooks each curry in its own small pot. Sapporo Rakkyo, nearby, has a classic chicken, pork and tomato broth that suits first-timers. It closes on the third Wednesday of the month.
Thin broth, big vegetables, rice on the side: the soup curry format.
Ramen beyond the Ramen Alley
Ganso Ramen Yokocho in Susukino is a 42-metre alley lined with 17 miso ramen shops. It's crowded from morning to night, and it's also where Sapporo people end a night of drinking with a bowl. It's worth a look, but the shops around it run on the same late-night habit.
Keyaki: Minami 6-jo Nishi 3-chome, 3 minutes from Susukino Station, open 10:00 to 2:00 (last order 1:45), every day of the year. A good bet when the alley queues are long.
Order like a local: miso is the Sapporo style. Spicy miso and miso with char siu are the alley's most popular orders with overseas visitors.
Sweetcorn, egg and a rich broth: what a cold Sapporo night calls for.
A one-day eating route
7:30 Tozai Line to Nijuyonken and walk to the Curb Market. Seafood bowl at one of the fish-shop restaurants.
9:30 Shop for crab or roe while stock is fresh. Ask about shipping.
12:30 Back downtown. Light lunch, or a look round Nijo Market by Bus Center-mae.
17:30 Early dinner: soup curry at Garaku before the broth runs out.
22:30 Susukino after dark, then a miso ramen to finish, in the alley or at Keyaki.
Morning: crab and roe at the market
Evening: the streets off Susukino
Late: Susukino, then ramen
Where to stay for a food trip
For both markets
Odori / Bus Center-mae
Nijo on foot, Curb Market on one line
Walk to Nijo, and take the Tozai Line straight to Nijuyonken for the Curb Market. Garaku is around the corner. Downside: busy with sightseers all day.
Be first at the market stalls tomorrow →
For late ramen
Susukino
Walk home after the last bowl
The ramen alley and Keyaki are minutes away, and you won't need a taxi at 1 a.m. Downside: lively and loud until late, so ask for a high floor.
Stay where Sapporo's nights end with noodles →
For a local feel
Nishi 18-chome / Nijuyonken
The Curb Market end of the line
Residential streets on the Tozai Line, close to the Curb Market and a few stops from Odori. Downside: far fewer hotels and less going on at night.
Live a few stops from Hokkaido's kitchen →
Choosing a base for a whole first trip? See Sapporo Station vs Odori vs Susukino.
🦀 First time ordering at a Japanese market? Klook lists an English-guided Sapporo market and seafood brunch tour, a 2-hour small-group ramen tour and an evening bar-hopping food walk, so someone can show you how ordering works before you go it alone.Eat your way through Sapporo with a local guide →
📅 Good to know before you book
No closing days at the markets: both the Curb Market and Nijo Market list no regular closing days, so your market morning can go on any day of the trip. Individual shops still set their own hours.
Soup curry sells out: Garaku closes when its broth is gone and other shops close irregularly, so keep a second choice nearby.
Book early for winter weeks: Sapporo's big winter weeks fill hotels near Odori and Susukino first. Most hotels on the big booking sites offer free cancellation, so holding a room costs nothing.
Hold a room near the noodles before winter fills up →
Breakfast the way Sapporo does it
Arinko: a handmade onigiri shop since 1980. The tourism office suggests the "cheese katsuo" rice ball with tonjiru pork and vegetable miso soup. Take it to Odori Park for a picnic.
Sandria: a takeout-only sandwich shop since 1978, open 24 hours with more than 40 kinds. The double egg sandwich is the most popular.
One more thing: a free ride to breakfast, and a bath after
Two Curb Market restaurants, Kita no Ryoba and Kaisen-Shokudo Kitano Gourmet-tei, run a free shuttle from hotels and JR Sapporo Station if you reserve a day ahead, so you don't have to work out the subway at 7 a.m. And if you're still there after lunch, the market has its own neighbourhood bathhouse, Sakae-yu, which opens at 13:00. It's a sento, not a tourist spa, and a warm soak is a very Sapporo way to finish a cold market morning.
Source: Sapporo official tourism site (sapporo.travel), breakfast and market features, checked 24 November 2026.

## First Trip to Kyoto: Kyoto Station, Kawaramachi/Gion or Karasuma?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kyoto-where-to-stay-first-trip
City: Kyoto · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For most first trips we'd stay around Shijo-Karasuma: the subway reaches Kyoto Station in 3 minutes (¥220), Kawaramachi and Nishiki Market are one stop or a short walk away, and Hankyu runs to Arashiyama in about 27 minutes. Choose Kyoto Station if you'll do JR day trips or arrive late with luggage. Choose Kawaramachi/Gion if evening walks in old Kyoto are the reason you came.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 23 November 2026
Before you choose: buses or trains?
A city bus is a flat ¥230, but Kyoto's own tourism site warns that routes like the 205 (to Kinkaku-ji) and 206 (towards Kiyomizu-dera) get very crowded in season, and it recommends trains and the subway. So we'd base yourself near the lines you'll actually use. A Subway 1-Day Pass is ¥800; the Subway & Bus 1-Day Pass is ¥1,100 and covers only the calendar day you start it, not 24 hours.
Rail-first suits
Short stays with a fixed list of sights
Early starts before the crowds
Travellers with luggage or kids
Bus-first only if
You travel outside cherry blossom and autumn leaf season
Your hotel is on a direct route to where you're going
You don't mind standing
Kyoto's city buses: a flat fare, but crowded on the big sightseeing routes.
Option A · Kyoto Station
Day trips, late arrivals, big bags
Inari in 6 min
JR from here reaches Fushimi Inari (Inari Station) in 6 minutes for ¥150 and Saga-Arashiyama in 17 minutes for ¥240. The tourism office notes plenty of lockers and luggage services, and that large hotels here are easier to find in peak season. Downside: old Kyoto is a ride away every evening. For an early bowl, Honke Daiichi Asahi, about 5 minutes' walk away, has served soy-sauce ramen since 1947, opens at 6:00 (closed Thursdays), and people queue before it opens.
Kyoto Station's huge atrium: the JR lines for Inari and Arashiyama leave from here.
Option B · Shijo-Karasuma
Two train lines, both directions
Our pick
Karasuma is Kyoto's business district, which is exactly why it works as a base: the Karasuma subway line north–south and the Hankyu line east–west cross here. Kyoto Station is 3 minutes away, Kawaramachi one Hankyu stop, and Arashiyama about 27 minutes with a change at Katsura (¥240). Downside: the streets are office blocks rather than wooden houses, so the atmosphere is a short walk east.
Nishiki Market runs between Shijo-Karasuma and Kawaramachi, an easy walk from either base.
Option C · Kawaramachi / Gion
Walk out at dusk into old Kyoto
Inari in 8 min
From Shijo-Kawaramachi you can walk to Yasaka-jinja and Gion, and Nishiki Market is next door. Keihan trains from Gion-Shijo reach Fushimi-Inari in 8 minutes (¥240). From Kyoto Station it's 13 minutes (¥390, subway then Hankyu), or a ¥230 bus if it isn't full. Downside: the tourism office describes the lodging here as long-standing ryokan and luxury hotels, so there are fewer budget rooms.
Gion after dark, when the day-trippers have gone home.
Nishiki tips: the market association says many shops close on Wednesdays, and asks visitors to eat in front of the shop rather than while walking.
Our verdict
We suggest: Shijo-Karasuma for a 3–4 night first trip. Two rail lines, Kyoto Station in 3 minutes and Kawaramachi one stop away. It changes if most days are JR day trips (Nara, Osaka, Himeji) or you arrive late: then sleep at Kyoto Station. And if this is a special-occasion trip and evenings in old Kyoto matter more than transport, splurge on Gion. Arashiyama is the tourism office's pick for an early morning with fewer people, but as a base for one night, not a first trip.

📅 Good to know before you book
New hotel tax since 1 March 2026, per person per night: ¥400 for rooms at ¥6,000–19,999 per person, ¥1,000 at ¥20,000–49,999, ¥4,000 at ¥50,000–99,999 and ¥10,000 from ¥100,000. Check whether a price includes it.
Peak seasons: the tourism office advises booking as early as possible for cherry blossom, autumn leaves and the Gion Matsuri in July; budget rooms go first. Many listings offer free cancellation, so an early booking can stay flexible.
Lock in a flexible room for Kyoto's cherry blossom weeks →
Nearby, if you have more time
Kamo River: the tourism office suggests a morning walk on the banks near Shijo-Kawaramachi.
Osaka: if you're splitting the trip, see where to stay in Osaka; Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome even has through Hankyu trains to Kyoto (Tenma guide).
The Kamo River banks: an easy morning walk from the Shijo area.
One more thing: breakfast at 7 in a 1940 coffee house
Staying in Karasuma? Walk about 10 minutes from Karasuma-Oike Station to Inoda Coffee's main shop on Sakaimachi-dori, open every day from 7:00. It has been serving its Arabian Pearl blend since it opened in 1940, traditionally served with milk and sugar (black if you ask), in a machiya townhouse. Cards are accepted.
Source: GOOD LUCK TRIP verified listing for Inoda Coffee (supervised by the shop, updated 20 April 2026), checked 23 November 2026.

## First Trip to Sapporo: Sapporo Station, Odori or Susukino?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/sapporo-where-to-stay-first-trip
City: Hokkaido · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For most first trips we'd stay in Odori: it sits in the middle, about 10 minutes underground from Sapporo Station and one subway stop from Susukino, next to Odori Park and Nijo Market. Pick Sapporo Station if you have early trains, day trips or big luggage (the airport train is 33 minutes at the fastest). Pick Susukino if dinner and a late drink are the point of the trip.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 23 November 2026
The short version
Easy wins
The centre is small: Sapporo Station to Susukino is about 1.5 km
You can do it all underground in a blizzard
Airport trains need no reservation, and Suica works
Watch out for
JR Sapporo and the subway's Sapporo Station are about 7 minutes apart on foot
Ice from mid-December to February
Snow Festival week (4–11 Feb 2027): book early
Odori Park and the TV Tower sit right in the middle of the compact centre.
Option A · Sapporo Station
Early trains and big bags
33 min to the airport
JR Rapid Airport trains run six an hour between 9:00 and 16:00, ¥1,230, no reservation needed for most seats (car 4 is reserved). Sleeping by JR Sapporo means no transfer with luggage, and it's the base for day trips by train, such as Otaru. Downside: evenings are calmer here, and the jingisukan grills and bars are 1.5 km south in Susukino. For breakfast, Cafe Yoshimi near the station opens at 7:30, with a morning toast set and drink for ¥580.
Snowy pavements in winter: one more reason to sleep close to your train.
Option B · Odori
The middle of everything
Our pick
Chi-Ka-Ho, the underground walkway under Ekimae-dori, links Sapporo Station and Odori in about 520 m, roughly 10 minutes, and is open 5:45 to 24:30. Odori Park runs about 1.5 km east to west, with the TV Tower at its east end. Nijo Market serves seafood bowls from about 7:00, and the Tozai Line takes you four stops to the Curb Market. Downside: the airport train still means a short subway ride or that underground walk with your bags.
Sapporo in deep winter: beautiful, and slippery. The underground walkways are why Odori works so well.
Option C · Susukino
Dinner, then a short walk home
3 min by subway
Sapporo's night district. From the airport it's about 58 minutes and ¥1,440 with one change to the Namboku Line. Jingisukan (grilled mutton) is the dinner to have here: Daruma's main branch, about 3 minutes from Susukino Station, is open every day from 17:00 to 5:00 and jingisukan is ¥1,280. Downside: it's one of Japan's best-known entertainment districts and busy until late, so light sleepers should ask for a high floor or stay a few blocks away.
Snow, neon and the tram: Sapporo after dark.
Our verdict
We suggest: Odori for a 3–4 night first trip; you'll walk to almost everything, underground when it snows. Switch to Sapporo Station if you leave on early trains or have day trips most days. Switch to Susukino if you're here for food and nights out, and you're fine with some street noise. In winter, the closer you are to a station entrance, the less ice you walk on.

Central Sapporo at dusk: the three bases are all within this view.
📅 Good to know before you book
Sapporo Snow Festival, 4–11 Feb 2027: the sculptures stand in Odori Park and along Susukino's main street (Minami 4 to 7-jo), so those two areas fill first. Many listings offer free cancellation; check the policy before you pay.
Winter walking: Sapporo's tourism office says pavements freeze from mid-December to February. Pack boots with grip; convenience stores sell anti-slip spikes.
Sleep a short walk from the snow sculptures →
Nearby, if you have more time
Curb Market: Sapporo's central wholesale market, four stops from Odori on the Tozai Line, for a seafood breakfast.
Otaru: some Rapid Airport trains run straight through Sapporo to Otaru, about 73 minutes from the airport at the fastest.
One more thing: rice balls at 3 a.m.
Meidai Nigirimeshi, in a corner of Susukino Market, makes onigiri by hand and never closes. Order the soy-sauce style with cod roe and butter, the one Sapporo's tourism office recommends, with a bowl of tonjiru pork soup. It works after a late night out, and just as well before an early train.
Source: Sapporo official tourism site, early breakfast feature, checked 23 November 2026.

## Hakone Freepass for a Ryokan Night: Worth It or Not?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/hakone-freepass-ryokan-one-night
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If your night in Hakone is really about the ryokan, skip the Freepass: Shinjuku to Gora and back, plus a short hop to the Open-Air Museum, costs ¥3,662 in single fares against ¥7,100 for the pass. Buy it the moment the ropeway and the Lake Ashi boat are in your two days: that loop costs ¥8,272 in singles, so the pass saves about ¥1,170 and gets you into Gora Park free. Arriving by Shinkansen? Buy the cheaper Odawara version, or none at all.
About a 4-minute read · fares for Wed 16 Dec 2026, adult IC fares · facts checked 23 November 2026
Who the pass suits, and who it doesn't
Buy the Freepass
You'll ride the ropeway and the pirate ship on day two
You like hopping on and off without buying tickets each time
You want Hakone Gora Park (free with the pass) and other discounts
Pay as you go
Ryokan, onsen, dinner, maybe one museum: that's the trip
Your inn is in Hakone-Yumoto and you won't go uphill
You continue to Kyoto from Odawara (the Shinjuku pass includes a return ride you won't use)
Answer A · Full sightseeing loop
Ropeway and boat in the plan? The pass wins
¥8,272 vs ¥7,100
The classic loop from Shinjuku with a night in Gora, in single IC fares: Odakyu to Gora ¥1,671, cable car to Sounzan ¥430, ropeway to Togendai ¥2,000, boat to Moto-Hakone ¥1,700, bus down to Hakone-Yumoto ¥1,210, Odakyu back to Shinjuku ¥1,261. Total ¥8,272. The 2-day Freepass from Shinjuku is ¥7,100 and covers all of it, so you save about ¥1,170 before any discounts.
Single fares
¥8,272
Six rides, one loop
Ropeway ¥2,000 and boat ¥1,700 are the big ones.
Freepass, Shinjuku
¥7,100
2 days, unlimited in the area
Romancecar fee (¥1,200 each way) is extra either way.
Answer B · Ryokan-focused stay
Inn, bath, one short outing: skip it
¥3,662 vs ¥7,100
Shinjuku to Gora and back is ¥1,671 each way. Add a two-minute ride to Chokoku-no-Mori for the Open-Air Museum and back (¥160 each way) and you're at ¥3,662: about ¥3,400 less than the pass. If your inn is in Hakone-Yumoto, where the Romancecar terminates, it's just ¥1,261 each way. Tap an IC card (Suica, PASMO) and you don't need to buy a single ticket.
Hakone-Yumoto, where the Romancecar ends. Stay here and you may not need a pass at all.
Answer C · Mixed route via Odawara
Shinkansen in, Kyoto next? Start at Odawara
¥6,000 pass
The Shinjuku Freepass includes one Odakyu round trip to Odawara. If you arrive by Shinkansen or carry on to Kyoto from Odawara, that part is wasted: buy the Odawara version (¥6,000). The same loop from Odawara and back costs ¥6,470 in singles, so the pass saves only about ¥470. A ryokan night in Gora with one short ride is about ¥1,860 in singles. Extra charges to remember: the Romancecar fee, and anything outside the pass area (the Shinkansen, Izu-Hakone buses).
In between: the Hakone Tozan Train 1-Day Pass (¥1,580) covers Odawara–Gora trains for one day and gets you into Gora Park free. It pays off if you hop off at two or three stations on the way up.
Our verdict
We suggest: no pass for a ryokan-first night. Tap your IC card and spend the difference on dinner. The answer changes the moment you add both the ropeway and the boat: then buy the 2-day Freepass from Shinjuku (¥7,100), or from Odawara (¥6,000) if the Shinkansen is part of your route. In December 2026 the ropeway's Owakudani–Sounzan section runs as a replacement bus from 7 to 24 Dec (Freepass valid), so allow extra time on that day.
Eat like a local in Gora
Tamura Ginkatsutei, two minutes from Gora Station, created Gora's signature dish in 1995: tofu katsuni, pressed tofu filled with minced pork, fried, then simmered with egg in a clay pot. Lunch runs to a 14:30 last order, dinner 17:00–19:00 last order. It's closed on Wednesdays and Tuesday evenings, and takes cards. Lunch is up to about ¥2,000. Room-only night in Yumoto instead? Our Hakone base guide has a late-dinner spot by the station.
Where to stay for a ryokan night

Hakone-Yumoto

📅 Good to know before you book
Ropeway works: Owakudani–Sounzan runs as a bus from 7 to 24 Dec 2026; Togendai–Ubako–Owakudani from 12 Jan to 26 Feb 2027. Buses run about every 15 minutes and can be crowded.
Freepass refunds: if a service stops for weather, Odakyu refunds unused parts at your last station. Keep the pass until the end; it's collected there.
Buying ahead: stations sell the pass from a month before; vending machines only sell same-day passes. Romancecar seats need their own ticket.
Have your Hakone pass ready before you reach Shinjuku →
The Hakone Tozan Bus brings you back down from the lake; ¥1,210 without a pass.
Nearby, if you have more time
Owakudani: the steaming volcanic valley at the top of the ropeway. On the replacement-bus days, Odakyu suggests reaching it on the section that is running.
Hakone Open-Air Museum: two minutes from Chokoku-no-Mori, one stop below Gora. See our ryokan dinner timing guide.
One more thing: one Gora Park ticket, two visits
Hakone Gora Park, between Koen-shimo and Koen-kami on the cable car, lets you back in the same day and the next day on one ticket (¥650, or free with the Freepass or the Tozan Train 1-Day Pass). Staying in Gora, walk in before the 16:30 last entry on arrival day, then go back at 9:00 the next morning, when the park opens, before you check out.
Source: Hakone Gora Park official site (hours, fees, re-entry), checked 23 November 2026.

## One Car-Free Night in Hakone: Yumoto, Gora or Lake Ashi?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/hakone-base-yumoto-gora-lake-ashi
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For one car-free night we suggest Hakone-Yumoto if you arrive after about 17:00 or leave early: the Romancecar ends there, our sample hotel is 150 m from the platform (¥16,800 for two) and dinner runs to a 21:30 last order. Choose Gora (¥18,540 with breakfast, 100 m from the station) if your day is the Open-Air Museum or the ropeway side. Choose Lake Ashi (¥18,225 with breakfast and a lake view) only if you'll be there by mid-afternoon: the last weekday bus up from Yumoto is 20:48 and lakeside kitchens close early.
Booking.com, Hakone Navi timetables, Odakyu Hakone and Jorudan · sample night Wed 16–Thu 17 Dec 2026, 2 adults · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Hakone-Yumoto
Off the train and into the room in minutes
¥16,800 · 150 m
Arrival with luggage: Yumoto is where the Romancecar from Shinjuku terminates, so there is no change with bags. Yumoto Station Hotel MIRAHAKONE is 150 m from the station; for Wed 16 Dec it showed an economy double with a private shower at ¥16,800 room only (a 30% deal on ¥24,000), and check-in runs until 23:30.
Dinner: this is the only base where a late arrival still has choice on foot. Kinosuke, 2 minutes from the station, serves charcoal-grilled dishes 17:30–22:00, last orders 21:30, closed Mondays. Next morning: the Hakone Tozan train climbs to Gora in about 36 minutes, and buses to Moto-Hakone on Lake Ashi take about 32 minutes from stop 2. The cost of the convenience is that every sight is uphill from here.
Room only, 2 adults

21:30
Kinosuke, 2 min

Suits: evening arrivals, big suitcases, an early train back. Not for: waking up in the mountains or by the lake.
Answer B · Gora
Halfway up, next to the museum and the cable car
¥18,540 with breakfast
Access to what you came for: the Hakone Open-Air Museum is one stop down the line (2 minutes by train, then a 2-minute walk), and the cable car to Sounzan and the ropeway to Owakudani start in Gora. Note the works: Odakyu Hakone replaces the Owakudani–Sounzan ropeway section with buses from 7 to 24 December 2026 (about every 15 minutes), and the Togendai–Owakudani section from 12 January to 26 February 2027.
The final walk: pick a hotel near the station, because Gora is built on a slope. Sundance Resort Hakone Gora is 100 m from Gora Station; on 16 Dec a Japanese-style room with breakfast (shared bathroom) was ¥18,540 + ¥300 tax at Booking's members-only price, or ¥32,040 with dinner too. Check-in runs 15:00–20:00 and the hotel wants your arrival time. Further up the hill, ryokan such as Kiritani Hakoneso send a car if you phone from the station.

Answer C · Lake Ashi
The lake in the morning, if you arrive early
¥18,225 · lake view
The value: you wake up where day-trippers end their loop. RoheN ASHINOKO, 300 m from Moto-Hakone, showed a lake-view double with a private bathroom and breakfast for ¥18,225 on 16 Dec (members-only price; standard ¥22,500), almost the Gora price with the lake outside. Hakone Shrine, with its torii in the water, is about a 10-minute walk from the Hakone-jinja-iriguchi bus stop.
The catch is the evening. Weekday buses from Hakone-Yumoto (stop 2) after 17:00 leave at 17:28, 17:58, 18:28, 18:58, 19:48 and a last 20:48, which reaches Moto-Hakone-ko at 21:20 (¥1,210). Food closes earlier: La Terrazza Ashinoko takes last orders at 19:00 (closed 2nd and 4th Tuesdays), and most lakeside lunch places shut between 16:00 and 18:00. Arriving after dark, book a hotel with its own restaurant (RoheN's listing has one) or eat in Yumoto first.
