Our verdict
We suggest: Hakone-Yumoto for most one-night, car-free trips with luggage. It had the lowest room price of our three on this date (room only), steps from the Romancecar, and the only base with dinner on foot until 21:30. Switch to Gora if your day is built around the Open-Air Museum or the ropeway and you'll check in by about 18:00. Switch to Lake Ashi only if you can be there by mid-afternoon: after about 19:00 the lake has no dinner and only two buses left. In December 2026 the ropeway's upper section runs as a bus from 7 to 24 Dec, so allow extra time if you cross from Gora to the lake.

One more thing: breakfast with your feet in the onsen
Staying by the lake? Bakery & Table Hakone at Moto-Hakone opens at 9:00 every day, and its terrace has a foot bath fed by Lake Ashi's hot spring. Buy bread downstairs, sit on the edge with your feet in the warm water and look across the lake; the upstairs café also looks over Lake Ashi (last orders 16:30). Hakone Navi suggests its curry doughnut made with rice flour.

## Hakone Ryokan With Dinner: What Time Should You Leave Tokyo?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/hakone-ryokan-dinner-leave-tokyo
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For a ryokan in Gora whose check-in closes at 18:00, we suggest the 15:00 Romancecar from Shinjuku: it reaches Gora at 17:03 with one change and leaves about an hour to spare. Want a stop first? Take the 10:00 Romancecar, spend the afternoon at the Hakone Open-Air Museum and leave it by 16:50. Can't leave Tokyo until evening? Skip the dinner plan: book a room-only hotel by Hakone-Yumoto Station and eat at a grill 2 minutes away, last orders 21:30.
Booking.com, Jalan, Jorudan timetables, the museum and Hakone Navi · sample day Wed 16 Dec 2026, 2 adults · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Go straight there
The 15:00 Romancecar, and the ryokan collects you
Gora 17:03 · ¥2,871
Our sample ryokan is Ryokan Kiritani Hakoneso in Gora: a Japanese-style room with breakfast and dinner was ¥34,000 for two (+¥300 tax) on Wed 16 Dec on Booking.com, and its check-in runs 15:30–18:00. Working back from 18:00 on that date: the 15:00 Romancecar Hakone 13 leaves Shinjuku, reaches Hakone-Yumoto at 16:25, and the 16:27 Hakone Tozan train climbs to Gora by 17:03. Total ¥2,871 by IC card, including the ¥1,200 seat.
The last stretch is where luggage hurts: the ryokan is about 850 m from Gora Station on Booking's map. Its Jalan listing gives two easier ways: call from Gora Station after 15:30 and they pick you up in about 5 minutes, or ride the cable car up to Koen-kami station and walk about 5 minutes. The fallback if you miss the 15:00 is the 15:21 rapid express with two changes (Gora 17:48, ¥1,671): it gets you there, but with 12 minutes to spare and no seat reservation.

Answer B · Add one stop
The Open-Air Museum, one stop before Gora
Leave the museum by 16:50
The stop that fits best is the Hakone Open-Air Museum: it is a 2-minute walk from Chokoku-no-Mori Station, one stop before Gora, so the detour costs you no extra transport. Take the 10:00 Romancecar Hakone 3 (Yumoto 11:27, Chokoku-no-Mori 12:16). The museum opens 9:00–17:00 every day (last entry 16:30); adults pay ¥2,000 at the door or ¥1,800 online. Free lockers (a ¥100 coin you get back) are at the entrance; for a big case, ask the museum or use the paid lockers at the station.
Trains from Chokoku-no-Mori to Gora on our sample date: 16:31, 16:47, 17:01, then nothing until 17:31. The firm rule: leave the museum by 16:50 for the 17:01, which reaches Gora at 17:03 and gives you the same hour of margin as Answer A. The 17:31 still works on paper, but only if the pickup is waiting.

Answer C · Leave Tokyo late
Room only by Yumoto Station, dinner on foot
¥16,800 + dinner by 21:30
If work or sightseeing keeps you in Tokyo until evening, a dinner-included ryokan is the wrong booking: you'd pay for a meal you can't reach. Book room-only next to Hakone-Yumoto Station instead. Yumoto Station Hotel MIRAHAKONE, 150 m from the station, showed an economy double with a private shower at ¥16,800 for 16 Dec (a 30% deal on a listed ¥24,000), and check-in runs until 23:30.
The 18:00 Homeway 5 from Shinjuku runs straight to Hakone-Yumoto by 19:40 (¥2,461 by IC card). Kinosuke, about 2 minutes from the station, grills local fish and Sagami meat over charcoal, with dinner 17:30–22:00 and last orders at 21:30; it closes on Mondays (Hakone Navi). Even the 19:00 departure from Shinjuku (Yumoto 20:38, one change) leaves time to order.

Our verdict
We suggest: for a Gora ryokan with an 18:00 check-in, be on the 15:00 Romancecar from Shinjuku, and call for the pickup from Gora Station. With a free morning, take the 10:00 instead and add the Open-Air Museum, leaving by 16:50. The answer changes if you can't leave Tokyo before about 18:00: then don't pay for a ryokan dinner, book room-only by Hakone-Yumoto Station and eat by 21:30 (not on a Monday). Your own ryokan's deadline may differ, so check it on the booking and move these times by the same amount.

One more thing: an onsen for room-only nights
Room-only hotels by the station rarely have a hot-spring bath. Hakone Yuryo, a day-onsen with open-air baths and private bath rooms, is a free shuttle ride of about 3 minutes from Hakone-Yumoto Station. The catch for late arrivals: on weekdays it closes at 20:00, with last entry at 19:00 (weekends and holidays 21:00, last entry 20:00), so it fits a train that reaches Yumoto by about 18:30, not the 19:40. Weekday adult entry is about ¥1,700–1,800.

## Cloudy Fuji Forecast: Move the Kawaguchiko Trip, Go Anyway or Keep the Night?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kawaguchiko-cloudy-fuji-forecast
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If you have a spare day and refundable bookings, we suggest moving the trip: decide the evening before, using the forecast and Yamanashi's official live Fuji cameras. An unused JR reserved ticket can be changed once for free before departure, and the lakeside hotel we checked cancels free until the day before. No spare day? Go anyway with a plan that doesn't need the mountain: the Itchiku Kubota Art Museum (¥1,500) and a bowl of hoto (¥1,210). Already booked a night? Keep it: you get the next morning as a second chance.
Yamanashi Tourism Organization, JR East, kosokubus.com, Booking.com, the museum and Yamanashi's tourism site · sample night Wed 16 Dec 2026 · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Flexible date
Move it, but only if the bookings let you
Decide the evening before
Look at two things the evening before: the weather forecast and the Fujisan Watcher page of the Yamanashi Tourism Organization, which streams live cameras pointed at Fuji from Lake Kawaguchiko, Fujiyoshida, Lake Shojiko, Lake Yamanakako and more. The forecast tells you about tomorrow; the cameras show you what cloud the mountain is wearing right now.
Then check what each booking lets you do. JR tickets: JR East lets you change an unused ticket once, free, and a reserved seat only before the train leaves. Highway bus: on kosokubus.com you can't move a booking to a new date; you cancel (day buses until 17:00 the day before) and book again, and the fee depends on the bus company. Hotel: on Booking.com, Toyoko Inn Fuji Kawaguchiko Ohashi showed a twin with breakfast for Wed 16 Dec at ¥14,910 with free cancellation before 15 Dec, while its ¥13,561 offer was prepaid with no changes. When Fuji is the reason for the trip, the flexible rate is the one to book.

JR East rules.
Hotel, sample night 16 Dec

¥14,910 twin, breakfast.
Suits: trips with two or more days in Tokyo and refundable tickets. Not for: a prepaid non-refundable night, or your last free day.
Answer B · Keep the day trip
Go anyway: kimono art, a garden and hoto
≈¥4,200 at the lake
The bus from Shinjuku takes about 100 minutes to Kawaguchiko Station, per the museum's access page. From there, the Red Line sightseeing bus reaches the Itchiku Kubota Art Museum in about 20 minutes. It shows Kubota's dyed kimono landscapes in buildings set in a garden of lava stone and running water, so it is worth the trip on a grey day. December to March it opens 10:00–16:30 (last entry 16:00), adults ¥1,500, and its calendar shows no closed day in December 2026.
For lunch, Hoto Fudo's main store on the north shore serves the local thick noodles in miso broth, 11:00–19:00 every day or until the noodles run out, with Fudo hoto at ¥1,210 (Yamanashi's official tourism site; about 15 minutes by bus from the station). The Mt. Fuji North Area 1Day Pass (¥1,500, in the Jorudan app) covers the Red, Green and Blue sightseeing lines; museum, hoto and pass come to about ¥4,200 per person, plus the trip from Tokyo. If the cloud lifts in the afternoon, you are already on the north shore, the side that faces Fuji.

Answer C · Keep the overnight
Keep the night: two chances instead of one
2-day bus pass ¥2,000
A night at the lake turns one roll of the dice into two: this afternoon and tomorrow morning. Do Answer B on day one, then check the live cameras when you wake up. If Fuji is out, go to the lakeshore before checkout. If it isn't, you lose nothing: the hotel and the hoto were part of the plan anyway.
Two small savings make the second chance cheap. The Fujikyu bus 2DAYPASS is ¥2,000, only ¥500 more than the one-day pass, and covers the same three sightseeing lines both days. And a hotel with breakfast, like the ¥14,910 twin above, means you can be out at first light without hunting for food. If the forecast says cloud for both days, book a room with an onsen bath, so the evening is worth it even if you never see the mountain.

Our verdict
We suggest: if you have a spare day and refundable bookings, move the trip; decide the evening before with the forecast and the live cameras, then use your one free JR change. If you have no other day, go anyway and plan the museum and hoto, which don't need the mountain. If you already have a night booked at the lake, keep it: the next morning is a second chance and the 2-day bus pass costs only ¥500 more. The answer changes when the live cameras show Fuji clear on the morning you travel: then go straight to the north shore before the cloud builds.

One more thing: matcha by the waterfall
Inside the Itchiku Kubota Art Museum, the tea room Itchiku-an serves matcha with a seasonal sweet while you look out at the "Ryumon" waterfall in the garden. The room has a floor of Ryukyu limestone and walls of Okinawan plaster, with pieces Kubota collected in India, Africa and Southeast Asia. The garden, built by Kyoto garden designer Yasuo Kitayama from Fuji lava, limestone, plants and spring water, gives you something to look at on a day when the mountain doesn't.
Source: Itchiku Kubota Art Museum, tea room and garden pages (itchiku-museum.com), checked 23 November 2026.

## Lake Kawaguchi by Bike in Half a Day: How Far Can You Ride?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/lake-kawaguchi-half-day-cycling
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Half a day is enough for one stretch of shore and lunch, not the whole lake (about 20 km around). If your train back is the 14:58 Fuji Excursion, we suggest a short ride from the station to the Kawaguchiko Ohashi Bridge and back, then lunch. If you are on the 16:48, ride the north shore to Oishi Park and eat there. If it is windy, wet or your deadline is tight, the Red Line bus reaches Oishi Park in 27 minutes, every 15 minutes.
Q-BIKE (Fujikyu Railway), Fujikyu Bus, Fujikyu Railway, Yamanashi Tourism Organization · December 2026 weekday times · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Short ride
Station to the bridge and back, then lunch
About 2 hours · ¥2,200
Q-BIKE is Fujikyu Railway's bike share. In the Kawaguchiko area it costs ¥1,100 per 60 minutes, paid in its app by credit card (you need a phone that can receive SMS), so two hours is ¥2,200. Ride from the station to the Kawaguchiko Ohashi Bridge and Ubuyagasaki at its north end, about 1.6 km away in a straight line. The town's tourism association lists both as Fuji viewpoints, and the bridge has a footpath where you can stop.
Set the turnaround by the train, not by the view. For the 14:58 Fuji Excursion, we would be back at a station-area port by about 13:00, then eat. Kosaku's Kawaguchi-ko branch, about 1.2 km from the station, is open 11:00–20:00 (last order 19:30) and takes cards, per Tabelog. Return the bike in the Kawaguchiko area: Q-BIKE charges for any bike left in another area until it is collected.
Q-BIKE, per hour
¥1,100
Capped at ¥3,300 a day
App + credit card.
Station to Ubuyagasaki
1.6 km
Straight line
Bridge footpath for photos.
Suits: a 14:08 or 14:58 train, first-time riders, a slow lunch. Not for: anyone without a credit card and an SMS-capable phone (use the station day pass instead).
Answer B · Longer ride
North shore to Oishi Park, lunch on the way
About 3.4 km each way · ¥3,300 max
Oishi Park is on the north shore, about 3.4 km from the station in a straight line (further by road around the east shore). The tourism association calls the north shore the side where Fuji's ridge shows all the way down. For lunch, Hoto Fudo's north main store at Kawaguchi 707 opens 11:00–19:00 (or until the noodles run out), every day, per Yamanashi's tourism site, with its hoto at ¥1,210.
Hours decide this one. The app is capped at ¥3,300 a day; the paper ¥4,400 day pass from the station baggage storage starts at 10:00 and the bike must be back by 17:00. On the 8:30 Fuji Excursion from Shinjuku you arrive at 10:26, so you are riding by about 10:45. That fits the 16:48 train comfortably. For the 14:58, the ride, lunch and the way back become a race, so take Answer A. Fun Japan suggests an electric-assist bike if hills or distance worry you.

Suits: confident riders on the 16:48 or 17:41 train, clear calm days. Not for: a 14:08 or 14:58 train, or a cold, windy December afternoon.
Answer C · Skip the bike
Red Line bus to the north shore, then walk
¥1,500 day pass · 27 min
Fujikyu's Red Line sightseeing bus leaves Kawaguchiko Station every 15 minutes from 9:00. It reaches the Music and Forest Museum stop in 19 minutes and Oishi Park in 27. The tourism association recommends the brick promenade between Kawaguchiko Circle Hall and the Museum of Art, where Fuji is in view the whole way; that is a walk, not a ride. A 1-Day Pass is ¥1,500.
The bus also removes the deadline stress. Buses back from Oishi Park leave every 15 minutes and take 27 minutes: the 14:12 reaches the station at 14:39, in time for the 14:58 train. Lunch at Hoto Fudo's north store fits on the way, near the Music and Forest Museum area. Choose this when the wind is up, the road is wet or you have only three hours.

Suits: windy or rainy days, families, a tight train. Not for: anyone who came specifically to ride.
Our verdict
We suggest: pick the plan by your train home. On the 14:58, ride to the Kawaguchiko Ohashi Bridge and back on Q-BIKE (about ¥2,200 for two hours) and have lunch near the station. On the 16:48 or later, ride the north shore to Oishi Park and eat at Hoto Fudo's north store. If the wind or rain makes riding unpleasant, or you only have three hours, take the Red Line bus and walk the promenade instead. The answer changes if you have no credit card for the app: then the ¥4,400 station day pass, available from 10:00, is your only bike, and the bus may be the better buy.
See Lake Kawaguchi bike and tour options →Opens Klook. Check the pick-up time against your train.
Coming from Tokyo with luggage? See bus or train with a big suitcase. Staying the night? See what a "Mt. Fuji view" room buys.
One more thing: the "THE Mount Fuji" stop
Four minutes before Oishi Park, the Red Line stops at Nagasaki Park entrance. The town's tourism association calls Nagasaki Park the place for the classic picture, just the lake and the mountain: it sits on a small peninsula, nothing blocks the view, and the far shore is flat with no tall buildings, so you see the longest stretch of Fuji's ridge on both sides.

## Tokyo to Kawaguchiko With a Big Suitcase: Bus or Train?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-to-kawaguchiko-big-suitcase-bus-or-train
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

With one big suitcase each, we suggest the highway bus from Busta Shinjuku: ¥2,000 online, the case rides free in the hold, and buses run from 6:45 to 22:25. Take the Fuji Excursion train (¥4,200) when you must arrive by a set time, such as a weekend, a holiday or a booked tour, because trains do not sit in traffic. If its seats are gone, or you leave after 10:30, the Kaiji to Otsuki plus a Fujikyu local runs all day with one change.
Fujikyu Bus, Fujikyu Railway, JR East · December 2026 weekday timetables · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Highway bus
Busta Shinjuku: the case goes under the bus
¥2,000 · about 1 h 45 min
Fujikyu Bus's rule is simple: large suitcases go free in the luggage compartment, one piece per person. You hand it over at the kerb and never lift it onto a rack. The bus leaves from the 4th floor of Busta Shinjuku, which Fujikyu puts about 2 minutes from JR Shinjuku's New South Gate, with a lift and escalators up. It stops right in front of Kawaguchiko Station. Fares are ¥2,000 booked online on Fujiyama Connect or ¥2,200 at the counter.
The risk is the road. Fujikyu gives the trip as about 1 hour 45 minutes and says times vary with traffic. Book a fixed seat (tickets are not sold on board), and note that changes and refunds stop at the scheduled departure, so a late arrival at Busta loses the ticket. Show the web ticket in your phone's browser; screenshots are not accepted.
Online fare, adult
¥2,000
¥2,200 at the counter
Child half price.
Big suitcases
1 each
Free, in the hold
Last bus 22:25.
Suits: one case per person, weekday trips, anyone staying near Shinjuku's south side. Not for: two big cases each, or a tight arrival time on a busy weekend.
Answer B · Direct train
Fuji Excursion: no traffic, few departures
¥4,200 · 1 h 53 min–2 h
The Fuji Excursion runs straight from Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko with no change. On December 2026 weekdays it leaves at 7:30, 8:30, 9:30 and 10:30, arriving 9:28, 10:26, 11:28 and 12:24, plus a seasonal 11:34 on weekdays until 29 December. The fare is ¥4,200 (¥2,580 fare + ¥1,620 limited express). It is on a railway, so road traffic does not affect it, which is why we pick it for a fixed arrival time.
Seats are the catch. Every seat is reserved, tickets go on sale one month ahead, and JR East's booking partner warns they often sell out at weekends and in peak seasons. Ekitan notes a luggage storage area on board; a shelf space is not reserved with your seat, so board early. As far as Otsuki the train runs coupled to a Kaiji or Azusa: check that your car number is a Fuji Excursion car. It leaves Shinjuku from platforms 9–10.
Last regular direct, weekday
10:30
Arrives 12:24
Seasonal 11:34 to 29 Dec.
Shinjuku to Kawaguchiko
¥4,200
Reserved seats only
On sale a month ahead.
Suits: weekends, holidays, a booked tour or check-in time. Not for: afternoon departures, or last-minute plans in busy seasons.
Answer C · Connecting trains
Kaiji to Otsuki, then a Fujikyu local
One change · runs until late
The Kaiji limited express leaves Shinjuku at about :30 past each hour on weekdays and reaches Otsuki about an hour later (12:30 arrives 13:28). At Otsuki you do not go outside: you walk through the connecting passage and transfer gate to the Fujikyu platform. Fujikyu trains for Kawaguchiko leave one to three times an hour (weekday afternoon locals 13:01, 13:55, 14:25, 15:03…), so allow for a wait of up to about 50 minutes; the 12:30 Kaiji, for example, meets the 13:55 local. The Japan Bullet Train guide puts this route about 20–30 minutes slower than the direct train.
It is the flexible option: the last weekday connection is the 21:59 Kaiji, reaching Otsuki at 23:02, for the 23:10 last train to Kawaguchiko. The Otsuki–Kawaguchiko fare is ¥1,170, and the locals need no seat ticket. The cost is a transfer with your case: the passage is signposted, but we could not confirm a step-free route at Otsuki, so travel light or allow extra time.
Last connection, weekday
21:59
Otsuki 23:02 → 23:10
Last Fujikyu to Kawaguchiko.
Fujikyu, Otsuki–Kawaguchiko
¥1,170
Locals: no seat ticket
1–3 trains an hour.
Suits: late starts, sold-out direct trains, travellers who like to keep plans open. Not for: two heavy cases each, or anyone who wants no change at all.
Our verdict
We suggest: on a weekday, with one big case each, book the highway bus from Busta Shinjuku: it is the cheapest (¥2,000), the case goes in the hold and you choose from departures across the day. Switch to the Fuji Excursion when the arrival time matters more than the fare (weekends, holidays, a booked dinner or tour), and book it the day sales open. Use the Kaiji via Otsuki when the direct train is full or you leave after 10:30. The answer changes if anyone has more than one big case: the bus takes one per person, so then take the train.
See Shinjuku–Kawaguchiko bus options →Opens Klook. Check the luggage rule on the ticket page.
Arriving in Tokyo first? See Shinjuku with a suitcase and bags before check-in. Sending the case ahead instead? See forward, carry or store.
One more thing: a ticket without a seat number
If the Fuji Excursion shows no reserved seats, look again. Fujikyu Railway says you can buy either a reserved-seat limited express ticket or an unreserved-seat ticket, which fixes only the date and section, not the train or seat. The same page notes that between Fujisan and Kawaguchiko stations you can ride the limited express with a normal fare ticket and take any free seat.
Source: Fujikyu Railway, Fuji Excursion (Fuji Kaiyu) page. Checked 23 November 2026.

## 'Mount Fuji View' Rooms at Lake Kawaguchi: What You Actually Buy
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kawaguchiko-fuji-view-room-what-you-buy
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Only one thing guarantees Fuji from your bed: a room type whose name says "Mt. Fuji View". The hotel's name does not, and neither does a room "selected at check-in". On Wed 16 Dec 2026 the named Fuji room at Fuji View Hotel cost ¥8,280 more than the same-size garden-view room. If the view matters more than the bed, we suggest a ¥14,910 twin by the lake and a walk to the Kawaguchiko Ohashi Bridge at first light, which costs nothing.
Booking.com, Jalan, Ikyu, Toyoko Inn and the Fujikawaguchiko Tourism Association · sample night Wed 16 Dec 2026, 2 adults · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · The room view
Buy the room type, not the hotel name
+¥8,280 for two
Fuji View Hotel has Fuji in its name, but on our night its cheapest rooms were listed with garden and inner-courtyard views. The room sold for the mountain is a separate category: Moderate Japanese-Style Room with Mt.Fuji View, 36 m², at ¥61,020 for two with breakfast. The 36 m² garden-view twin was ¥52,740 on the same terms. The difference, ¥8,280, is the actual price of the view.
Two things make this the safe way to pay for Fuji. The view is written into what you book, so it is not left to the front desk. And both rates could be cancelled free before 9 December. The hotel is about 10 minutes by car from Kawaguchiko Station, with a free hourly shuttle from the station until 19:45 (per its Jalan listing).
Mt.Fuji View room, breakfast
¥61,020
36 m², 2 adults
+ ¥300 tax, Wed 16 Dec.
Same size, garden view
¥52,740
The view costs ¥8,280
Same hotel, same night.
Suits: couples who want Fuji from the room without a cold dawn walk. Not for: anyone reading "Fuji" in a hotel name as a promise.
Answer B · The shared view
"Selected at check-in" means the view is not yours yet
¥47,500 vs ¥39,330
Kasuitei Ooya, a lakeside ryokan about 550 m from Kawaguchiko Station in a straight line, sells a Japanese-Style Room Selected at Check-In: ¥47,500 for two with breakfast on 16 Dec. Its room sold as No View was ¥39,330. So you pay ¥8,170 more for a room the hotel chooses on arrival. Booking.com lists that room type at 17 m².
What the hotel does promise is shared. Its Ikyu listing describes a 7th-floor observation bath overlooking the lake, open 15:00–24:00 and again 5:00–10:00, and a private bath you can book for ¥3,300 per 50 minutes. If the picture that sold you the room was taken from a bath, a lounge or a terrace, check when guests can use it. Here the early session starts at 5:00, so you can be in the bath before sunrise.

Suits: onsen lovers happy to see the view from the bath. Not for: anyone who wants it in writing that the room faces Fuji.
Answer C · The public viewpoint
Standard room, then walk to the bridge
¥14,910 · view free
Toyoko Inn Fuji Kawaguchiko Ohashi had a 15 m² twin at ¥14,910 for two on 16 Dec, breakfast included and taxes in, free cancellation until 15 December. Breakfast runs 6:30–9:00, so you can be out at first light and back for it. The hotel is a 15-minute walk or a 7-minute free shuttle from Kawaguchiko Station.
The view is public. The Fujikawaguchiko Tourism Association points to the Kawaguchiko Ohashi Bridge, which has a footpath (stay off the roadway), and to Ubuyagasaki at its north end, famous for Fuji with the bridge and for the upside-down reflection on still mornings. Ubuyagasaki is about 1.6 km north of the station in a straight line. The first sightseeing bus there only leaves the station at 9:00, so at dawn you walk.
Twin with breakfast, 2 adults

Viewpoint cost

Suits: travellers on a budget, photographers who would go out anyway. Not for: very cold mornings with small children, or anyone with limited mobility.
Our verdict
We suggest: if you are paying for Fuji, pay for a room type that names it, and compare it with the same-size room in the same hotel; on our night that gap was ¥8,280. Don't pay extra for a hotel name or a room picked at check-in. If you would rather spend the money elsewhere, book the ¥14,910 twin and walk to the bridge at dawn. The answer changes with the weather: cloud can hide Fuji completely, and both paid view rooms here had to be cancelled by 9 December, a week before the stay. When you cannot change the date, the free viewpoint loses less on a grey morning.
Compare Lake Kawaguchi rooms for your date →Opens Booking.com. Read the room name, not the hotel name.
Choosing where to sleep at the lake? See station hotel, north shore or lakeside ryokan. Getting there with luggage? See bus or train with a big suitcase.
One more thing: the reflection is a dawn thing
The "upside-down Fuji" in the lake is not only seen from Ubuyagasaki. The town's tourism association says you can see it from most of the north shore when there is no wind and the water is calm, and that it is most likely right from daybreak. It also notes that Yagisaki Park on the south shore has few clear Fuji views, so a "lake view" on that side may show water, not the mountain.
Source: Fujikawaguchiko Tourism Association, 22 Recommended Mt. Fuji Photo Spots. Checked 23 November 2026.

## Lake Kawaguchi Without a Car: Station Hotel, North Shore or Lakeside Ryokan?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/lake-kawaguchi-station-or-lake-view
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Without a car, we suggest one of two ends, not the middle. If the budget allows, book a lakeside ryokan with dinner and a room sold as "Mt. Fuji view": dinner is in the building and Fuji is outside the window at dawn (¥57,200 for two with both meals on our sample night). On a budget, sleep by Kawaguchiko Station (¥13,200), eat by about 18:00, and take the 05:49 train to the pagoda viewpoint. The north shore on its own is the hard one: the last bus out there leaves the station at 17:45.
Booking.com, Fujikyu Bus, JR East and Tabelog · sample night Wed 16 Dec 2026, 2 adults · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Station area
Sleep by the station, eat early, take the first train
¥13,200 · dinner by 19:00
The cheapest way to get both things is to stay within a few minutes of the platform. Kawaguchiko Station Inn, 100 m from the station, was ¥13,200 for two in a Japanese-style twin with a shared bathroom (rated 8.8) on Wed 16 Dec. You walk from the train to the room with your bags, no bus needed.
The catch is dinner time. Hoto Fudo's station branch, a minute's walk away, lists 11:00–19:00, or until sold out, every day, on Tabelog, and takes no cards or e-money (budget ¥1,000–1,999 a head). For Fuji at first light, the 05:49 local from Kawaguchiko reaches Shimoyoshida at 06:03 on JR East's December 2026 timetable; the pagoda viewpoint is a short walk and a climb from there. The sightseeing buses do not start until 9:00.
Station Inn, Wed 16 Dec
¥13,200
Twin, shared bath
100 m from the station.

Suits: budget trips and early risers. Not for: a late, relaxed dinner, or travellers who want Fuji from the room.
Answer B · North shore
Fuji across the water, but check the room and the bus
Last bus out 17:45
From the north shore you look south across the lake to Fuji. HOTORI no HOTEL BAN sits on the Red Line, 19 minutes from the station by bus, and its Deluxe Twin (20 m²) was ¥24,300 room only. Read the listing closely: Booking.com describes those rooms as mountain, city and inner-courtyard view, and the Annex rooms as city view. Nothing there promises Fuji from your bed, so ask the hotel in writing which way your room faces.
Then the evening. Fujikyu's Red Line runs every 15 minutes, but the last bus from the station leaves at 17:45 and reaches the Hotel Ban stop at 18:04; the last one back toward the station leaves Oishi Park at 18:27. So a dinner near the station means eating very early or a taxi back; we could not confirm a taxi fare from an operator, so book one ahead and ask the price.

Answer C · Lakeside stay with dinner
Pay for dinner in, and for the right window
Dinner +¥4,400 for two
A ryokan with dinner solves the transport problem: you arrive, and you do not go out again. Lakeland Hotel Mizunosato, a lakeside hotel about 7 minutes by car from the station, offers a free pickup if you ask the ryokan association desk at the station to call (14:45–20:00, per its Jalan listing). On Wed 16 Dec its Mt. Fuji view room (28 m²) was ¥50,600 room only, ¥52,800 with breakfast and ¥57,200 with breakfast and dinner, for two, plus ¥300 tax.
Two things we noticed. Dinner adds only ¥4,400 for two over the breakfast rate, close to what a simple dinner out for two costs (Hoto Fudo's Tabelog budget is ¥1,000–1,999 a head), with no ride back to arrange. And the view is what you really pay for: the same hotel sells a no-view room at ¥38,500, so Fuji costs ¥12,100 more, and it sells "lake view" as a separate room type, so a lake-view room is not a Fuji-view room. These rates showed free cancellation until 11 December.
Fuji-view room, both meals

2 adults, + ¥300 tax

Fuji view vs no view
+¥12,100

Same hotel, same night.
Suits: couples who want dinner and dawn without leaving the building. Not for: tight budgets; the station room costs about a quarter of this (meals not included).
Our verdict
We suggest: for one night without a car, book the lakeside stay with dinner and a room sold as "Mt. Fuji view" if ¥57,200 for two fits your budget: no evening transport, and the view is in the room. Otherwise sleep by Kawaguchiko Station for about ¥13,200, have dinner by 18:00 and take the 05:49 train for the morning view. Choose the north shore only if you arrive by mid-afternoon, eat near the hotel and have the room's view confirmed in writing. The answer changes if the forecast turns cloudy before the free-cancellation date (then the ¥12,100 view premium buys nothing), or if you rent a car.
Compare Lake Kawaguchi stays for your date →Opens Booking.com. Check the room type says "Mt. Fuji view".
Going on to Hakone with a big case? See forward, carry or store. Starting from Tokyo? See where to stay on a first trip.
One more thing: the pagoda before breakfast
From Shimoyoshida Station it is about a 10-minute walk to Arakurayama Sengen Park, then 398 steps up the Sakuya Hime Stairway to the Chureito Pagoda, with Fuji behind it (there is also a sloping footpath). The park is free and open all day, so the 05:49 train works. Reviewers on GOOD LUCK TRIP call the view worth the climb and suggest coming early for easier photos; one also warns that clouds often hide Fuji, so check the sky before you set an alarm.
Arakurayama Sengen Park, 3353-1 Arakura, Fujiyoshida. Source: GOOD LUCK TRIP directory and reviews; train times JR East December 2026 timetable. Checked 23 November 2026.

## Big Suitcase and One Night in Hakone: Forward It, Carry It or Store It?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/hakone-big-suitcase-forward-carry-store
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For a one-night stop, we suggest sending the suitcase straight from Tokyo to your Kyoto hotel and travelling through Hakone with a small overnight bag. Yamato's own search shows a case sent from Shinjuku on Tue 15 Dec arriving in central Kyoto on Wed 16 Dec, and a large case up to 160 cm costs ¥3,160. If you must have it in Hakone, hand it to the luggage desk at Hakone-Yumoto by noon (¥1,500–2,500). If you change trains at Odawara both ways, a large locker there is about ¥1,600 for the night.
Yamato Transport, Hakone Tozan Bus and JR East locker pages · sample trip Tokyo 15 Dec → Hakone → Kyoto 16 Dec 2026 · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Forward it
Send it from Tokyo to Kyoto, skip Hakone entirely
¥3,160 · next day
We ran Yamato Transport's delivery-date search from Shinjuku (160-0022) to the Kyoto Station area (600-8216): sent on Tue 15 Dec 2026, it shows delivery on Wed 16 Dec, with a morning time slot available. That fits a Tokyo check-out on the 15th, one night in Hakone and a Kyoto check-in on the 16th. Most Tokyo hotel desks can arrange the pickup; Yamato says cut-off times vary by counter, so ask at check-in, not at check-out.
Prices on that route, per piece: up to 160 cm and 25 kg: ¥3,160 cash (¥3,157 cashless), up to 180 cm and 30 kg: ¥4,480, up to 200 cm: ¥5,410. Size is length + width + height. Two checks before you send: your Kyoto hotel must agree to hold a parcel that arrives before you do, and your overnight bag needs everything for the ryokan night and the next morning.
160 size, Tokyo to Kyoto
¥3,160
Up to 25 kg
Cash price, per piece.
Sent Tue 15 Dec
Wed 16
Morning slot possible
Yamato date search.
Suits: almost every Tokyo, Hakone, Kyoto trip. Not for: a Kyoto hotel that won't accept parcels before check-in, or a case you need in Hakone.
Answer B · Take it along
Carry it to Hakone-Yumoto, let Hakone carry it up
¥1,500–2,500 · by 12:00
Hakone Tozan Bus runs a Hakone Luggage Transport Service from Hakone-Yumoto Station, the gateway station. Drop the case at the counter between 8:30 and 12:00 on arrival day (book online by 11:30 the same day, or queue at the counter) and collect it at your hotel after 15:00. In between, you ride the mountain trains and boats with your hands free.
The fee is per piece, one way: ¥1,500 for a regular piece (up to 140 cm, 15 kg) and ¥2,500 for a large one (up to 200 cm, 30 kg). Two limits: it only delivers to partner facilities, so check your ryokan is on the list before you book, and in early January some hotels around Lake Ashi may not be served because of road congestion.
Large piece, one way
¥2,500
Up to 200 cm, 30 kg
Regular ¥1,500.
Drop at Yumoto
8:30–12
At your hotel

Suits: travellers going back to Tokyo after Hakone, or anyone who needs the case that night. Not for: arriving at Yumoto after 12:00, or a ryokan that is not a partner.
Answer C · Store it on the way
An L locker at Odawara, if you pass it twice
≈¥1,600 + ¥500 to reserve
Odawara is where the Tokaido Shinkansen meets the trains into Hakone, so travellers who arrive by Shinkansen and leave by Shinkansen pass it twice. JR East's Multi ecube site lists a locker bank inside the JR gates, in the Shinkansen connecting passage: L ¥800 per day (M ¥600, S ¥500), plus ¥500 if you reserve, open from the first to the last train.
The catch is in the FAQ: a locker "day" starts at 2:00 a.m., so one night counts as two days, about ¥1,600 for an L, or ¥2,100 reserved. An L is 86 cm high, 34 cm wide and 65 cm deep: measure how thick your case is. When we checked, that bank showed only 4 free L lockers, so we would reserve.
L locker, one night
¥1,600
¥2,100 if reserved
Two locker days.
L locker size
86×34×65 cm
Max 3 days
JR East Multi ecube.
Suits: Shinkansen in, Shinkansen out, and a case under 34 cm thick. Not for: travellers on the Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku who never enter the JR gates at Odawara.
Our verdict
We suggest: forward the suitcase from your Tokyo hotel straight to your Kyoto hotel (¥3,160 for a 160-size case on the route we checked, delivered the next day) and spend the Hakone night with a small bag. It is the only option where you never touch the case between two cities. The answer changes if your Kyoto hotel will not hold parcels, or you return to Tokyo after Hakone: then use the Yumoto luggage desk (arrive by 12:00). If you change at Odawara by Shinkansen both ways and want the case for day two, reserve an L locker there.
Lockers full? Book luggage storage →Opens Radical Storage. Book a spot near your station in English.
Arriving in Tokyo early with the same case? See who takes your suitcase before check-in. Two suitcases in one room? See double or twin.
One more thing: the bag-free last morning
The Hakone luggage service also runs downhill. Hand the case to your hotel's front desk by 10:00 on check-out day, spend the morning on the ropeway or the lake with nothing to carry, and collect it at Hakone-Yumoto Station between 13:30 and 18:30 on your way out. It can only be arranged at the hotel desk on the day (no online booking for this direction), so ask about it when you check in.
Same fees as the outbound service. Source: Hakone Tozan Bus, Hakone Luggage Transport Service (hakonenavi.jp), checked 23 November 2026.

## Tokyo Disney: Book the Hotel Night Before or After Your Park Day?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-disney-hotel-night-before-or-after
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If the room is at one of the six Disney hotels, we suggest the night before: their early entry, Happy Entry, works on every day of your stay except the day you check in. If it is an Official Hotel such as the Hilton or Sheraton, there is no early entry either way, so we'd spend the night after, when the park closes at 21:00 and a tired child is one monorail ride and a free shuttle from bed. And if your Tokyo hotel is near the Keiyo Line, keeping it can cost about the same.
Tokyo Disney Resort official pages and Booking.com · park day Thu 17 Dec 2026, 2 adults + 1 child aged 6 · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · The night before
Sleep there first, if it's a Disney hotel
Happy Entry: 15 min early
Tokyo Disney Resort's own rule is the whole answer here. Guests at a Disney hotel can enter Tokyo Disneyland 15 minutes before other guests through a special entrance, and the benefit applies on every day of the stay, including check-out day, except the day of check-in. The six hotels listed for Tokyo Disneyland include the Tokyo Disney Resort Toy Story Hotel and the Tokyo Disney Celebration Hotel. Each guest aged 4 or over gets a pass.
Two honest limits from the same page: it "does not guarantee" a full 15 minutes if the hotel entrance is busy, and a few dates are excluded for some hotels (at Tokyo Disneyland, 12 January 2027 for MiraCosta, Fantasy Chateau and Celebration Hotel guests). The time you save on the commute is real too: Tokyo Disney Resort gives about 20 minutes from Tokyo Station and 40 minutes from Shinjuku to the park.
Happy Entry
15 min
Not on check-in day
Disney hotels only.
Park hours, Thu 17 Dec
9–21 h
1-Day Passport ¥10,900
Adult, that date.
Suits: families booking a Disney hotel who want the first rides. Not for: Official Hotel guests, who get no early entry. Disney hotel rates are not on Booking.com, so we could not compare them on the same dates.
Answer B · The night after
Official Hotel: use it for the 21:00 exit
Monorail + free shuttle
Tokyo Disney Resort's list of Official Hotel benefits has a free shuttle, ticket help and baggage services, but no early entry. So the morning is the same whether you slept at Maihama or not, and the hotel is worth more at night. After the 21:00 closing you ride the Disney Resort Line to Bayside Station (the monorail loops its four stations in about 13 minutes; ¥300 adult, ¥150 child, last train 23:30) and take the free Disney Resort Cruiser bus to the hotel.
Prices for 2 adults and a 6-year-old on Thu 17 Dec 2026 on Booking.com: Sheraton Grande Tokyo Bay ¥40,000 (Ocean Dream Room, 3 beds), Hilton Tokyo Bay ¥43,505 (Twin Hilton Room Park), Hotel Okura Tokyo Bay ¥40,117 (Deluxe). A Disney hotel the night after works too, but you pay Disney hotel rates for proximity only: no Happy Entry on the check-in day.
Sheraton, Thu 17 Dec
¥40,000
3 beds, incl. taxes
2 adults + child.
Resort Line loop
13 min
¥300 / child ¥150
Last train 23:30.
Suits: families staying for the 20:30 Starbright Christmas show (on 17 Dec) with a child who will fall asleep on the way. Not for: anyone who booked a Disney hotel for the early entry.
Answer C · Both nights in Tokyo
Keep one room on the Keiyo Line
Hatchobori ≈ same price
Besides Tokyo Station, consider Hatchobori, the first Keiyo Line stop after Tokyo on the way to Maihama. You board one stop closer than Tokyo Station, and you never repack: the suitcases stay in one room for the whole trip. Tokyo Disney Resort puts Maihama about 15 minutes by train from Tokyo Station, so the ride from Hatchobori is a little shorter.
What surprised us: on these dates it was not much cheaper. ICI Hotel Tokyo Hatchobori was ¥39,600 on Wed 16 Dec and ¥37,950 on Thu 17 Dec, against ¥43,000 and ¥40,000 at the Sheraton. So the case for C is no move with the bags, not the money. One exception: Hotel Okura Tokyo Bay had a Black Friday deal at ¥27,594 for Wed 16 Dec; deals like that change the maths, so check your own dates.

Sheraton, Wed / Thu
¥43,000 / ¥40,000
Official Hotel
Same search.
Suits: families with Tokyo nights on both sides of the park day and big suitcases. Not for: a child who cannot manage a train ride after 21:00.
Our verdict
We suggest: match the night to the hotel type. A Disney hotel: the night before, because Happy Entry never works on the check-in day. An Official Hotel: the night after, because it has no early entry and its value is the short ride home after the 21:00 closing. The answer changes if your central hotel is on the Keiyo Line and within a few thousand yen of Maihama (then keep it and skip the move), or if a deal makes a Maihama room much cheaper on one of the two nights.
Compare Maihama hotels for your dates →Opens Booking.com. Book in English; many rooms show free cancellation.
Still choosing your Tokyo base? See where to stay on a first trip and what to do with bags before check-in.
One more thing: check out without the suitcase
If you sleep at an Official Hotel the night before, you do not have to carry your bags around the park or back to the station. Tokyo Disney Resort's Station Delivery Service (fee required) lets you leave them at the hotel when you check out, between 7:00 and 12:30, and pick them up at the counter on the street level of the Tokyo Disney Resort Welcome Center, next to JR Maihama Station, when you leave. It works in reverse on arrival: a counter on the station level sends your bags to the hotel.
Pick-up time depends on when you dropped the bags off. Source: Tokyo Disney Resort, Guest Benefits at Hotels Affiliated with Tokyo Disney Resort, checked 23 November 2026.

## Kiyosumi-Shirakawa as a Tokyo Base: Quiet Mornings, but Breakfast at Seven?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kiyosumi-shirakawa-base-7am-start
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Yes, it works as a base for 7 a.m. starts, if you pick the right hotel. The famous coffee does not open early: Blue Bottle opens at 8:00. For a fixed 7:00 departure we suggest a hotel above the station with breakfast from 6:30, then the 07:05 train, which starts at Kiyosumi-Shirakawa and reaches Shibuya at 07:28. Want a café breakfast at 7:00? The riverside CLANN opens then, but it is a 10-minute walk from the station.
Sample weekday Wed 16 Dec 2026 · official café, garden and hotel pages, Booking.com, Jorudan · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · A named place serving at seven
CLANN BY THE RIVER
Opens 7:00 · 10 min from Exit A3
The restaurant on the 2nd floor of LYURO Tokyo Kiyosumi (it used to be PITMANS) lists 7:00–22:00 every day and serves a soup breakfast with bread from chigaya, the Kuramae bakery, and coffee from LEAVES COFFEE ROASTERS beans. It sits right on the Sumida River with a wooden terrace. It is cashless only: card, Suica or Pasmo, or QR payment.
The catch is the clock. It is about 10 minutes on foot from Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Exit A3, so breakfast at 7:00 means a train closer to 7:30. That is a perfect slow start if you sleep at LYURO itself, but not if you must be out at 7:00. The restaurant also asks you to contact it for details, so check before an important morning.
Listed opening time
7:00
Soup and bread
Cashless only.
Walk from the station
10 min
Exit A3
Or Suitengumae Exit 4.
Suits: guests at LYURO, and anyone whose day starts at 7:30–8:00. Not for: a strict 7:00 departure from a hotel near the station.
Answer B · Stay for a slow morning
Blue Bottle at 8, the garden at 9
8:00 · 9:00 · ¥150
The neighbourhood's reputation is built on later mornings. Blue Bottle's Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Flagship Cafe opens 8:00–19:00 every day, with 47 seats. Kiyosumi Gardens opens at 9:00 (last entry 16:30) for ¥150, and is closed only from 29 Dec to 1 Jan.
So the people who love this base are the ones who are not rushing: a coffee at 8, the pond garden at 9, then the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo or the river walk. Our Kiyosumi-Shirakawa guide covers what is worth paying for there.

Answer C · A fixed 7:00 departure
Hotel breakfast above the station
From 6:30 · 0 min from Exit B1
Comfort Hotel Tokyo Kiyosumi Shirakawa sits at Exit B1 (the hotel says 0 minutes on foot) and serves a free buffet breakfast from 6:30 to 9:30 on the 2nd floor. On Booking.com a double for 1 adult with breakfast was about ¥16,000 for Wed 16 Dec 2026 (¥16,072) before it sold out later the same day.
The route out: on our Wednesday the 07:05 Hanzomon Line train started at Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, so it leaves from here rather than arriving full, and reached Shibuya at 07:28 (¥209) with no change, or Tokyo Station at 07:18 via Otemachi (¥178). The 07:08 Oedo Line also started here and reached Shinjuku at 07:40 (¥272). Breakfast at 6:30, at the platform by 7:05.

Suits: day trips, early trains from Tokyo or Shinjuku, anyone who wants a sure breakfast. Not for: travellers who came for a café breakfast; save that for a slow day.
Our verdict
We suggest: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is a good base for quiet mornings even with 7:00 starts, if you sleep by the station and eat the hotel breakfast from 6:30. Trains starting here put you in Shibuya by 07:28 or Shinjuku by 07:40. The answer changes when your departure moves to about 7:30: then walk to CLANN for its 7:00 riverside breakfast. And keep one morning with no alarm for Blue Bottle at 8:00 and the garden at 9:00, which is why people stay here.
See stays in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa →Opens Booking.com. Check breakfast times and the walk to the station.
Planning a Sunday here? See Monzen-nakacho's market days, one stop away. Still choosing an area? See where to stay on a first trip.
One more thing: the bridge five minutes from your bed
On your first evening, walk five minutes from the station to Kiyosubashi Bridge. It is a 1928 suspension bridge modelled on one in Cologne, now a National Important Cultural Property, and it is lit up from just after sunset until 23:00. From the middle you see the Sumida River with Skytree in the distance, and the riverside terrace below is almost empty at night.
Kiyosubashi, Kiyosumi 1, Koto-ku; about 5 min from Kiyosumi-shirakawa Station. Lit from about 15 min after sunset to 23:00. Free. Sources: GO TOKYO, Tokyo Metropolitan Government Location Box, nightscape.tokyo.

## Arriving in Tokyo at 8 a.m.: Who Will Take Your Suitcase Before Check-in?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-early-arrival-luggage
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If you land early, we suggest booking a hotel with a 24-hour front desk that says in its FAQ it keeps bags before check-in: you drop them at 8 a.m. and walk away. A self check-in apartment usually cannot take them; the one we checked opens its doors at 16:00. Then a station locker is the fallback: a large one at a JR station costs about ¥900–1,000 a day, and Ueno alone has hundreds.
Hotel FAQ, Booking.com listing and JR East locker guides · sample stay Wed 16 Dec 2026 · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · A staffed hotel
Drop the bags at the front desk
Free · 24-hour desk
Hotels with a staffed desk often state this in their FAQ. Sotetsu Fresa Inn Tokyo-Toyocho's own FAQ, as an example: the front desk is open 24 hours, and staff keep luggage before check-in and after check-out, limited to those two days. So an 8 a.m. arrival is fine; you are not asking a favour.
Read the small print on two points. The same FAQ says it cannot take luggage that is too large or in large quantities, so a family with four big cases should ask first. And it will hold parcels you courier ahead for up to one week before check-in, handy if you want to send a case on from your first stop.
Front desk
24 h
Bags before check-in
Same day only.
Couriered bags held
7 days
Before your check-in
Per the hotel FAQ.
Suits: almost everyone arriving before noon. Not for: oversized loads; check the FAQ or email first.
Answer B · An apartment stay
Self check-in: check for a real drop-off point
Door opens 16:00
Apartments win on space (see our room-size comparison), but mornings are their weak spot. The Kinshicho flat we priced, Brillia ist Kinshi Park, uses smart check-in with an unmanned desk, check-in runs 16:00–22:00, and luggage storage is not in its facilities list. Land at 8 a.m. and that is eight hours before anyone can let you in.
Some hosts do offer a drop-off room or a partner shop. We suggest you ask in a message before booking, and only count on it if the answer names a place and its opening hours. "We'll try" is not a drop-off point.
Check-in window
16–22 h
Unmanned desk
No listed bag storage.
Gap after an 8 a.m. arrival
8 h
Bags need a plan
Ask the host in writing.
Suits: afternoon arrivals, or hosts who confirm a drop-off address. Not for: red-eye flights with no plan for the bags.
Answer C · Station storage
A large locker where your day ends
≈¥900–1,000 · first to last train
Put the case in a locker at the station nearest to where you will sleep, so you collect it on the way in. JR East gives its usual locker prices as S ¥500, M ¥700–800 and L ¥900–1,000, available from the first to the last train. By its size guide, L fits a larger suitcase and LL a larger suitcase plus shopping.
Ueno as an example, where the Keisei airport trains from Narita end: JR East lists 21 locker sites around the station, 13 of them in JR Ueno. Outside the Shinobazu gate are 20 LL and 56 L lockers; inside, the Shinobazu gate passage has 119 L and the Park gate passage 100 L. Busy stations fill up, so JR East's Multi ecube lockers can be reserved up to a month ahead, at ¥100–200 more for M and L in busy periods.
JR East L locker, usual
¥900–1,000
S ¥500 · M ¥700–800
First to last train.
LL lockers, Shinobazu gate
20
Plus 56 L outside
JR Ueno, per JR East.
Suits: apartment guests, and anyone whose hotel is next to a big station. Not for: a day that ends far from the station where the bag sits.
Our verdict
We suggest: with an 8 a.m. arrival, book a staffed hotel whose FAQ says it keeps bags before check-in, and drop them on the way from the airport. It costs nothing and you collect them at the desk. Book the apartment only if the host names a drop-off point; otherwise budget about ¥1,000 for an L locker at the station nearest the flat. The answer changes with oversized or many cases (ask the hotel first, or use LL lockers), and if you arrive after about 16:00, when even the self check-in flat is open.
Lockers full? Book luggage storage →Opens Radical Storage. Book a spot near your station in English.
Still choosing your airport train? See Narita and Haneda: which train. Landing at Narita for Asakusa? See which Asakusa station.
One more thing: send the suitcase ahead
Before you think about lockers, consider not carrying the suitcase at all. Airport counters with the Hands-Free Travel logo (JAL ABC, Yamato and others) can deliver your bag to your hotel the same day if you drop it off in the morning, so you go straight into the city with a day bag. JAL's same-day service from Haneda Terminal 3 costs ¥4,500 a bag. It delivers to hotels only and may slip to the next day at peak times.
Look for the Hands-Free Travel counters in the arrival lobbies at Narita, Haneda and Kansai. Same-day cut-off times and prices vary by company and airport. Sources: JNTO (japan.travel) Hands-Free Travel, JAL Same-day Delivery Service.

## Tokyo for ¥15,000: Double, Twin or a Bigger Room Farther Out for Two Suitcases?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-double-or-twin-two-suitcases
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For two people opening two suitcases, we suggest the bigger room farther out. On Wed 16 Dec 2026 a 25 m² flat in Kinshicho was ¥10,968 for 2 adults, while the only room under budget at our Ueno hotel was a 13.8 m² double at ¥15,250. The twin at the same hotel was 18.4 m² but ¥19,650, and its second bed takes most of the extra space. Kinshicho added no time to Shinjuku or Shibuya.
Wed 16 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, 2 adults, prices including taxes on Booking.com · floor plans from the hotel's official site · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · The double: what the plan really shows
ICI HOTEL Ueno Shin Okachimachi, double
¥15,250 · 13.80 m²
This is a typical well-reviewed Ueno-side hotel (8.4 on Booking.com), a 3-minute walk from Shin-Okachimachi Exit A2 on the Oedo Line. Its standard double was ¥15,250 for our night, the only room type for two there within ¥15,000-ish.
The hotel publishes the floor plan: 13.80 m² in total, of which the sleeping area is 4.9 tatami mats. The bed is 140 cm wide and pushed against one wall. Reading the plan with the bed as a ruler, that leaves one strip of floor roughly 85–90 cm wide beside the bed, narrowed further by the desk at the window end. One large case opened flat fits there; a second one ends up on the bed.
Whole room, official plan
13.8 m²
Bed 140 × 195 cm
Against one wall.
Free floor beside the bed
≈85 cm
Our plan reading
Room for one open case.
Suits: light packers, one big case between two, short stays. Not for: two people who both live out of a large suitcase.
Answer B · The twin at the same hotel
Same hotel, standard twin
¥19,650 · 18.40 m²
The twin is the obvious upgrade: 18.40 m² on the official plan, 4.6 m² more than the double. But the plan draws the two 120 cm beds side by side, with almost no gap between them, and the free floor is again one strip, this time at the foot of the beds, about 95 cm wide where the desk is not. The bigger win is the entrance: the area inside the door is wider, so a case can stand open there too.
It cost ¥19,650 on our night, ¥4,400 more than the double and over budget. A tip from the same price list: the hotel's deluxe double is about 18 m² with one 180 cm bed and was ¥18,750, ¥900 less than the twin. One bed in the same floor area should leave more floor, but the hotel does not publish that plan, so ask for a photo before you book.

Suits: two people who need separate beds more than floor space. Not for: anyone paying extra mainly for suitcase room.
Answer C · A bigger room, one area farther out
Brillia ist Kinshi Park, Kinshicho
¥10,968 · 25 m²
East of the Sumida River, Kinshicho is a busy local hub on the JR Sobu Line and the Hanzomon subway. A 25 m² one-bedroom flat here (a double bed plus a futon, kitchen and washing machine, 9.0 on Booking.com) was ¥10,968 for 2 adults including taxes, a 5-minute walk from the station. If you want even more room, the 40 m² version was ¥18,804.
The commute: leaving around 9:00 on our Wednesday, Kinshicho to Shinjuku was 21 minutes (one change at Ochanomizu, ¥253) and to Shibuya 31 minutes with no change on the Hanzomon Line (¥252). From the Ueno hotel the same trips took 27 and 33 minutes. Where Kinshicho loses is Ueno and Ameyoko: about 16 minutes with a change, which the Ueno hotel covers on foot. The catch: no staffed desk, check-in 16:00–22:00 only, and quiet hours from 21:00.

Our verdict
We suggest: for two big suitcases at ¥15,000, book the bigger room one area out. In Kinshicho ¥10,968 bought 25 m², almost double the Ueno double, with no extra time to Shinjuku or Shibuya. The answer changes if you land in the morning (an unstaffed flat cannot take bags before 16:00) or if your days centre on Ueno and Asakusa: then the Ueno double works for one open case, and the deluxe double at ¥18,750 is a better upgrade than the twin, if you can stretch the budget by about ¥3,750.
See stays around Kinshicho →Opens Booking.com. Filter by room size and check the check-in hours.
Arriving before check-in? See who will take your suitcase at 8 a.m. Still choosing an area? See where to stay on a first trip.
One more thing: the craft street under the tracks
If you pick Ueno–Okachimachi, walk four minutes from Okachimachi's South Exit to 2k540 AKI-OKA ARTISAN, about 50 small workshops, studios and cafés built into the arches under the JR line. Everything is made by hand in Japan, including leather, wood, ceramics and denim, and some shops let you try making something yourself. It's a far better souvenir run than the airport.
2k540 AKI-OKA ARTISAN, 5-9 Ueno, Taito-ku; about 4 min from JR Okachimachi South Exit. 11:00–19:00; closed Wednesdays (hours vary by shop). The name is its distance from Tokyo Station: 2.54 km. Sources: GO TOKYO, Time Out Tokyo, NAVITIME.

## Last Night in Tokyo: Move from Shinjuku to Nippori Before a Narita Flight?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/last-night-shinjuku-or-nippori
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For an 08:30 arrival at Narita, stay in Shinjuku: leave at 07:13, change once at Nippori, and Skyliner 15 has you at Terminal 1 at 08:27. Moving to Nippori lets you board that same train at 07:45, only 32 minutes more sleep, and the move costs about that much the evening before. Sleep at the airport only when you need to be there before the first Skyliner arrives at 06:03.
Sample departure morning Thu 17 Dec 2026, last night Wed 16 Dec · Jorudan, nine hours, Narita Airport and Booking.com, checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Stay put in Shinjuku
Out of the hotel by about 7:00
07:13 → 08:27 · ¥2,840
The fastest route on our sample morning: JR Yamanote Line from Shinjuku at 07:13 to Nippori at 07:34, then Skyliner 15 at 07:45, arriving at Narita Terminal 1 at 08:27. ¥2,840 in total, with one change and a 10-minute transfer allowance at Nippori.
Prefer no change with your bags? Narita Express 3 left Shinjuku at 06:34 and reached Terminal 1 at 07:58, ¥3,330. You start 39 minutes earlier, but you sit down once and stay seated.
Leave Shinjuku
07:13
At T1 08:27
Yamanote + Skyliner, ¥2,840.
No-change option
06:34
N'EX, at T1 07:58
¥3,330.
Suits: most travellers with a mid-morning or later flight. It keeps your last evening free and your room already booked. Not for: two big suitcases at 07:34 on a Yamanote-to-Skyliner change, if that worries you.
Answer B · Move once, to Nippori
32 minutes saved, paid for the night before
07:45 → 08:27 · ¥2,580
The morning: from Nippori you board the same Skyliner 15 at 07:45 and reach Terminal 1 at 08:27 for ¥2,580. You leave 32 minutes later than from Shinjuku and skip the change.
The evening before: check out of Shinjuku, ride the Yamanote Line 21 minutes to Nippori (our sample: 18:02 to 18:23, ¥260), walk to the hotel and check in again. APA Hotel TKP Nippori Ekimae, 200 m from the station, was ¥14,742 for 2 adults on Wed 16 Dec; the middle of the first 20 Shinjuku results that night was about ¥18,800. So the move roughly breaks even on time, and can save money if your Shinjuku nights are cancellable.

Suits: heavy luggage, travellers who want the last morning calm, and anyone whose final evening is in Ueno, Yanaka or Asakusa anyway. Not for: a last dinner in Shinjuku, since you then ride across town with your bags.
Answer C · Sleep at the airport for a very early flight
9h nine hours Narita Airport
From ¥7,000 per person
The first Skyliner on our sample morning left Nippori at 05:25 and reached Terminal 1 at 06:03; from Shinjuku you would need the 04:44 Yamanote Line to catch it. If you need to be at the airport earlier than that, trains cannot help.
The capsule hotel 9h nine hours Narita Airport is on the landside of Terminal 2 and directly connected to it. Check-in runs from 14:00 to 05:00 (tell them if you arrive after midnight), check-out is by 10:00. On 16 Dec a capsule was from ¥7,000 for men and ¥7,700 for women, per person, including taxes. Flying from Terminal 1? The free terminal shuttle bus takes about 10 minutes from Terminal 2.

Suits: solo travellers and flights where you must be at the airport before about 06:00. Not for: couples who want to share a room, as the capsules are single.
Our verdict
We suggest: keep your Shinjuku hotel and take the 07:13 Yamanote Line plus Skyliner (or the 06:34 Narita Express for no change) whenever arriving at Narita around 08:00–08:30 is enough. Move to Nippori only if you carry big bags, your last evening is on that side of town, or the room there is clearly cheaper. The answer changes when you need to be at the airport before 06:00: then sleep at Narita, because the first Skyliner does not arrive until 06:03.
See hotels near Nippori Station →Opens Booking.com. Check the walk to the Keisei gates.
Checking out hours before your train? Radical Storage lists luggage spots near Shinjuku and Nippori. Choosing your first-night base instead? See Narita, three nights, then the Shinkansen.
One more thing: dango that Soseki wrote about
Two minutes from Nippori Station is Habutae Dango, open since 1819 and famous enough to appear in Natsume Soseki's novel I Am a Cat. The dumplings are silky, made only from rice flour, and come two ways: grilled with a soy glaze that isn't sweet, or covered in smooth red bean. Eat them in the shop with green tea; they don't keep well, so they are not one for the suitcase.
Habutae Dango main shop, Higashi-Nippori 5-54-3, about 2–5 min from Nippori Station; there is also a café by the station. About ¥263 a skewer. Sources: Tabelog, Time Out Tokyo (Japanese), Retty.

## Shibuya Nightlife and a Quiet Room: Is It Worth Paying More?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shibuya-nightlife-quiet-room
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

You do not need to pay more. On Wed 16 Dec 2026 a double for 2 adults at Shibuya Granbell, on a side street in Sakuragaoka that reviewers keep calling quiet, was ¥23,800, about a 9-minute walk from a late dinner in central Shibuya. A hotel in the Udagawacho nightlife area was ¥29,045 and an Ebisu hotel ¥31,293, all including taxes. In the nightlife-area hotel, the noise reviewers mentioned came from the lift and the neighbours, not the street.
Wed 16 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, 2 adults, Booking.com · late-dinner reference: ICHIRAN Shibuya (open 24 hours) · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Same hotel: which rooms are actually loud?
Shibuya Tobu Hotel, Udagawacho
¥29,045 · ≈320 m from dinner
This is the "walk home in 4 minutes" option: about 320 m from ICHIRAN Shibuya through the Udagawacho side of the nightlife area. Its double with a small double bed was ¥29,045 for our night.
We read the most recent reviews (about 150) for anything about noise. For the double rooms, one guest in December 2024 praised how well the room kept out street noise; the complaints were a room next to the lift where guests could be heard talking (January 2026) and hearing the room next door (January 2025). A March 2026 guest described the location as close to everything but not on a loud street. So the side of the building mattered less than the position on the corridor.
Double, 2 adults, incl. taxes
¥29,045
Wed 16 Dec 2026
Small double bed.

Not the street

Suits: late nights in Udagawacho, when the shortest walk matters most. Not for: anyone who wants the most space for the money; the room is a small double.
Answer B · Same budget, a side street
Shibuya Granbell Hotel, Sakuragaoka
¥23,800 · ≈660 m from dinner
Granbell sits on the Sakuragaoka side, past the station from the nightlife streets. From ICHIRAN Shibuya the street walk is about 660 m, roughly 9 minutes, and it goes past Shibuya Station on the way. A 20 m² double for 2 adults was ¥23,800 including taxes, with free cancellation before 13 Dec.
Reviews from 2024 to November 2026 keep using the same words: a quiet street behind the station, the quiet side of Shibuya, far enough to sleep but close to the action. A November 2026 guest called the location quiet and comfortable; a December 2024 guest who stays there often called the area calm. Note that the cheapest "single room for 2 adults" in the annex is small; the 20 m² double is the fair comparison.

Suits: most couples who want nights out and a calm street, and anyone catching an early JR train. Not for: those who want to stumble home in under 5 minutes.
Answer C · A different neighbourhood: Ebisu
Prince Smart Inn Ebisu
¥31,293 · last train 00:48
Ebisu is one stop away and quieter at night, but it was not cheaper: a standard double for 2 adults was ¥31,293 including taxes, about 500 m from Ebisu Station.
Getting home: the last JR Yamanote Line train on our Wednesday left Shibuya at 00:48 and reached Ebisu at 00:50 (¥160), then the walk to the hotel. Miss it and it is about 2.3 km on foot (around 31 minutes) or about 2.7 km by taxi. Tokyo's meter starts at ¥500 for the first 1 km and adds ¥100 per 232 m, so roughly ¥1,300 before any late-night surcharge or time in traffic.

Suits: travellers whose evenings are in Ebisu itself, or who prefer a residential feel all day. Not for: Shibuya nights that end after the last train, every night.
Our verdict
We suggest: for Shibuya nights with a quiet sleep, book the side street, not the upgrade. Shibuya Granbell on the Sakuragaoka side was ¥5,245 cheaper than the Udagawacho hotel and ¥7,493 cheaper than Ebisu on our night, and reviewers describe it as quiet. The answer changes if your nights regularly end in Udagawacho after midnight: then the 4-minute walk is worth the ¥29,045, and asking for a room away from the lift costs nothing. Ebisu only wins when your evenings are in Ebisu.
See hotels on the Sakuragaoka side →Opens Booking.com. Compare the same room size and occupancy.
Want a quieter base a few stops out instead? See Yoyogi-Hachiman vs Yoyogi-Uehara. Just here for the crossing? See the best free and paid views.
One more thing: a drink in Drunkard's Alley
Before you head back to your quiet room, walk a few minutes from the station to Nonbei Yokocho, two narrow lanes of tiny bars that have stood next to the tracks since the early 1950s. Many counters fit only four or five people, so go as one or two, find an open seat, and ask about the seat charge first. It's the opposite of the scramble crossing: quiet, local and old.
Shibuya Nonbei Yokocho, 1-25 Shibuya (about 39 small businesses). Bars open in the evening; each has its own hours and charge (an otoshi or seat charge is common). Bring cash. Sources: GO TOKYO, Time Out Tokyo.

## Which "Asakusa Station" Will You Actually Use from Narita?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/asakusa-which-station-from-narita
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

From Narita you arrive at the Toei Asakusa Line station: Keisei's Access Express runs straight through, 70 minutes for ¥1,380 with no change. A hotel advertised "3 minutes from Asakusa Station" may mean the Tsukuba Express station instead, which no Narita train reaches directly. For the TX-side hotel we traced, that is about 670 m with your bags on day one, then a genuinely handy base for the next two mornings.
Traced for Hotel Trend Asakusa Annex, Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, 2 adults · Jorudan, Jalan, Booking.com and OpenStreetMap, checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Match your airport train to its station
The Access Express ends up at Toei Asakusa
70 min · ¥1,380 · no change
Our sample Access Express left Narita Terminal 1 at 15:09. At Oshiage it simply continues onto the Toei Asakusa Line (you stay seated) and reaches Asakusa at 16:19. That is the cheapest easy way in, and it puts you at the Toei station near Azuma-bashi bridge and Kaminarimon-dori.
The other airport routes land at different Asakusas. The Skyliner to Keisei-Ueno plus the Ginza Line reaches the Ginza Line's Asakusa station (16:24, ¥2,760); the Skyliner with a change at Aoto reaches the Toei station faster (16:06, ¥2,430). Reaching the Tsukuba Express Asakusa station took two changes on our search, Skyliner, JR Yamanote Line and TX via Akihabara: 16:30 and ¥3,010.
Narita T1 to Toei Asakusa
70 min
¥1,380, no change
Access Express, through-running.
Narita T1 to TX Asakusa
2 changes
72 min, ¥3,010
Skyliner + JR + TX.
Suits: anyone landing at Narita and heading to Asakusa. Check the station line in your hotel's access notes before you book, not after you land.
Answer B · The "cheaper" hotel near the Tsukuba Express
From the airport train to a TX-side hotel
≈670 m with bags
Hotel Trend Asakusa Annex lists itself as 3 minutes from the Tsukuba Express Asakusa station and 5 minutes from the Ginza Line. From TX exit A1 the street walk is only about 240 m. But you will not be coming out of TX exit A1: from the Toei station's step-free exit A2b the walk is about 670 m, roughly 9 minutes at a normal pace, before you add suitcases.
And on our dates it was not the cheaper choice. Three nights for 2 adults, 14–17 Dec 2026: Hotel Trend Asakusa Annex was ¥37,500 for a double; SORA Kaminarimon, about 250 m from exit A2b, was ¥36,845, both including taxes. The Ginza Line's Exit 1, which has a lift, is about 460 m from the Annex and about 100 m from SORA Kaminarimon.
Toei exit A2b to TX-side hotel
≈670 m
About 9 min on foot
Against ≈240 m from TX A1.
3 nights, 2 adults
¥655
The difference, the other way
Annex ¥37,500 vs SORA ¥36,845.
Suits: light packers, or anyone who will mostly use the TX. Not for: two big suitcases after a long flight, when a hotel near the Toei exits saves most of that walk.
Answer C · One arrival walk vs the next two mornings
Where the TX-side hotel earns its keep
Akihabara 5 min · Shibuya 35 min
Morning 2, Akihabara: from the TX station next door, our sample train left at 08:31 and reached Akihabara at 08:36, ¥230, with no change.
Morning 3, Shibuya: walk about 420 m to Tawaramachi on the Ginza Line and ride straight through: 08:31 to 09:06, ¥260. From the main Asakusa Ginza Line station it is 37 minutes, so the TX-side hotel loses nothing here.
Departure day: back to the Toei station for the Access Express. Our sample left Asakusa at 09:21 and reached Narita Terminal 1 at 10:32, ¥1,380, again with no change. That is the same 670 m walk, so the luggage penalty is paid twice.
TX Asakusa to Akihabara
5 min
¥230
Straight from the hotel's station.
Asakusa to Narita T1
71 min
¥1,380, no change
From the Toei station only.
Suits: trips built around Akihabara, or a day out to Tsukuba. If your days are mostly Asakusa itself, Ueno and the airport, the Toei side wins.
Our verdict
We suggest: from Narita, plan on the Access Express to the Toei Asakusa station and book within about 300 m of it (Kaminarimon or Azuma-bashi side) when you carry big bags, because the TX-side hotel adds about 670 m on both arrival and departure day and, on our dates, saved nothing. The answer changes when you will use the Tsukuba Express most mornings (Akihabara, Tsukuba) and travel light, or when the TX-side room is clearly cheaper on your own dates.
See hotels around Kaminarimon →Opens Booking.com. Check which Asakusa station each listing measures from.
Arriving before check-in? Radical Storage lists luggage spots around Asakusa, so you can see the temple first. Comparing airport trains in general? See which airport train into Tokyo.
One more thing: a drink where Asakusa started drinking
Come up at Ginza line Exit 3 (or Toei Asakusa line Exit A5) and the first door you pass is Kamiya Bar, open since 1880 and known as Japan's first Western-style bar. Order its own Denki Bran, a sweet brandy-based mix created here, with a draft beer on the side the way regulars do. It is loud, cheap and full of locals at the long tables, which is exactly the point after a long flight.
Kamiya Bar, 1-1-1 Asakusa. About 11:00–21:00, last order 20:30, closed Tuesdays; hours change, so check before you go. Sources: Time Out Tokyo and NAVITIME listings.

## "Five Minutes from Shinjuku Station": How Long Is It with a Suitcase?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-five-minutes-with-a-suitcase
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

"Five minutes" starts at one exit, not at your train. Hotel Gracery Shinjuku says 5 minutes from JR Shinjuku's East Exit, but with a suitcase from the Narita Express the lift route comes out at the south gates, about 1 km and 15–20 minutes from reception. The Narita Limousine Bus to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower stops about 200 m away: slower to Shinjuku, but almost no walk.
Traced for Hotel Gracery Shinjuku (Kabukicho) on Wed 16 Dec 2026 · operator pages and Jorudan, checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Narita Express, platform to reception
From the N'EX platform
≈1 km with lifts
Our sample N'EX left Narita Terminal 1 at 15:14 and reached Shinjuku at 16:41 (87 minutes, ¥3,330). It stops at platforms 5–6, and JR East's own note says the step-free route from there leads only to the New South, Koshu-kaido and Miraina Tower gates, at the south end of the station.
The hotel is at the north end, in Kabukicho. From the Busta Shinjuku side the street walk is about 970 m, roughly 13 minutes at a normal pace, before you even count the walk along the platform and through the gates. The route planner allows 12 minutes just from the JR platforms to Seibu-Shinjuku Station, which the hotel says is 3 minutes from its door. With a suitcase we would budget 15–20 minutes, then a lift: reception is on the 8th floor.
N'EX platforms
5–6
Lift route goes south
New South / Koshu-kaido / Miraina gates.
South gates to hotel
≈970 m
About 13 min walking
Plus the station itself.
Suits: light packers and hotels on the south or west side. A hotel such as Hotel Sunroute Plaza Shinjuku, which says 3 minutes from the South Exit and from Busta Shinjuku, fits this train far better than a Kabukicho address.
Answer B · The advertised exit, and the lift that gets you there
East Exit, or Metro Exit B11
≈450–470 m on the street
The advertised exit: from the JR East Exit plaza the street walk to the hotel is about 470 m, about 6 minutes. That is the "5 minutes", and it holds if you already stand at the East Exit.
The nearest step-free alternative: Tokyo Metro's Marunouchi Line station at Shinjuku lists a lift from the platform to its East Gate, and lifts from the East Gate up to Exits B11 and A6, from 6:00 to 23:00 only. From Exit B11 the street walk is about 450 m, along Kabukicho's Sakura-dori. Useful if you came in on the Marunouchi Line from Tokyo Station or Ginza; check which side your train arrives on, as the lift listed serves the platform towards Ikebukuro.
East Exit to hotel
≈470 m
The advertised 5 min
Street walk only.
Exit B11 lift
6–23 h
Marunouchi Line
About 450 m to the hotel.
Suits: arrivals by subway in the daytime. After 23:00 the Metro lifts are off, so plan on stairs or escalators.
Answer C · When a closer bus stop is worth a slower ride
Narita Limousine to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower
¥3,600 · ≈200 m walk
The Airport Limousine runs from Narita straight to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower, which the hotel says is about a 2-minute walk away (about 190 m on the street). On our sample timetable the bus left Terminal 1 at 15:40 and was due at 17:35: 115 minutes for ¥3,600, against 87 minutes and ¥3,330 by N'EX.
So the bus saves about 800 m of walking with your bags and every lift hunt, at the cost of about 30 minutes more on board and ¥270 more, and only if a departure fits your landing. If none does, the hotel suggests the buses to Busta Shinjuku, but from there it is the same 970 m walk as the train.
Suits: big suitcases, travellers with children or limited mobility, anyone landing tired. Not for: tight schedules, or when the next bus is more than about half an hour away.
Our verdict
We suggest: before booking, check which exit the "minutes" are counted from and match it to your airport transfer. For a Kabukicho hotel like Hotel Gracery Shinjuku with a big suitcase, take the Narita Limousine to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower when a departure is within about 30 minutes of clearing customs; otherwise take the N'EX and budget 15–20 minutes from platform to reception. If your hotel is near the South Exit or Busta Shinjuku instead, the N'EX's lift route ends right there and the train wins outright.
See hotels near Shinjuku's South Exit →Opens Booking.com. Check which exit each listing measures from.
Arriving before check-in? Leave the suitcase with Radical Storage near the station and walk the last kilometre light. Not sure which Shinjuku station to book near? See JR Shinjuku vs Shinjuku-sanchome vs Higashi-shinjuku.
One more thing: Memory Lane, once the bag is gone
Once the suitcase is at the hotel, walk back to the West Exit and duck into Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane). It started as a black market among the rubble around 1946 and is now a lane of tiny counters grilling yakitori and simmering nikomi stew, barely wide enough for two people. It's two minutes from the station and the best place to feel you've arrived in Tokyo.
Shinjuku Nishiguchi Omoide Yokocho, 1 Nishi-Shinjuku; about 2 min from JR Shinjuku West Exit. Hours and charges vary by shop. Sources: Omoide Yokocho official site (history), GLTJP (supervised by Omoide Yokocho), GO TOKYO.
