## Landing at Haneda at 11 p.m.: Book Central Tokyo or Sleep at the Airport?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/haneda-late-arrival-first-night
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If you land at 23:00 and have checked bags, we suggest sleeping at the airport the first night: Villa Fontaine Grand Haneda Airport, connected to Terminal 3, cost about ¥18,700 for two on our sample Wednesday, the same as a central business hotel. Book central Tokyo only if your hotel is on the Tokyo Monorail side (last train 00:10) or on the late-night bus route to Shinjuku.
Last trains for Wed 16 Dec 2026 from Jorudan · bus times from Airport Limousine · Booking.com prices for 2 adults, 16–17 Dec 2026, checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Train, if you are out fast
The last workable trains
23:37 to 00:10
After a 23:00 landing, immigration, bags and customs take time, so we plan on reaching the arrivals hall at about 23:45 at the earliest. Measured against that, on our sample weekday:
Asakusa
23:37
Keikyu, last train
Arrives 00:23. Usually missed after a 23:00 landing.
Shinjuku / Shibuya
23:51
Keikyu, change at Shinagawa
Shinjuku 00:41, Shibuya 00:33. Tight.
Tokyo Stn / Ueno
00:10
Tokyo Monorail
Hamamatsucho 00:26, Tokyo 00:38, Ueno 00:46.
After midnight the Monorail is the last train standing: 00:10 from Terminal 3.
Then add the walk from the station and check-in. A hotel near Hamamatsucho, such as HOTEL MYSTAYS Hamamatsucho (about ¥19,900 for two that night), is the safest central pick, because the Monorail ends right there at 00:26 with no change.
Suits: hand luggage only, a hotel on the Monorail side, or a flight that lands early. Not for: Asakusa hotels, or anyone who still needs to buy an IC card at midnight (see IC card or subway pass).
Answer B · After the trains, or two people sharing
Late-night bus or fixed-fare taxi
¥2,800 per person or ≈¥9,800 per car
The late-night Limousine Bus leaves Terminal 3 at 0:20, 1:00, 1:40 and 2:20 for Shinjuku Station West Exit (arriving 0:48 on the first bus), Busta Shinjuku, Higashi-shinjuku and Ikebukuro, for ¥2,800. It is the cheap answer if your hotel is near one of those stops.
Taxis at the Terminal 3 stand (1st floor) run on Haneda fixed fares, with a 20% late-night premium from 22:00 to 5:00 and expressway tolls on top (about ¥1,000). That comes to about ¥9,800 to Shinjuku, ¥9,200 to Shibuya, ¥8,300 to Tokyo Station's ward and ¥9,900 to Ueno and Asakusa. Split by two, that is roughly ¥5,000 each, door to door, at any hour.
Suits: two to four people with bags, or a Shinjuku/Ikebukuro hotel on the bus route. Check that your hotel has a 24-hour front desk before you arrive at 1 a.m.
Answer C · When sleeping at the airport is the practical choice
A hotel connected to Terminal 3
≈¥18,700 for two
Villa Fontaine Grand Haneda Airport is directly connected to Terminal 3 and its Booking.com listing shows a 24-hour front desk (rated 8.7; about ¥18,700 for two on Wed 16 Dec, run-of-house room). The Royal Park Hotel Tokyo Haneda, inside Terminal 3, was about ¥27,800. On the same night, comparable central rooms were about ¥19,200 (APA Hotel Shinjuku Kabukicho Tower) and ¥19,900 (HOTEL MYSTAYS Hamamatsucho), so the airport costs about the same and you skip the taxi.
Next morning: the first trains leave Terminal 3 at about 5:26, and you ride into the city in daylight with time to buy an IC card, store bags or go straight out sightseeing.
Airport hotel

Taxi saved
≈¥10,000
Shinjuku at night
Fixed fare + tolls, per car.
Sleep at the airport and you ride into town in daylight.
Sleeping at the airport is the practical choice when you land after about 22:30 with checked bags, are heading to Asakusa or the west side, or are travelling alone (no one to share a taxi with). It is not worth it with hand luggage and a Monorail-side hotel.
Our verdict
We suggest: for a 23:00 landing at Haneda, book Villa Fontaine Grand Haneda Airport for night one and start your central stay the next day. The answer changes if your central hotel is near Hamamatsucho, Tokyo Station or Ueno and you are out by midnight (take the 00:10 Monorail), if it sits on the late-night bus route to Shinjuku or Ikebukuro (¥2,800 at 0:20), or if two or more of you can share a taxi (about ¥5,000 each to Shinjuku). If your flight lands before about 22:30, go straight into town.
A late landing is easier when the first night is already sorted.
See hotels at Haneda Airport →Opens Booking.com. Check "connected to Terminal 3" and the front-desk hours on each listing.
Rather be met at arrivals? A pre-booked car through Welcome Pickups waits with a name sign, so there is no taxi queue after a late landing. For daytime arrivals, compare the lines in Narita or Haneda: which train.
One more thing: a hot spring above Terminal 3
If you decide to stay at the airport, Izumi Tenku no Yu on the 12th floor of the hotel block connected to Terminal 3 is open 24 hours. The men's bath looks out over the runways and the women's side faces Mount Fuji on clear days. A soak at 1 a.m. turns a late landing into the first good memory of the trip, and its restaurant is open around the clock too.
Izumi Tenku no Yu Haneda Airport, connected to Terminal 3. Baths close for cleaning roughly 10:00–12:30/13:00; hotel guests get priority when it is full. Check the current fee on the official site. Sources: official site (Sumitomo Fudosan), Time Out Tokyo.

## Narita In, Three Nights, Then the Shinkansen: Ueno, Tokyo Station or Shinagawa?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/narita-three-nights-then-shinkansen
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For most travellers we suggest Ueno. The Skyliner runs there from Narita in as little as 41 minutes, three nights for two cost about ¥41,000–50,000 on our sample dates, and departure morning only adds about 13 minutes on the way to Kyoto. Tokyo Station saves those minutes but cost about twice as much. Shinagawa wins when your sightseeing days are around Shibuya and the west side.
Booking.com prices for 2 adults, Mon 14–Thu 17 Dec 2026 (3 nights), checked 23 November 2026 · train times from Keisei, JR East and Jorudan
Answer A · Best value for this exact trip
Ueno
3 nights from ≈¥41,000
Arrival: the Skyliner goes straight from Narita to Keisei Ueno in as little as 41 minutes for ¥2,470, with every seat reserved. Keisei Ueno is a separate station from JR Ueno: the route planner allows about 9 minutes on foot between them, so pick a hotel on the Keisei side if you can. On our dates, well-rated hotels within 400 m came to about ¥41,300 (HOTEL LiVEMAX Ueno-Ekimae, rated 7.6), ¥45,800 (APA Hotel Ueno Ekikita, 8.0) and ¥49,700 (Ueno Touganeya Hotel, 8.8) for all three nights.
Departure morning: Ueno to Kyoto took 2 hours 28 minutes on our sample 9:00 search: 5 minutes on the Ueno-Tokyo Line, a 10-minute change at Tokyo Station, then the Nozomi. That is 13 minutes longer than starting at Tokyo Station, with one change and your bags.
Narita to Ueno
41 min
Skyliner, ¥2,470
Fastest service, to Keisei Ueno.
Ueno to Kyoto
2:28
One change at Tokyo
+13 min vs starting at Tokyo Station.
Suits: budget-minded couples, museum and Asakusa days. Not for: anyone who wants zero changes with luggage on departure day. Shibuya is 30 minutes away on the Ginza Line.
Answer B · Walk to the platform
Tokyo Station
3 nights from ≈¥84,000
Arrival: the Narita Express reaches Tokyo Station in 53 minutes at its fastest for ¥3,140 (our sample afternoon train took 60 minutes). Departure: the Tokaido Shinkansen starts here, so the 9:00 Nozomi reached Kyoto at 11:15 with no change.
The catch is the room. On the same three nights, the cheapest well-rated hotels within 700 m were lyf Ginza Tokyo (8.8, 700 m) at about ¥83,600, remm Tokyo Kyobashi (8.7, 600 m) at about ¥88,700 and Super Hotel Premier Tokyo Station Yaesu-Chuoguchi (8.4, 400 m) at about ¥98,500. That is about ¥28,000–33,000 a night, roughly double Ueno, to save 13 minutes once.

Suits: an early Shinkansen with heavy bags, travellers with mobility needs, or a trip where comfort beats budget. Not for: three nights on a normal budget.
Answer C · When your days are on the west side
Shinagawa
3 nights from ≈¥59,000
Arrival: the Narita Express continues past Tokyo Station to Shinagawa; our sample train took 71 minutes, for ¥3,330. Departure: the same Nozomi leaves Shinagawa 7 minutes after Tokyo, so Shinagawa to Kyoto was 2 hours 8 minutes, the shortest of the three.
The sightseeing day: Shibuya is 13 minutes away on the Yamanote Line, against 18 minutes from Tokyo Station (one change) and 30 from Ueno. Rooms sat in the middle: Shinagawa Prince Hotel N Tower (7.9, twin with light breakfast) about ¥58,900, Shinagawa Tobu Hotel (8.1) about ¥62,300 and Miyako City Tokyo Takanawa (8.8) about ¥64,000 for three nights.
Shinagawa to Kyoto

To Shibuya

Yamanote Line

Shinagawa wins this itinerary: Narita in, a Shibuya / Harajuku / Shinjuku day and a Meiji Jingu morning, then the Nozomi out. Not for: an Asakusa- and Ueno-heavy plan, or the lowest price.
Our verdict
We suggest: stay in Ueno, close to Keisei Ueno. On our sample dates it saved about ¥40,000 over three nights compared with Tokyo Station, and cost about 13 minutes on departure morning. The answer changes in two cases: if two or more of your days are around Shibuya and the west side, book Shinagawa (about ¥18,000 more than Ueno for three nights, but 13 minutes to Shibuya and the shortest ride to Kyoto). If you have a very early train, very heavy bags or limited mobility, Tokyo Station's no-change departure is worth paying for on the last night only.
See hotels near Ueno →Opens Booking.com. Check the distance to Keisei Ueno on each listing.
Prefer the west side? See hotels near Shinagawa. Still choosing your first area? Start with where to stay on a first Tokyo trip, and match the airport train in Narita or Haneda: which train.
One more thing: Tokyo Station from above, free
Whichever base you choose, before your Shinkansen leaves, cross from the Marunouchi South Exit to KITTE and take the lift to the 6th-floor rooftop garden. It looks straight down on the red-brick station building and the bullet trains sliding in and out, and it costs nothing. Go at dusk, when the station lights come on.
KITTE Garden, KITTE Marunouchi 6F, about 1 min from Tokyo Station Marunouchi South Exit. Free; open until about 23:00 (22:00 Sundays and holidays); may close in bad weather; no tripods. Sources: GO TOKYO, nightscape.tokyo.

## Kiyosumi-Shirakawa: Garden, MOT Museum or a Free Walk?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kiyosumi-shirakawa-what-to-pay-for
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

The one thing worth paying for on a sunny morning is Kiyosumi Gardens. It costs ¥150, opens at 9:00 and is 3 minutes from Exit A3. A full loop of the pond takes about 40 minutes. After it, walk free to Kiba Park. On a rainy afternoon, pick the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo (MOT), but check the date first. Its two big paid shows end on 6 and 13 December 2026. On our sample date, Wednesday 16 December, only the ¥500 MOT Collection is on, and it is free for visitors aged 65 and over because it is the third Wednesday of the month.
Prices, hours and exhibitions from the Tokyo Metropolitan Park Association, MOT and GO TOKYO · sample date Wed 16 December 2026 · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Worth the ¥150
Kiyosumi Gardens, once round the pond
9:00–17:00 · last entry 16:30
Kiyosumi Gardens is a strolling garden built around a large pond, 3 minutes from Exit A3 of Kiyosumi-shirakawa Station (Toei Oedo Line and Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line). Admission is ¥150, or ¥70 for visitors aged 65 and over. Primary-school children and younger go free. The park association says a full loop takes about 40 minutes. The only uneven parts are the iso-watari, stepping stones set apart along the pond's edge. They are optional, and the path beside them carries on. The association's FAQ says half of the pond loop is a flat wheelchair route and that four wheelchairs are available to borrow. A free garden guide walk runs on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays at 11:00 and 14:00 (the language isn't stated). The garden closes from 29 December to 1 January.
Admission
¥150
¥70 for 65+
Primary-school age and younger free. Closed 29 Dec–1 Jan.
Pond loop
≈40 min
Half of it a flat wheelchair route
Stepping stones on the edge are optional.
Suits: a calm morning, photographers, and parents who want a short loop with benches. Not for: picnics. Picnic sheets and alcohol brought in are not allowed, though you can eat on the benches.
Answer B · Depends on the date
Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo
10:00–18:00 · closed Mon
MOT sits inside Kiba Park, about 9 minutes from Exit B2 (Hanzomon Line) or about 13 minutes from Exit A3 (Oedo Line). It opens 10:00–18:00, and the last tickets are sold 30 minutes before closing. It is closed on Mondays and from 28 December to 1 January. What your ticket buys depends on the day. "Tada Minami―Still, shimmering light" runs until 6 December 2026 (adult ¥1,600). "Synchronic Constellation: Cross-Boundary Perspectives in Art" runs until 13 December (adult ¥2,000). Both tickets include the MOT Collection. From 14 December only "MOT Collection: Past Light, Present Sight" is listed, until 6 January 2027. It costs ¥500 for adults and ¥250 for visitors aged 65 and over, and is free for 65+ on the third Wednesday of each month. On 16 December that means a small, cheap visit rather than a major show.
On 16 Dec 2026
¥500
MOT Collection only
Free for 65+ that day (third Wednesday).
Until 13 Dec
¥2,000
Synchronic Constellation
Includes the Collection. Tada Minami (¥1,600) closes 6 Dec.
Suits: rainy afternoons, and contemporary-art fans visiting before 13 December. Not for: Mondays, or anyone expecting a major exhibition after 13 December.
Answer C · Free
River bridge, then Kiba Park
always open
For a free walk, start at Exit A3 and walk to Kiyosu Bridge over the Sumida River. GO TOKYO gives the walk as 5 to 7 minutes, depending on the page. Then turn back east past the garden entrance and continue to Kiba Park. MOT puts its building, inside the park, about 13 minutes on foot from Exit A3. The Tokyo Metropolitan Park Association lists Kiba Park as always open and about 238,711 m² in size. Its landmark is Kiba Park Bridge, a 250 m cable-stayed bridge. If the weather turns, the museum is right there.
Kiba Park
24 h
Always open, free
About 238,711 m². MOT stands inside it.
Exit A3 to MOT
≈13 min
On foot
Kiyosu Bridge is 5–7 min the other way.
Suits: travellers on a tight budget, and families who need space to run around. Not for: anyone wanting a classic Japanese garden. Kiba Park is a large public park, not a landscaped pond garden.
Our verdict
We suggest: on a sunny morning, Kiyosumi Gardens at 9:00 (¥150), then walk free through to Kiba Park. On a rainy afternoon, MOT from 10:00 to 18:00, but check the date. Up to 13 December 2026, pay for Synchronic Constellation (¥2,000), which includes the Collection. From 14 December only the ¥500 Collection is on, so treat it as a short stop. Older visitors get in free on the third Wednesday (16 December). Avoid Mondays, when MOT is closed. Between 29 December and 1 January the garden and the museum are both shut, so the free walk is your only option.
One more thing: ¥400 for a whole Edo street
If you pay for one more thing here, make it the Fukagawa Edo Museum, three minutes from the station. Inside is a life-size copy of this exact neighbourhood around 1840, with shops, a fire lookout and tenement houses you can step into, take off your shoes in and photograph. Volunteer guides, some of whom speak English, explain what you're looking at. It feels like a film set, and it costs less than a coffee.
Koto City Fukagawa Edo Museum, 1-3-28 Shirakawa; about 3 min from Kiyosumi-shirakawa Exit A3. 9:30–17:00 (last entry 16:30); closed 2nd and 4th Mondays and at New Year; about ¥400. Sources: GO TOKYO, LIVE JAPAN, visiting-japan.com.

## Itami Sky Park: Can You Watch Planes Without a Car?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/itami-sky-park-without-a-car
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Yes, and it's cheap. Take the Hankyu line from Osaka-umeda to Itami (21 minutes, ¥240), then Itami City Bus route 25 for 8 minutes (¥250) to the "Itami Sky Park / Kamisuko" stop. The park is free and open 9:00–21:00 in winter. We suggest a loop, though. Go out via Hotarugaike and the monorail to the free observation deck at Osaka Airport. Then ride the same route 25 bus 8 minutes from the airport to Sky Park, and head back to Umeda through Hankyu Itami. You see planes from both sides for ¥1,180 in total, with no backtracking.
Fares and timetables from Hankyu, Itami City Bus, Osaka Monorail, Osaka Airport and Itami Sky Park · sample date Wed 16 December 2026 · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Cheapest
Hankyu to Itami, then city bus 25
¥490 each way
On Hankyu's route search for Wednesday 16 December, the 12:31 from Osaka-umeda reached Itami at 12:52, with one change at Tsukaguchi (¥240). Itami City Bus route 25 ("via Kamitsu, for Osaka Airport") leaves from stop 6 outside the station. On the weekday timetable it ran at 13:18 and 13:48, roughly every 25–30 minutes at midday. Allow for up to half an hour's wait. The 13:18 reaches the Itami Sky Park / Kamisuko stop at 13:26. The fare is ¥250, paid when you board, so have coins ready. Routes 22/23 (Iwaya loop) from the same stop also serve the park. Coming back, route 25 leaves the Sky Park stop for Hankyu Itami and JR Itami twice an hour, with the last bus at 22:03. The park itself is 1.2 km long and runs beside the runway. It has North, Central and South entrances, six toilets, and a take-out café at the Central Entrance.
Umeda to the park
¥490
21 min train + 8 min bus
Plus the wait for the bus: about every 25–30 min at weekday midday.
Last bus back
22:03
Route 25 to Hankyu Itami
Weekdays and weekends. The park closes at 21:00.
Suits: budget travellers, families, and anyone happy to check a bus timetable. Not for: a tight schedule. Missing a bus costs up to 30 minutes.
Answer B · Fastest out
Hankyu to Itami, taxi to the park, bus back
about ¥1,100 taxi
A taxi from Hankyu Itami skips the bus wait. On an OpenStreetMap route estimate, the drive to the park's address is about 2.1 km. Itami falls in the Kobe taxi-fare area. The upper-limit fare there is ¥700 for the first 1.3 km and ¥100 for every 225 m after that, so expect about ¥1,100 on the meter. Fares vary slightly by company. The return trip is the weak point. Neither the park nor the city lists a taxi rank at Sky Park, so plan to come back on route 25 (¥250 to Hankyu Itami). That makes about ¥1,830 for the round trip from Umeda, against ¥980 by bus both ways.
Taxi, Hankyu Itami to park
≈¥1,100
About 2.1 km
Upper-limit Kobe-area fare. Saves the wait of up to 30 min.
Way back
Bus
No taxi rank listed at the park
Route 25 from the Sky Park stop, ¥250.
Suits: a group of three or four sharing the fare, or anyone who has just missed a bus. Not for: solo budget trips. The taxi alone costs more than the whole round trip by bus.
Answer C · Easiest
Osaka Airport observation deck
free · ¥440 from Umeda
If you mainly want to watch takeoffs and landings, the airport's own deck is the easiest choice. Take a Hankyu express from Osaka-umeda to Hotarugaike (13 minutes, ¥240). Then ride the Osaka Monorail one stop to Osaka Airport (¥200, 1.4 km). The deck is on the 4th floor of the terminal. Entry is free and it is open every day. At the time of checking, the airport listed hours of 6:00–21:30, with last entry at 21:00. The airport describes views of aircraft up close and of the runways at night. It may close without notice for weather or security. The terminal's shops and cafés are right below you. Flights at Itami run from 7:00 to 21:00.
Umeda to the deck
¥440
Hankyu 13 min + monorail 1 stop
No bus, no wait for a connection.
Deck hours now
6:00–21:30
Last entry 21:00 · free
Open every day. May close for weather or security.
Suits: short visits, grandparents, cold or wet days when you want the terminal close by, and early starts before Sky Park opens. Not for: the low, under-the-approach angle that the park beside the runway gives you.
Our verdict
We suggest: a loop. Go Osaka-umeda → Hotarugaike → monorail to the airport deck. Then take city bus 25 from Osaka Airport stop 7 to Sky Park (8 minutes), and finally bus 25 to Hankyu Itami and the train back to Umeda. That's ¥1,180, and you never ride the same leg twice. The answer changes with time and weather. With only an hour or two, or in rain, stay on the deck (¥440 each way). With three or four people and a missed bus, take the taxi from Hankyu Itami for the way out only. In winter Sky Park opens at 9:00. From April to October it opens at 7:00 on weekends and holidays. Either way, leave the park by about 22:00 to catch the 22:03 last bus.
One more thing: beer in a 240-year-old sake brewery
Itami is one of the places Japanese sake was born, and five minutes from JR Itami Station you can eat inside that history at Shirayuki Brewery Restaurant Choujugura. The building is a sake brewery more than 240 years old, run by Konishi, a brewer founded in 1550, and it now also brews its own KONISHI craft beer on site. Lunch sets are around ¥1,500, there is an English menu, and cards are accepted.
Shirayuki Brewery Restaurant Choujugura, about 5 min walk from JR Itami Station. Lunch 11:30–14:00; closed Tuesdays; check hours before you go. Sources: Gurunavi listing, Rurubu.

## Yanaka Ginza: Which Way Should You Walk With Your Parents?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/yanaka-ginza-which-direction
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Start at JR Nippori and finish at Sendagi. From Nippori you reach the Yuyake Dandan steps first and walk down them into the shopping street. GO TOKYO calls them the staircase "leading down" to the street. Then stroll the 170 m street and carry on to Tokyo Metro Sendagi Station, which has a lift down to the platform. If you walk the other way, the same steps come at the very end, going up. If anyone in your group should avoid stairs completely, start and finish at Sendagi and turn round before the steps.
Routes and facilities from the Yanaka Ginza association, GO TOKYO, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Tokyo Metro and Toei · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Start at Nippori
Down the steps first, then the whole street
about 5 min to the street
Leave JR Nippori on the west side. GO TOKYO says to take the North West Exit and follow the main road along the edge of Yanaka Cemetery towards Yanaka Ginza. The association puts the street 5 minutes on foot from Nippori. The descent starts at Yuyake Dandan, the staircase at the top of the street. GO TOKYO says the shops begin about 1 minute below it. One thing to watch: the Tokyo government's accessible-route guide notes that the street at the top of Yuyake Dandan slopes toward the stairs, so take the first step slowly. At the bottom, Yanaka Ginza runs for about 170 m with about 60 shops. Keep walking straight to Yomise-dori and turn towards Sendagi Station. The association puts Sendagi 5 minutes from the street too.
The street
170 m
About 60 shops
Association figures. Each shop sets its own hours.
Steps
Down
At the start, not the end
Yuyake Dandan sits between the Nippori side and the street. The top of the steps slopes towards them.
Suits: parents who can manage one flight of outdoor steps going down, and anyone who wants the classic view from the top first. Not for: wheelchairs, strollers, or anyone who can't use stairs at all. See Answer C.
Answer B · Start at Sendagi
The same street in reverse ends with a climb
steps come last
Starting at Tokyo Metro Sendagi (Chiyoda Line) is easy at first. GO TOKYO lists the Dokanyama-side exit as 3 minutes from the street, and the association says 5 minutes. You walk along Yomise-dori and enter Yanaka Ginza from its lower end. The catch is at the far end. To get to Nippori from there you go up Yuyake Dandan, with tired legs and shopping bags. That climb is the end of the outing this brief is trying to avoid. Reverse order makes sense only if you plan to come back the same way to Sendagi, or if lunch near Sendagi is fixed for the start of the day.
Sendagi to the street
3–5 min
GO TOKYO 3 min, association 5 min
Along Yomise-dori. GO TOKYO names the Dokanyama-side exit.
Finish
Up
Yuyake Dandan to Nippori
The last part of the walk is the climb.
Suits: an out-and-back visit from Sendagi, or a group that wants to finish at JR Nippori for the Yamanote or Keisei lines and doesn't mind the climb. Not for: parents who tire easily at the end of a walk.
Answer C · Step-free
Sendagi lift, Yomise-dori, turn round before the steps
no stairs
For a stroller, a wheelchair or anyone avoiding stairs, use Sendagi in both directions. Tokyo Metro lists a lift from platforms 1 and 2 to a dedicated lift gate. The Tokyo government's accessible-route guide places it between Exits 1 and 2, and the ecomo barrier-free guide places it near the Dangozaka-shita bus stop. From there, walk Yomise-dori into Yanaka Ginza, browse to the foot of Yuyake Dandan, and come back the same way. The government guide warns that Yomise-dori has no sidewalk, so keep to the side. Its alternative from Nippori starts at the East Exit, which JR serves with a lift from the North Gate. That route passes Kannonji Temple and Yanaka Cemetery, where the road down to Yomise-dori runs downhill for about 300 m. It is longer, on narrow roads with cars. The guide also mentions the Taito City "Megurin" loop bus from Yanaka Cemetery towards Yanaka Ginza and Yomise-dori.
Sendagi Station
Lift
Platform to a lift-only gate
Between Exits 1 and 2, on the Dangozaka side. Accessible toilets inside the gates.
Lunch
11:00
Restaurant Ryu, 1 min from Exit 1
Western-style lunch sets 11:00–15:00, last order 14:00. Closed Wed and Thu (per its listings).
Suits: strollers, wheelchairs, and anyone who wants a short, flat outing that finishes at a station with a lift. Not for: seeing the view from the top of Yuyake Dandan. You see the steps from below. Restaurant Ryu's hours come from its Gurunavi and Hot Pepper listings, not its own site. The listing says closing days may change, so check before you go.
Our verdict
We suggest: JR Nippori → down Yuyake Dandan → Yanaka Ginza → Yomise-dori → Tokyo Metro Sendagi. Plan to sit down for lunch near Sendagi around 11:30–13:30. The answer changes if anyone can't use stairs at all. Then start and finish at Sendagi with the lift and turn round at the foot of the steps. If you must finish at Nippori for a JR or Keisei train, accept the climb, or take the longer step-free Nippori East Exit route. On Wednesdays and Thursdays our lunch pick is closed, so choose another place on the street.
One more thing: breakfast in a 1938 coffee house
Start at the Nezu end and you pass Kayaba Coffee, a kissaten (old-style coffee house) that opened in 1938 in a wooden house from the 1910s. Order the egg sandwich and the "Russian", coffee mixed with cocoa, the way regulars have for decades. There's tatami seating upstairs if your parents want to sit on the floor the old way.
Kayaba Coffee, 6-1-29 Yanaka, Taito-ku; between Nezu and Nippori stations. Opens at 8:00; hours vary by source, so check before you go. Busy at weekends. Sources: Time Out Tokyo, LIVE JAPAN, Taito Historical and Cultural Society (taireki.com).

## Monzen-nakacho: Is Market Day the Best Day to Visit?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/monzen-nakacho-market-day
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For a quiet morning, skip market day. Come on a Tuesday to Friday that is not the 1st, 15th or 28th. Those three dates are fair days at both the shrine and the temple, and Koto City calls them very busy. Sundays bring the antique market to Tomioka Hachimangu: 6, 13 and 27 December 2026. Go on a market day only if browsing antiques is the reason for your visit. Mondays are quiet too, but the shrine-grounds lunch spot, Fukagawa Juku, is closed.
Times and dates from Fukagawa Fudoson, Koto City, GO TOKYO, the market organiser and Koto tourism · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Market morning
Sunday antique market at Tomioka Hachimangu
6, 13, 27 Dec · from 6:00
The Tomioka Hachimangu antique market, run by the organiser Rakuichi Rakuza, takes place on the 1st (except January), 2nd, 4th and 5th Sundays of each month, 6:00–17:00. It is not held when one of those Sundays falls on the 15th or the 28th. In December 2026, that gives Sundays 6, 13 and 27 December. The organiser says about 140 stalls line both sides of the shrine approach. They sell ceramics, kimono, glassware and toys, and old postcards and paper items are popular. Entry is free and the market goes ahead in light rain. From Exit 1 of Monzen-nakacho Station (Tozai Line), turn left and walk about 150 m to the shrine's torii gate.
December 2026
6 · 13 · 27
Sundays, 6:00–17:00
No market on 20 Dec, the 3rd Sunday. Free entry.
Stalls
≈140
Organiser's figure
Ceramics, kimono, glass, toys, postcards and paper items. Held in light rain.
Suits: collectors and anyone who enjoys browsing secondhand ceramics and kimono. Not for: a quiet shrine visit. On market Sundays the approach is lined with stalls.
Answer B · Ordinary weekday
Temple, shrine, then a fukagawa-meshi lunch
Tue–Fri · goma at 9:00
Fukagawa Fudoson's gates open at 8:00. Exit 1 of Monzen-nakacho Station on the Tozai Line is 2 minutes away; on the Oedo Line, use Exit 6 (5 minutes). The approach street to the temple is about 150 m long. The goma fire ritual takes place every day at 9:00, 11:00, 13:00, 15:00 and 17:00, and GLTJP says visitors can attend for free. The inner hall opens at 9:00, and its 4th floor shows a ceiling painting of Dainichi Nyorai over a lotus pond, which the temple calls one of the largest in Japan. Next door, the grounds of Tomioka Hachimangu are open 24 hours, and the shrine office opens 9:00–17:00. Finish at Fukagawa Juku, inside the shrine grounds, for fukagawa-meshi (clams in a miso broth over rice). Weekday lunch runs from 11:00 with last orders at 14:30. It has 30 seats and is closed on Mondays.
Goma fire ritual
9:00
Then 11:00, 13:00, 15:00, 17:00
Daily. Temple gates 8:00–18:00. Inner hall from 9:00.
Weekday lunch
11:00
Fukagawa Juku, last order 14:30
Inside Tomioka Hachimangu. Closed Mondays, unless it is the 15th or 28th.
Suits: a slow morning, travellers who want to watch a ritual, and parents or anyone who prefers a calm visit. Not for: Mondays if you want this lunch. Also avoid the 1st, 15th and 28th if quiet is the point.
Answer C · Weekend without a market
Saturdays and the 3rd Sunday
lunch L.O. 16:30
If your free day falls on a weekend, Saturdays and the 3rd Sunday (20 December 2026) have no antique market. The temple keeps the same 8:00–18:00 gate hours and the same goma times on weekends. For a food-focused visit, the weekend works well at lunch: Fukagawa Juku serves from 11:00 with last orders at 16:30 and no afternoon break, so you can eat late. We could not confirm weekend morning hours for the other shops on the approach street from an official source. Plan the temple and shrine for the morning and eat from 11:00.
Weekend lunch
11:00–16:30
Last order 16:30
Fukagawa Juku Tomioka Hachiman branch. 20 table seats and 10 tatami seats.
No market
20 Dec
3rd Sunday of December
Every Saturday is market-free too. Check that the date isn't the 1st, 15th or 28th.
Suits: food-focused travellers who want a late lunch. Not for: anyone counting on early-morning snacks on the street. Those hours are unconfirmed.
Our verdict
We suggest: a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday that is not the 1st, 15th or 28th. Arrive at Fukagawa Fudoson for the 9:00 goma, walk over to Tomioka Hachimangu, and sit down at Fukagawa Juku when it opens at 11:00. The answer changes with the calendar. If antiques are why you are coming, pick a market Sunday (6, 13 or 27 December 2026). If you can only come on a weekend and care most about food, choose Saturday or 20 December and enjoy the 16:30 last order. Avoid Mondays for lunch here unless it is the 15th or 28th.
One more thing: the crystal corridor inside Fudodo
Most people watch the fire ritual and leave, but look for the corridor inside Fukagawa Fudodo's main hall, the Inori no Kairo (prayer corridor). Its walls are lined with about 10,000 small crystal stupas, each holding a tiny Fudo figure, and they glow when the light catches them. It's free, and photos are not allowed inside, so it stays a quiet surprise.
Naritasan Fukagawa Fudodo, 1-17-13 Tomioka, Koto-ku; about 2 min from Monzen-nakacho (Tozai line). Open 8:00–18:00 daily, free. No photography inside the hall. Sources: GLTJP (facility-verified), Rurubu.

## Is NIFREL Worth a Two-Hour Trip?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/nifrel-two-hours
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If you are already at Expo City, two hours is more than enough. NIFREL itself suggests 1 to 1.5 hours, so you can take it slowly. If your two hours have to cover the whole trip from central Osaka, it gets tight. From Umeda, the trains take about an hour there and back, which leaves roughly 50 minutes inside. From Namba, you would get less than 30 minutes, which is not worth a ¥2,400 ticket. In that case, we suggest the Osaka Museum of Housing and Living, three minutes from Higashi-Umeda (¥600).
Hours and prices from NIFREL's official site · routes and fares from Ekitan · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Already at Expo City
Two hours inside: enough to go slowly
¥2,400 · 1–1.5 h suggested
NIFREL calls itself a "living museum" of live animals. It suggests 1 to 1.5 hours for a visit, or about 2.5 hours if you take your time. There is no time limit once you are in, and you can re-enter the same day until one hour before closing. In November and December 2026, it opens 10:00–18:00 on weekdays (last entry 17:00) and 9:30–19:00 on weekends and holidays (last entry 18:00). On 19, 20 and 24–27 December, day visits end at 17:00 because of a night event, which needs its own web-only ticket. Tickets cost ¥2,400 for adults and ¥1,200 for elementary and junior-high students. Entry is timed: on weekdays it is capped hour by hour until 15:00, and on weekends every 15 minutes all day.
Adult ticket
¥2,400
Children ¥1,200 · age 3+ ¥700
Same price online. Web tickets go on sale 30 days ahead.
Quieter after
15:00
NIFREL's own advice
It is busiest just after opening and in the early afternoon. Weekday last entry is 17:00.
Suits: families and anyone already shopping at Expo City or visiting Expo '70 Commemorative Park. Not for: anyone hoping to arrive after last entry. Weekday last entry is 17:00, and on the December night-event days the day visit ends at 17:00.
Answer B · Two hours from central Osaka
The full round trip, counted
≈1 h of trains from Umeda
NIFREL is in Expo City, about a 2-minute walk from Bampaku-kinen-koen station on the Osaka Monorail. From Osaka-umeda, take the Hankyu Kyoto Line to Minami-Ibaraki, then change to the monorail. It costs ¥530 each way, and our sample search took 31 minutes out (including a 7-minute wait for the monorail) and 30 minutes back. From Namba, take the Midosuji Line, which continues as the Kita-Osaka Kyuko to Senri-Chuo, then the monorail. That costs ¥680 each way and took about 43 minutes. Add the walks inside Umeda or Namba station and to the entrance, and a two-hour window leaves roughly 50 minutes inside from Umeda, or under 30 minutes from Namba.
From Umeda
≈50 min

From Namba
<30 min
Left inside NIFREL
Midosuji Line + Kita-Osaka Kyuko + monorail. ¥680 each way, about 43 min.
Suits: a quick look from Umeda if you go after 15:00 on a weekday, when the time slots are no longer capped. Not for: a two-hour window from Namba. You would spend more time on trains than inside.
Answer C · Closer, if two hours is everything
Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
¥600 · 3 min from Higashi-Umeda
This museum is on the 8th floor of a building directly connected to Exit 3 of Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome station. Its main exhibit is a detailed indoor recreation of an Osaka town from 1830–1844, and the scenery changes with the time of day. The Tanimachi Line from Higashi-Umeda takes 3 minutes (¥190). From Namba it is about 16 minutes with one change at Nippombashi (¥240). It opens 10:00–17:00 (last entry 16:30) and is closed on Tuesdays and from 29 December to 3 January. Adult tickets cost ¥600. The building faces the Tenjinbashisuji shopping street.
Adults
¥600
High school and university ¥300

Open
10:00–17:00

Suits: rainy days, a short break between plans in Umeda, and anyone who likes old streets. Not for: Tuesdays, or children who mainly want to see animals.
Our verdict
We suggest: go to NIFREL when you can spend at least two hours on the whole outing from Umeda, and more from Namba. Ideally that means a weekday after 15:00, when NIFREL says it is calmer and entry is no longer capped. The answer changes with your starting point and the clock. If two hours must cover everything from Namba, or you would arrive after the 17:00 weekday last entry, skip NIFREL that day and go to the Housing and Living museum instead (not on Tuesdays). If you are already at Expo City, two hours inside is plenty.
Search NIFREL tickets on Klook →Opens Klook. NIFREL's own counter price is ¥2,400 for adults.
One more thing: go inside the Tower of the Sun
Across the monorail from NIFREL, the Tower of the Sun isn't just for photos: since 2018 you can go inside Taro Okamoto's 70 m tower, up past the huge "Tree of Life" sculpture that has stood in it since Expo '70. Entry is by timed reservation, so book online before you leave Osaka. Reviewers say it's completely different from seeing it outside.
Tower of the Sun Museum, Expo '70 Commemorative Park; about 10 min walk from Bampaku-kinen-koen monorail station. 10:00–17:00 (last entry 16:30), closed Wednesdays. ¥720 plus park entry (about ¥260). Reserve up to 120 days ahead, pay by card. Sources: official Tower of the Sun site, osaka-info.jp, Time Out Osaka.

## Three Nights on ¥30,000: Namba or Tennoji Before a Kansai Airport Flight?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/namba-or-tennoji-30000-yen
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For three evenings around Dotonbori, we suggest Namba. On the weeknights we checked, a well-rated private room near Tennoji was ¥1,403 cheaper. Once we added the airport trains and the subway to Dotonbori and back each evening, Namba came out ¥217 cheaper: ¥16,681 against ¥16,898. You also walk home after dinner instead of watching the clock for a 00:17 last train. Both bases leave more than ¥13,000 of a ¥30,000 budget. Tennoji wins when your evenings are not in Dotonbori, or when it is clearly cheaper on your dates.
Booking.com prices for 1 adult, Mon 14–Thu 17 Dec 2026 (3 nights), taxes included, checked 23 November 2026 · fares and train times from Nankai and Ekitan
Answer A · Built around the airport
Tennoji: the cheapest room, a direct JR line
¥13,338 · 3 nights
The cheapest private room we found within 1 km of Tennoji Station, rated 8 or higher, was an economy double at Smile Hotel Osaka Tennoji: ¥13,338 for all three nights, taxes included. It is 0.6 km from the station and rated 8.0 from 613 reviews. From Tennoji, the JR Kansai Airport Rapid runs straight to the airport for ¥1,060. Our sample journey took about 48 minutes. On Thursday 17 December, the first direct train leaves at 05:25 and reaches Kansai Airport at 06:10. Dotonbori is a 6-minute Midosuji Line ride away (¥240). The last train back from Namba on a weekday in December leaves at 00:17.
Room, 3 nights
¥13,338
Smile Hotel Osaka Tennoji
Economy double, 0.6 km from Tennoji Station, 8.0 rating. Taxes included.
To the airport
¥1,060
JR Kansai Airport Rapid
No change of train. About 48 min. First direct train 05:25 on 17 Dec.
Suits: days spent around Tennoji, Abeno and Shinsekai, and evenings that end before midnight. Not for: late nights in Dotonbori. After the 00:17 last train, the only way back is a taxi.
Answer B · Evenings around Dotonbori
Namba: walk home, cheapest airport train
¥14,741 · 3 nights
Using the same filters near Osaka Namba Station, the cheapest room was an economy single at Toho Hotel Namba Motomachi. It costs ¥12,184 plus ¥2,557 in taxes and fees, so ¥14,741 for three nights. It is 0.6 km from the station and rated 8.4 from 1,816 reviews. If you want a double bed, APA Hotel Namba Shinsaibashi Higashi was ¥17,918 (0.9 km, 8.3). Nankai's Airport Express from Namba costs ¥970 and needs no change. Our sample journey took about 43 minutes. On 17 December the first train reaches the airport at 05:58. The Rapi:t limited express is faster, from 34 minutes, and adds a ¥700 seat ticket (¥550 if you buy it through Nankai's online ticketless service).

Answer C · The complete stays, priced
Room + airport both ways + three evenings out
¥30,000 budget
Sample itinerary: arrive and depart at Kansai Airport by train, and spend three evenings around Dotonbori. From Tennoji that adds six Midosuji Line rides at ¥240 each. From Namba you walk. Neither base needs a late-night taxi, as long as Tennoji guests catch the 00:17 last train.

The ¥217 gap is small and prices change daily. Several hotels near both stations showed temporary "Black Friday" discounts on 23 November, so we left those out of the totals. Search your own dates before you decide.
Our verdict
We suggest: base yourself in Namba for an itinerary with evenings around Dotonbori. On our dates it cost ¥217 less, the airport train is cheaper with no change, and you walk home after dinner. Choose Tennoji if your evenings are around Tennoji, Abeno or Shinsekai. Choose it too if, on your dates, its room is more than about ¥1,620 cheaper than Namba's: that is what six subway rides and the extra airport fare add up to. If you will be out in Dotonbori after 00:17, stay in Namba either way.

One more thing: Abeno Harukas' free sky garden
If you stay in Tennoji, you don't need the paid observation deck for a view. Take the shuttle lift to the 16th floor of Abeno Harukas, where the open-air garden, about 80 m up, is free. Office workers eat lunch there, and it is lit up at night.
Abeno Harukas 16F garden, next to JR Tennoji and Kintetsu Osaka-Abenobashi stations; the 16th floor is a free zone, while the 58–60F HARUKAS 300 deck is paid. Sources: Rurubu, Walkerplus (quoting Abeno Harukas PR).

## Kagurazaka Lunch: Main Street or Back Lanes?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kagurazaka-lunch-main-street-or-lanes
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

With little time, eat on the main street. Tonkatsu Kagurazaka Sakura on Kagurazaka-dori is open all day and has weekday lunch sets from ¥990. For the alley atmosphere Kagurazaka is known for, book a table at Kagurazaka Oishinbo, an old house on a stone-paved lane (last lunch order 14:00, closed Sundays). If your schedule is flexible, walk the lanes first and eat later. Le Bretagne serves its lunch menu after 14:00 too, and is closed on Mondays.
Hours and prices from the restaurants' own listings · alley information from GLTJP · walks from Google Maps · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Main street, no planning
A weekday set on Kagurazaka-dori
from ¥990 · L.O. 22:00
Tonkatsu Kagurazaka Sakura's main store is at Kagurazaka 5-1-1, on the main street about 150 m (2 minutes) from Bishamonten temple. It is open every day from 11:00 to 23:00 with last orders at 22:00, so there is no lunch cut-off to race. The weekday-only lunch menu lists prices with tax: a coarse-ground minced cutlet set at ¥990, a pork loin cutlet set at ¥1,100 and a fillet set at ¥1,380. Iidabashi Station's B3 exit is a 4-minute walk.
Weekday lunch
¥990
Minced cutlet set
Pork loin cutlet set ¥1,100, fillet ¥1,380, tax included.
Open daily
11:00
Until 23:00
Last order 22:00. Kagurazaka 5-1-1.
Suits: a short break, solo travellers, anyone who wants a clear price. Not for: weekends if you want the lunch prices (the lunch menu is weekdays only), or travellers looking for the lanes' old-house feel.
Answer B · Back lanes, booked
Yuba lunch in an old house on a stone alley
from ¥1,500 · L.O. 14:00
Kagurazaka Oishinbo, at Kagurazaka 4-8, describes itself as an old house with a black board fence on a stone-paved lane. Google Maps puts it 230 m, about 3 minutes, from Bishamonten. Lunch runs 11:30 to 15:00 with last orders at 14:00, and it is closed on Sundays. Its signature lunch, yuba-meshi (tofu-skin rice), starts at ¥1,500. There are 50 seats: a counter, tatami and sunken-table seating, and private rooms for 2 up to 20 people. It takes reservations by phone or online. If you book seats only and don't turn up, it charges ¥5,000 per person.
Lunch
11:30–15:00
Last order 14:00
Closed Sundays. Yuba-meshi from ¥1,500.

50
Counter to private rooms
Private rooms for 2 to 20 people. Book by phone or online.
Who should book ahead: groups, anyone who wants a private tatami room, and anyone with a fixed lunch hour. Not for: Sundays, or a break that starts after 14:00.
Answer C · Walk first, eat later
A lane walk ending at galettes after 2 p.m.
≈¥1,680 · closed Mon
From Iidabashi Station, walk up Kagurazaka-dori to Bishamonten (280 m, about 5 minutes). Hyogo Yokocho begins at a narrow passage across the street from the temple. It is a pedestrian-only stone lane, at its entrance barely wide enough for one person. Kakurenbo Yokocho, a small maze of lanes, lies between Kagurazaka Naka-dori and Honda Yokocho. Both are public walkways, but people live there, so GLTJP asks visitors to keep their voices down. Stay in the lanes and don't step into doorways or gardens. Finish at Le Bretagne (Kagurazaka 4-2), a Breton crêperie 140 m from Bishamonten. It opens at 11:30, serves its lunch menu after 14:00 too, and stays open into the evening. Lunch averages ¥1,680 with a drink or dessert. It has 38 seats and is closed on Mondays.
Lunch menu
after 14:00
Le Bretagne, Kagurazaka 4-2
Opens 11:30. Closed Mondays. Average lunch ¥1,680.
Station to lanes
≈5 min
Iidabashi to Bishamonten
280 m up Kagurazaka-dori. Hyogo Yokocho starts opposite the temple.
Suits: a flexible afternoon and travellers who came for the alleys. Not for: Mondays, wheeled luggage, or heels on the stone paving.
Our verdict
We suggest: walk the lanes first and eat a late lunch. Start at Bishamonten, wander Hyogo Yokocho and Kakurenbo Yokocho, then sit down at Le Bretagne after 14:00, when you no longer need to watch the clock. This changes by day and by time. On a Monday, Le Bretagne is closed, so eat at Tonkatsu Sakura on the main street instead. If your break is fixed between 11:30 and 14:00 and you want the alley setting, book Oishinbo (not Sundays). If you have less than an hour, skip the hunt and take the ¥990 weekday set on Kagurazaka-dori.
One more thing: the glass shrine at the top of the hill
After lunch, walk to the top of Kagurazaka to Akagi Shrine. It is a centuries-old shrine that architect Kengo Kuma rebuilt in 2010 as a calm glass-and-wood hall, so it looks nothing like the shrines on most itineraries. It is a short walk from Exit 1 of Kagurazaka Station, free to enter, and has its own café if lunch ran short.
Akagi Shrine, 1-10 Akagimotomachi, Shinjuku-ku; near Kagurazaka Station (Tozai line) Exit 1. Sources: GO TOKYO, Time Out Tokyo, Lonely Planet.

## Asakusa: Should You Book Across the River in Azumabashi or Honjo?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/asakusa-across-the-river
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

On the December weeknights we checked, crossing the river did not save money. A double at SORA Kaminarimon Hotel, 190 m from Kaminarimon gate, cost ¥36,845 for three nights. A similar double at Tabist Urban Stays Asakusa, just over Azumabashi bridge, cost ¥37,350. That is ¥505 more for an 8-minute walk. Only a room farther into Sumida, near Oshiage, was clearly cheaper: ¥7,585 less over three nights, but with a shared bathroom and a 28-minute walk to the temple. So we suggest you price the west bank first and cross only if the gap on your dates is real.
Booking.com prices for 2 adults, Mon 14–Thu 17 Dec 2026 (3 nights), taxes included, checked 23 November 2026 · walks from Google Maps

Three minutes home from dinner
¥36,845 · 190 m
Our west-bank sample was SORA Kaminarimon Hotel (Kaminarimon 2-chome), a double rated 8.2: ¥36,845 for three nights including taxes and fees, about ¥12,300 a night. Google Maps puts it 190 m, about 3 minutes, from Kaminarimon gate. After dinner near the temple you are home almost at once, and an early visit before the crowds is easy. Asakusa's cheapest well-rated double on these dates was ¥35,002, so the temple side was not the expensive option.

The 8-minute walk over Azumabashi
¥37,350 · 550 m
Tabist Urban Stays Asakusa sits in Azumabashi 1-chome, on the Skytree side of the river. A double with a small double bed, also rated 8.2, was ¥37,350 for the same three nights. Google Maps traces the walk to Kaminarimon at 550 m, about 8 minutes, west along Asakusa-dori and over Azumabashi bridge, with the Asahi Beer Hall and Tokyo Skytree behind you. Answer C · Farther into Sumida
Save ¥7,585, walk 28 minutes
¥29,260 · 1.9 km
The clearly cheaper rooms were farther east. OCICA Oshiage Tokyo by R Hotel (Narihira 4-chome), rated 8.7, had a double with a shared bathroom for ¥29,260 for three nights: ¥7,585 less than the room by Kaminarimon, about ¥2,500 a night. The cost is distance. Kaminarimon is 1.9 km away, about 28 minutes on foot, or about 15 minutes door to door by the Toei Asakusa Line or bus. At 9 p.m. you are not stranded: the restaurant floors of Tokyo Solamachi under Skytree (6F, 7F, 30F and 31F) stay open until 23:00, an 850 m, 12-minute walk from the hotel. A Honjo hotel with a private bathroom (unito residence, Honjo 3-chome, 18 minutes' walk from Kaminarimon) cost ¥46,564 on our dates, so "farther out" is not automatically cheaper.

Our verdict
We suggest: price a room within 5 minutes of Kaminarimon first. On our December weeknights it cost less than the hotel across the bridge, and you can walk home from dinner in 3 minutes. Book across Azumabashi bridge when it is cheaper on your dates. The 8-minute walk is easy, so we would cross for even ¥1,000 a night. Go farther into Sumida only if saving about ¥2,500 a night matters more than a private bathroom and walking to the temple. Prices move daily, so compare both banks for your exact nights.
See hotels in Asakusa →Opens Booking.com. Compare with Sumida Ward on the same dates before you book.
One more thing: the shop that invented Tokyo's sakura mochi
Staying on the Sumida side puts you near Chomeiji Sakuramochi, the shop that created Tokyo-style sakura mochi in 1717 and still makes nothing else. A thin crêpe-like cake is wrapped around red bean paste and then in two or three salted cherry leaves; the shop suggests you take the leaves off and just enjoy the scent they leave behind. Have one with green tea at the counter, because they taste best fresh.
Chomeiji Sakuramochi (Yamamotoya), Mukojima 5-1-14, Sumida-ku; about 12 min from Hikifune or 15–20 min from Asakusa. About ¥250 to take away, ¥500 with tea in the shop. Closed Mondays (and some Tuesdays); takeaway only in cherry-blossom season. Sources: Serai (Shogakukan), All About, Highlighting Japan (Government of Japan).

## Sakai: Can You Watch a Knife Being Made Without Booking?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/sakai-watch-knife-making
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Yes, if you go on a Friday. Sakai Traditional Crafts Museum holds a free sharpening demonstration by a knife craftsman every Friday from 13:30 to 15:00, with no booking. Sharpening is the step that gives a Sakai blade its edge. Watching the forging itself is different: the workshops listed by Sakai's tourism bureau ask for a booking 10 to 15 days ahead. On other weekdays, the museum's free knife exhibit and its shop of 24 Sakai makers are what you can see without planning.
Times and rules from Sakai Traditional Crafts Museum and the Sakai Tourism and Convention Bureau · route from Google Maps · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · No booking, Friday afternoon
Watch a craftsman sharpen a blade
Fri 13:30–15:00 · free
The museum says a knife craftsman demonstrates sharpening (togi) right in front of visitors every Friday from 13:30 to 15:00. On Saturdays and Sundays there are re-sharpening demonstrations instead, from 11:00 to 12:00 and 13:00 to 15:00. Entry is free and you just walk in. Cancellations are posted on the museum's website, so check it on the morning you go.
Sharpening demo
Fri 13:30
Until 15:00, free
No booking. Weekend re-sharpening demos at 11:00 and 13:00.
From Namba
≈35 min
¥290 on the Nankai Line
Local to Sakai Station (15 min), then a 1.1 km walk (16 min).
Suits: anyone with a free Friday afternoon who wants to see a real craftsman at work. Not for: travellers who want to see the hammering and fire of a forge. That needs a booking (Answer B).
Answer B · Plan ahead
A forge visit or a sharpening class
10–15 days' notice
Sakai's tourism bureau lists knife workshops that accept visitors by reservation. Sasuke, a forge run by a fifth-generation knife and scissor maker, takes bookings up to 15 days ahead (open 10:00–19:00, closed irregularly, in principle on Thursdays). Fujii Hamono Seisakusho, which does every stage from forging to fitting the handle in-house, takes bookings up to 10 days ahead and closes on Sundays. The museum also runs occasional hands-on sharpening classes. The next one listed is Thursday 24 December 2026, 14:00 to 15:30, for ¥2,000. You sharpen two of your own knives with a certified craftsman, so it suits people who travel with knives or plan to buy one first.
Forge visits
10–15 days
Book before you fly
Sasuke up to 15 days ahead, Fujii Hamono up to 10 days ahead.
Sharpening class
¥2,000
Thu 24 Dec 2026, 14:00
16 places, first come. Bring two knives, an apron and a towel.
Suits: cooks and knife buyers who know their dates early. Not for: a spontaneous afternoon. If you would rather have the booking, transport and translation handled, guided Sakai knife tours are sold online. Check what each one includes before you book.
Answer C · Any open day
The free knife museum and shop
10:00–17:00 · free
On days without a demonstration, Sakai Traditional Crafts Museum still shows how a Sakai knife is made. Its knife museum, "Cut", covers the history, production steps and tools with models and real examples. Downstairs, the shop stocks knives from 24 Sakai makers, more than anywhere else in one place, according to the museum. Makers take turns helping on the shop floor, and English-speaking staff are on hand. If you buy a knife, the museum also re-sharpens knives from ¥1,600.
Entry
Free
Open 10:00–17:00
Closed the third Tuesday of the month and 29 Dec–3 Jan.
In the shop
24 makers
Compare side by side
English-speaking staff on hand to help you choose.
Suits: any weekday visit, and anyone buying a knife. Not for: the third Tuesday of the month, when the museum is closed.
Our verdict
We suggest: go on a Friday and arrive by 13:30 for the free sharpening demonstration, then browse the exhibit and the 24-maker shop before it closes at 17:00. You don't need to book anything. If you can't make a Friday, weekend re-sharpening demos start at 11:00 and 13:00. If you want to see the forging itself, book a workshop at least two weeks before your visit. A plain Monday-to-Thursday visit without a booking means the museum and shop only.
See Sakai knife tours →Opens Klook. For a guided visit with the booking done for you. The Friday demo itself is free.
One more thing: Sakai's 700-year-old sweet
Sakai's other craft is a sweet: kurumi mochi from Kanbukuro, a shop founded in 1329 whose name is said to have come from Toyotomi Hideyoshi. Despite the name there are no walnuts; "kurumi" means wrapped, and the soft rice cakes are wrapped in a pale green bean paste made to a recipe the shop keeps to itself. Order it in the shop, or as kori kurumi mochi under plain shaved ice. Tabelog reviewers say it is a taste you won't find anywhere else.
Kanbukuro, Sakai-ku, Sakai. A single serving is about ¥410. It doesn't keep (eat it the same day) and is sold only at the shop. Check hours before you go. Sources: Gendai (Kodansha), Retty, Tabelog reviews, Sakai Tourism Bureau sweets map.

## Nakazakicho vs Umeda: Would You Walk for ¥3,000 Less a Night?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/nakazakicho-vs-umeda-hotel
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Key facts:
- Saving: ¥24,920 near Nakazakicho vs ¥34,394 at Hotel Monterey Osaka for the same three nights (14–17 Dec 2026, 1 adult, Booking.com, checked 23 Nov 2026): about ¥3,160 a night.
- The walk: about 800 m, roughly 12 minutes from Osaka Station, plus the time from your platform to the street.
- Taxi: Osaka city fares start at ¥600 for the first 1.2 km, so expect about ¥600–800 for this ride.
- Station hotel: Hotel Granvia Osaka was ¥49,243 for the same three nights, worth it only for early trains on most mornings.

For three weeknights in December, a well-rated double near Nakazakicho Station cost about ¥3,160 a night less than a similar room by Osaka Station: ¥9,474 saved over the stay. The catch is a 12-minute, 800 m walk from Osaka Station. With a small bag we'd walk it. With a heavy suitcase, a taxi of about ¥600 to ¥800 on arrival still leaves most of the saving.
Booking.com prices for 1 adult, Mon 14–Thu 17 Dec 2026 (3 nights), checked 23 November 2026 · routes from Google Maps · taxi fares from the Kinki District Transport Bureau
Answer A · With a small bag
Walk from Osaka Station
800 m · ≈12 min
Our sample hotel was Quintessa Hotel Osaka Umeda Comic & Books, about 400 m from Nakazakicho Station: ¥24,920 for three nights in a double room, taxes included. Google Maps puts it 800 m and about 12 minutes on foot from Osaka Station. Add a few minutes to get from your platform out to the street, because Osaka Station is big. If you'd rather not walk, Nakazakicho Station is one stop from Higashi-Umeda on the Tanimachi subway line.

See hotels near Nakazakicho →Opens Booking.com. Check each listing's distance to Nakazakicho Station and compare Umeda on the same dates.
One more thing: the croquette stop
Right outside Exit 2 of Nakazakicho Station (about 86 m) is Yamatatsu, a small butcher's counter that fries its croquettes after you order, so they come out hot and crisp. It is takeaway only and cash only: cards, e-money and QR payments are not accepted. Grab one on your way out in the morning. It is the kind of breakfast no hotel buffet gives you, and it is what living in this neighbourhood instead of Umeda feels like.
Yamatatsu (山辰), 3-1-19 Nakazaki, Kita-ku. Hours change, so check before you go. Source: Tabelog listing and reviews, checked 23 November 2026.

## Senso-ji Before Breakfast or After Dinner?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/sensoji-morning-or-evening
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Senso-ji's grounds never close, so both quiet times work, but they show you different things. Come early if you want to step inside the main hall: it opens at 6:30 from October to March (6:00 from April). Come after dinner for photos: the gates, the pagoda and the main hall stay lit until about 23:00, but the hall itself is shut after 17:00. Midday is for Nakamise's shops, and for crowds.
Checked 23 November 2026 · hours from GO TOKYO, japan-guide.com, the Asakusa tourist centre and MISOJYU
Answer A · Before breakfast
Early morning: inside the main hall
hall from 6:30 (Oct to Mar)
The grounds are open all night, so you can walk through Kaminarimon and Nakamise before the stalls open. The main hall opens at 6:30 in the colder months and 6:00 from April to September. Then walk to MISOJYU, a miso soup shop at 1-7-5 Asakusa, 3 minutes from Exit 1 of Asakusa Station on the Ginza Line. It serves a morning set (miso soup, a rice ball, half a seasoned egg and pickles) for ¥850 from 8:00 to 10:00.
Main hall
6:30–17:00
Oct to Mar
6:00–17:00 from April to September. Grounds always open, free.
Breakfast
¥850
MISOJYU, from 8:00
Morning set 8:00–10:00. 3 min from Ginza Line Asakusa Exit 1.
Suits: early risers, anyone who wants to pray or look inside the hall, and jet-lagged arrivals. Not for: shopping, because the Nakamise stalls aren't open yet.
Answer B · Daytime
Daytime: Nakamise open, and full
250 m · about 90 stalls
Daytime is the only time you get both things: the main hall open and the Nakamise stalls trading. Nakamise runs about 250 m from Kaminarimon to Hozomon, with around 90 stalls selling snacks, sweets and souvenirs. This is also the most crowded part of the visit, so expect to move slowly from Kaminarimon to Hozomon.
Nakamise
250 m
The busiest walk
Kaminarimon to Hozomon. The hall closes at 17:00.
Suits: first-time visitors who want snacks and souvenirs and don't mind crowds.
Answer C · After dinner
After dinner: lit up, quieter, hall closed
lights until ≈23:00
Kaminarimon, Hozomon, the five-storied pagoda and the main hall are lit every day from sunset until about 23:00. Our short photo route: start on the free 8th-floor terrace of the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center (open to 22:00), opposite Kaminarimon, for the view down Nakamise. Cross to Kaminarimon, walk Nakamise to see the painted shutters on the closed stalls, then go through Hozomon to the pagoda and the front of the main hall.
Lights
to ≈23:00
Every day
From sunset. You see the hall from outside: it closes at 17:00.
Terrace
9:00–22:00
Tourist centre, 8F
2-18-9 Kaminarimon, opposite the gate. Free, open every day.
Suits: photographers and anyone staying nearby after dinner. Not for: visitors who want to see inside the main hall.
Our verdict
We suggest: come after dinner if photos are the point: you get the lights, quieter paths and the shutter murals. Choose the morning instead if you want to go inside the main hall without crowds: arrive at 6:30 from October to March (6:00 from April), then have breakfast at MISOJYU from 8:00. Come in the daytime only if the Nakamise shops matter to you. If you're staying in Asakusa, you can do both quiet visits on one day.
See hotels in Asakusa →Opens Booking.com. Stay within a short walk of Kaminarimon for an easy 6:30 start.
One more thing: stay for rakugo after dark
If you pick the evening, walk five minutes west to Asakusa Engei Hall, one of only four theatres in Tokyo that stage rakugo (comic storytelling) every day of the year. You buy a ticket at the door on the day and can drift in and out between acts. Most of it is in Japanese, but the mix of storytellers, manzai pairs and magic is easy to enjoy even without the words.
Asakusa Engei Hall, 1-43-12 Asakusa, about 1 min from Tsukuba Express Asakusa Exit A1. Open daily, roughly 11:30–20:45; general admission about ¥3,500, cash. Sources: GO TOKYO (Tokyo Convention & Visitors Bureau) and NAVITIME.

## Two Hours Before Dinner in Shinjuku: Garden, Skyline or Side Streets?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-two-hours-before-dinner
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

From October to mid-March Shinjuku Gyoen stops letting people in at 16:00 and closes at 16:30, so the garden only works if your two hours start by about 14:00. Later than that, take the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government observatory, open to 22:00. If it rains, stay in Shinjuku-sanchome, where a big bookstore connects straight to the subway.
Checked 23 November 2026 · hours from the Ministry of the Environment, the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and GO TOKYO
Answer A · For an early start
Shinjuku Gyoen
last entry 16:00 (Oct to mid-Mar)
Enter at Shinjuku Gate, a 5-minute walk from Shinjuku-sanchome Exit E5 or 10 minutes from the South Exit of Shinjuku Station. The autumn leaves usually peak from late November to early December, and the best viewpoints are close to that gate: the Japanese Garden for maples, and the Formal Garden with its plane trees. We suggest staying at the Shinjuku Gate end rather than crossing the whole garden, so you are not rushing to leave at 16:30.
Winter hours
9:00–16:30
Last entry 16:00
1 Oct to 14 Mar. Summer closes at 18:00, and 11 June to 31 July at 19:00.
Adults
¥500
Closed Mondays
Or the next weekday after a Monday holiday, and 29 Dec to 3 Jan. IC cards work at the gates.
Suits: a free afternoon that starts by about 14:00, on a dry day that isn't a Monday. Not for: a late afternoon in winter.
Answer B · For the skyline, any time until 21:30
Tokyo Metropolitan Government observatory
free · 202 m
Allow about an hour: roughly 10 minutes on foot from the JR Shinjuku West Gate, 20 to 30 minutes in the lift queue (the official estimate), time at the windows, and the walk back. After 17:30 only the South Observatory is open, except on days the South one is closed. When it gets dark, the building's free TOKYO Night & Light projection plays on the outside wall until 21:45, so you can watch it on your way to dinner.
South Observatory
9:30–22:00
Last entry 21:30
Closed 1st and 3rd Tuesday. North closes 17:30 and is closed 2nd and 4th Monday.
Plan for
≈1 hr

10 min from JR West Gate each way, plus a 20 to 30 minute lift queue.
Suits: a late afternoon or early evening, dinner on the west side, and anyone who wants sunset and city lights for free. Not for: a rainy or very hazy day, when there's not much to see.
Answer C · For an unhurried walk, and for bad weather
Shinjuku-sanchome side streets
3 min from JR East Exit
Walk out of the JR East Exit and head along the east side toward Shinjuku-sanchome. The one stop we'd make is Kinokuniya Books Shinjuku Main Store, about 3 minutes from the JR East Exit and connected directly to Exit B7 of Shinjuku-sanchome Station. It is open 10:00 to 21:00 every day, so you can browse right up to dinner. If the rain starts, use the subway concourse and come up close to your restaurant.
Kinokuniya
10:00–21:00
Open every day
3-17-7 Shinjuku. Direct from Shinjuku-sanchome Exit B7.
Suits: rainy days, a dinner booking on the east side, and anyone who'd rather wander than queue.
Our verdict
We suggest: if your two hours start by 14:00 on a dry day, Tuesday to Sunday, take Shinjuku Gyoen, especially during the autumn leaves in late November and early December. If they start later, or it's a Monday, go up the free observatory and stay for the projection after dark. If it rains, stick to Shinjuku-sanchome and Kinokuniya. From mid-March the garden stays open until 18:00, so then it also works for a 15:30 start.
One more thing: the shrine behind Golden Gai
Between the side streets and dinner, slip into Hanazono Shrine, Shinjuku's guardian shrine, which was already old in the Edo period. Its red gates sit between Yasukuni-dori and the back of Golden Gai, so you walk from neon into lanterns and quiet in a few steps. It's dedicated to Inari, the deity of business, and entertainers have long come here to pray for success.
Hanazono Shrine, 5-17-3 Shinjuku; next to Exit E2 of Shinjuku-sanchome Station. Grounds open 24 hours, free. Sources: Time Out Tokyo, GLTJP, Tokyo Cheapo.

## Would You Stay Outside Shibuya for a Quieter Morning?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shibuya-quiet-base-yoyogi
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For three nights with evenings out in Shibuya, we would stay in central Shibuya. Both "quiet" neighbours need a change of train every night, and on our dates they were not cheaper: about ¥61,300 for three nights near Yoyogi-Hachiman against about ¥57,900 for the cheapest central hotel rated 8+. Yoyogi-Hachiman wins only on the morning walk, with Yoyogi Park 6 minutes from the station.
Booking.com prices for 2 adults, Wed 16–Sat 19 Dec 2026 (3 nights), checked 23 November 2026 · routes from Yahoo! Transit for the same Wednesday
Answer A · For morning walks in the park
Yoyogi-Hachiman
≈¥61,300 for 3 nights
A small Odakyu Line station on the west side of Yoyogi Park. The Tokyo park association puts the park 6 minutes' walk away, and the park is always open and free, so a dawn walk is easy. The catch is the trip home: from Shibuya you ride the Keio Inokashira Line to Shimokitazawa and change to the Odakyu Line, about 18 to 19 minutes (¥256). On our dates, MI-HOTEL ATELIER HATSUDAI (rated 8.3, about 500 m from Yoyogi Hachimangu Shrine) came to about ¥61,300 for a double with private bathroom.

Suits: early risers who want green space first thing. Does not suit: late nights in Shibuya, or anyone who hates a change of train after dinner.
Answer B · For breakfast and a neighbourhood feel
Yoyogi-Uehara
few hotels, mostly apartments
A residential area where the Chiyoda Line meets the Odakyu Line. For breakfast, Katane Bakery opens at 7:00 from Wednesday to Saturday (closed Sunday to Tuesday), about 10 minutes' walk from the station; Tabelog notes that credit cards are not accepted. Back from Shibuya, the quickest route is the Ginza or Hanzomon Line to Omotesando, then the Chiyoda Line: 11 to 13 minutes, ¥178. Hotels are scarce: the nearest Booking.com listing, a private twin 400 m from the station, was about ¥73,400 for our three nights, and the cheaper well-rated options were apartments about 1 km away toward Hatagaya, from about ¥39,000.

Suits: longer stays in an apartment, and travellers who like local bakeries and quiet streets. Does not suit: a short trip on a hotel budget.
Answer C · For evenings out
Central Shibuya
from ≈¥57,900 for 3 nights
On the same dates, the cheapest hotel rated 8 or higher within 1 km of Shibuya Station was Hotel SUNROAD (adults only, rated 8.4, 0.5 km) at about ¥57,900 for an economy double. lyf Shibuya Tokyo (8.9) came to about ¥77,100 and Shibuya Granbell Hotel (8.0, 250 m) about ¥83,200. You walk home from dinner, and lyf is about 0.9 km from Yoyogi Park, so a morning walk is still possible.

Our verdict
We suggest: for three nights with evenings out, book central Shibuya, ideally on the north side of the station, toward Yoyogi Park. On our dates it cost the same or less and saved about an hour and a half of evening trains. Choose Yoyogi-Hachiman when central rooms rated 8+ cost about ¥5,000 a night more than the Yoyogi side, or when you are usually back before midnight and the 6-minute walk to the park is the point of the trip. Choose Yoyogi-Uehara for a week or more in an apartment.
See hotels in Shibuya →Opens Booking.com. Filter to rating 8+ and check the distance to the station.
One more thing: Japan's largest mosque, five minutes from the station
Stay near Yoyogi-Uehara and you're five minutes from Tokyo Camii, the largest mosque in Japan, a white Ottoman-style building tucked into a quiet residential street. Visitors are welcome every day and entry is free; the domed prayer hall with its stained glass is one of the most beautiful interiors in Tokyo. Hardly anyone puts it on a Shibuya itinerary.
Tokyo Camii & Diyanet Turkish Culture Center, 1-19 Oyamacho, Shibuya-ku; about 5 min from Yoyogi-Uehara Station. Open daily 10:00–18:00, free. Dress modestly: no shorts; women cover their hair (scarves are provided). Be quiet and don't take photos during prayers. Sources: Tokyo Camii official FAQ, GLTJP.

## Minoh Falls in Autumn: Leave Osaka at 1, Back Before Dark?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/minoh-falls-autumn-afternoon
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Yes, on a weekday. Leave Osaka-umeda at 13:00, reach Minoh at 13:26, walk about 45 minutes uphill and you are at the falls around 14:15. Spend 20 minutes there, walk down, and you are back at the station around 15:30, more than an hour before the 16:48 sunset. At weekends in the leaf season the path is packed, so leave by 11:00 instead.
Timed for Thursday 26 November 2026 · walking times from the Minoh Park office · checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · The full outing from Umeda
Station to the falls and back
≈2 h 30 min door to door
Take the 13:00 Hankyu Takarazuka Line express from Osaka-umeda, change at Ishibashi handai-mae (13:15, cross to the Minoo Line, 13:20) and arrive at Minoh at 13:26. The waterfall path starts about 5 minutes from the station and climbs gently along the river for about 2.7 km. The park office gives 40 to 50 minutes to the 33 m falls. Entry to the park is free.
Umeda to Minoh
26 min
¥280 with an IC card
One change at Ishibashi handai-mae. Trains about every 10 minutes.
Walk up
40–50 min
About 2.7 km
Paved riverside path, no cars. Wear proper shoes.
Sunset 26 Nov
16:48
Back by ≈15:30
Down the same path, then 26 minutes to Umeda.
Suits: reasonably fit walkers on a weekday. Does not suit: a weekend in late November, when crowds slow the path from the station onward.
Answer B · Shorter, with a snack stop
Momiji tempura and the red bridge at Ryuan-ji
≈1 h 15 min round trip
Walk up the shopping stretch at the start of the path, where shops fry momiji tempura, Minoh's famous snack of salted maple leaves in sweet batter. Carry on past the insect museum (15 to 20 minutes from the station) to Ryuan-ji temple and its red bridge, about 5 minutes further, then turn around. You see the autumn colour on the lower path without the climb to the falls.
Turnaround
≈25 min
Ryuan-ji temple
The park office's autumn photos of 20 Nov were taken right here.

Maple-leaf tempura
Sold at several shops along the first part of the path.
Suits: a late start, children, or anyone who would rather wander than hike.
Answer C · If the waterfall is the priority
Leave two hours earlier
Umeda by 11:00
Leaving at 13:00 works, but with only about 20 minutes at the falls. Leave Umeda around 11:00 and you can stop for lunch near the station, take the climb slowly, spend an hour at the falls and still walk down in daylight. At weekends and on holidays from 14 November to 6 December the park office expects a solid stream of people on the path all the way from the station, so the early start matters even more then.

Light-up
to 21:30

Our verdict
We suggest: on a weekday, the 13:00 train from Osaka-umeda is enough: falls by about 14:15, back at Minoh Station around 15:30, before the 16:48 sunset. That changes at weekends and on holidays until 6 December, when we would leave by 11:00, or flip the plan and arrive around 15:30 to walk up for the light-up (sunset to 21:30). If you set off after 14:00, do the short walk to Ryuan-ji instead.
See hotels in Umeda →Opens Booking.com. Hankyu trains to Minoh leave from Osaka-umeda.
One more thing: the brewery on your way back
Get off one stop early on the way back, at Makiochi, and walk about 10 minutes to Minoh Beer Warehouse. Minoh Beer is a family-run brewery founded in 1997 that has won awards abroad, and this is its own taproom in a quiet residential street, with the beer at its freshest. After the falls and the momiji tempura, it is the local way to finish the day.
MINOH BEER WAREHOUSE, 3-14-18 Makiochi, Minoh; about 10–12 min walk from Hankyu Makiochi Station. 11:00–21:00 (last order 20:30), Sundays to 20:00; closed Thursdays. Sources: Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp), Tabelog.

## Shibuya Crossing: Is It Worth Paying to See It From Above?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shibuya-crossing-view
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If the crossing is what you came for, you don't need Shibuya Sky. Watching one light change from Hachiko Square is free, and the best paid view of the scramble itself is the MAG8 rooftop right above it at ¥1,800 with a drink. Shibuya Sky (from ¥2,700) is worth it for the skyline, not for the crossing.
Prices and hours from MAGNET by SHIBUYA109, SHIBUYA SKY and GO TOKYO, checked 23 November 2026
Answer A · Free
Street level: Hachiko Square
¥0
Leave JR Shibuya Station by the Hachiko Exit. The south-east corner of the crossing is at Hachiko Square, about 50 m away. Stand back from the kerb for one full cycle: the lights change about every 2 minutes, and at peak times around 3,000 people cross on a single green. Watch once, then cross with the next wave.
From the exit
50 m
Hachiko Exit
JR Shibuya Station. Tokyu and Tokyo Metro users come up at Exit 8.
One cycle
≈2 min
Watch, then cross
Up to about 3,000 people per green light, all directions at once.
Suits: first-timers who want to feel the crowd and take a quick video. Does not suit: anyone hoping for the classic overhead photo.
Answer B · The price of a drink
Window seat: Starbucks SHIBUYA TSUTAYA
buy a drink, no seat guaranteed
The famous Starbucks now fills the whole 2nd floor of the QFRONT building on the north-west corner. You must order to use it, payment is cashless, and there are no reservations. Since the 2024 renovation the seats are set back from the glass and the window strip is kept for standing and photos, so you will get a look, but not a guaranteed seat with the view.
Floor
2F
QFRONT building
The ground-floor Starbucks is takeaway only. Go up the escalator.
Window seat
No booking
First come
Expect a crowd at the glass, especially in the evening.
Suits: a coffee break with a quick look down. Does not suit: anyone who wants to sit and watch for half an hour.
Our paid pick for the crossing itself
MAG8 rooftop at MAGNET by SHIBUYA109
¥1,800 incl. 1 drink
CROSSING VIEW & ROOFTOP LOUNGE MAG8 sits on the roof of MAGNET by SHIBUYA109, on the north side of the crossing, and looks straight down onto the scramble. The fee includes one drink (soft drink or alcohol), and there is an indoor lounge if it rains. It may shorten hours or close in bad weather.
Entry
¥1,800
One drink included
Cash not accepted. Children 6 and under free.
Hours
10–22:00
Last entry 21:30
The crossing at night, lit by the screens, is the shot most people want.
Answer C · For the skyline
Shibuya Sky
from ¥2,700 online
An open-air rooftop 229 m up on Shibuya Scramble Square, directly connected to the station. You can look down on the crossing and Center-gai, but from that height the people are dots. What the ticket really buys is the 360-degree view: Tokyo Tower, Tokyo Skytree, and Mt. Fuji to the west on a clear day. Bags, hats and selfie sticks go in lockers on the 46th floor, and the roof closes in strong wind or rain.
Web, before 15:00
¥2,700
¥3,400 from 15:00
At the counter ¥3,000 and ¥3,700. Online sales open two weeks ahead.
Hours
10:00–22:30
Last admission 21:20
No time limit. GO TOKYO says most people stay about 90 minutes.
Suits: a clear evening and someone who wants the whole city. Does not suit: a crossing-only visit, or a windy, cloudy day.
Our verdict
We suggest: watch one light change from Hachiko Square, cross it yourself, then go up to the MAG8 rooftop if you want the overhead photo. That covers the scramble for ¥1,800. Book Shibuya Sky instead only if you care about the skyline: buy a slot before 15:00 to pay ¥2,700, or around sunset if the day is clear (sunset in early December is about 16:30). If the forecast says strong wind or rain, skip both rooftops and use the Starbucks window.
See Shibuya Sky tickets →Opens Klook. Compare with the official web price of ¥2,700 / ¥3,400.
One more thing: a free view with a masterpiece beside it
Before you pay for a view, walk into the passage between JR Shibuya and the Keio Inokashira line inside Shibuya Mark City. One wall is Myth of Tomorrow, Taro Okamoto's 30 m mural of the moment an atomic bomb explodes. It was painted for a hotel in Mexico, lost for decades, found in 2003, and installed here in 2008. The windows opposite look straight down on the crossing, free, on two levels; the glass is meshed, so it's better for watching than for photos.
Shibuya Mark City connecting passage (2F), Shibuya Station. Free and open whenever the station is. Sources: Time Out Tokyo, Lonely Planet, JR Pass blog.
