## "Shinjuku" on the Booking: Which Station Will You Actually Use?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-which-station
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

On the same Wednesday night, a double room rated 7 or higher within 500 m cost from about ¥13,000 near Higashi-shinjuku, about ¥15,000 near Shinjuku-sanchome and usually over ¥22,000 right by JR Shinjuku. The cheaper rooms are fine, as long as their station runs the trains you need.
Booking.com prices for 2 adults, Wed 16–Thu 17 Dec 2026, checked 23 November 2026 · routes from Tokyo Metro, Toei and JR East
Answer A · For an early train out
Near JR Shinjuku
from ≈¥22,000 (rated 8+)
The Narita Express leaves from JR Shinjuku, with the first departure around 5:55 and a ride of about 1 hour 20 minutes to Narita Airport (¥3,250 standard seat). Rooms close to the station cost the most: on our date the well-rated options started around ¥22,000 to ¥27,000. One budget exception, Apartment Hotel Shinjuku (about 450 m away, about ¥12,500 with fees), sits between JR Shinjuku and Shinjuku-sanchome.
Suits: travellers with an early airport train or limited express and a big suitcase.
Inside Shinjuku Station: with a suitcase, allow extra minutes to reach your exit.
Answer B · For shopping and direct subway trips
Near Shinjuku-sanchome
from ≈¥15,000
A separate subway station on the east side with three lines: the Marunouchi Line toward Ginza and Tokyo Station, the Fukutoshin Line to Shibuya and Ikebukuro (with through trains to Yokohama), and the Toei Shinjuku Line. Its exits run straight into Isetan. On our date Hotel Tateshina came to about ¥15,300 and Hotel Rocks about ¥17,000 for two.
Suits: shoppers and anyone heading to Shibuya, Ikebukuro or Ginza most days.
Answer C · For the lowest price
Near Higashi-shinjuku
from ≈¥13,000
One stop north of Shinjuku-sanchome on the Fukutoshin Line, plus the Toei Oedo Line. On our date Sakura Cross Hotel Shinjuku East (rated 8.3) was about ¥13,700 and Shinjuku Granbell (8.0) about ¥14,600. Two catches: express trains on the Fukutoshin Line pass through without stopping, and for Roppongi on the Oedo Line you change at Tochomae.
Suits: budget-minded travellers happy to ride local trains and add one change on some days.
The station area spreads well beyond the JR gates, so check the walk to your hotel.
Our verdict
We suggest: pick Shinjuku-sanchome for most trips, because it costs less than the JR side and its subway lines reach Shibuya, Ikebukuro and Ginza without a change. Pay for JR Shinjuku only on nights before an early Narita Express or limited express. Choose Higashi-shinjuku if saving about ¥2,000 a night matters more than one extra stop.
See hotels near Shinjuku-sanchome →Opens Booking.com. Check the distance to the station on each listing.
Shinjuku after dark, whichever station you sleep near.
One more thing: the station café commuters swear by
Right by JR Shinjuku's East Exit, in the basement of Lumine Est, is BERG, a tiny beer-and-coffee counter that has fed commuters since 1970. It opens at 7:00, so you can have rye bread, sausages and a coffee (or a morning beer, like some regulars) before the crowds. Tabelog put it on its 2025 list of the 100 best cafés in east Japan, and most visitors walk straight past it.
BEER&CAFE BERG, Lumine Est B1F, 3-38-1 Shinjuku, near the JR East Exit. Daily 7:00–23:00 (food last order 22:30); budget under ¥1,000. Sources: Time Out Tokyo, Gurunavi, Tabelog Cafe 100 EAST 2025.

## Cup Noodles Museum Ikeda: Design a Cup, Make Noodles, or Just Explore?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/cup-noodles-museum-ikeda
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

The museum itself is free and about 20 minutes from Umeda. What costs money, and sometimes planning, are the two hands-on experiences. For a short visit we suggest designing your own cup (¥500, no booking). Book the Chicken Ramen workshop only if you want 70 minutes of real cooking.
Hours, prices and booking rules checked 23 November 2026 against the museum's official site and osaka-info.jp
Answer A · For a short visit
My CUPNOODLES Factory
¥500 per cup
Draw on your own cup, then pick one of four soups and four of twelve toppings, and the staff seal it for you to take home. No reservation: numbered tickets are handed out on the day, so arrive earlier on weekends and holidays.
Price
¥500
Per cup
Pay per cup you make.
Booking
None
Numbered ticket
Collected at the museum on the day.
Suits: couples, families and anyone with an hour or two in Ikeda.
Answer B · For hands-on cooking
Chicken Ramen Factory
70 min · book ahead
You knead, roll, steam and season the dough, then flash-fry it into instant noodles yourself. Sessions run five times a day (9:40, 10:50, 12:00, 14:00 and 15:10 at the time of checking) and must be reserved in advance on the museum's booking site. Age limits apply; check them when you book.
Junior high +
¥1,200
Adults
Elementary school students ¥600.
Session
70 min
Reservation only
Online, or by phone on 072-751-0825.
Suits: families with school-age kids and food lovers who planned ahead.
Answer C · If both are full
The free museum
no ticket needed
Walk through the Instant Noodles Tunnel lined with about 800 packages, see the reproduction of the backyard shed where Chicken Ramen was invented in 1958, and watch the CUPNOODLES Drama Theater. The museum shop sells limited items. Some listings note cards are not accepted, so bring cash.
Our verdict
We suggest: for most visitors, the ¥500 cup is the right pick. It needs no booking and fits a half day. Book the Chicken Ramen Factory only if you can commit to a session time. Avoid Tuesdays, when the museum is closed.
Open
9:30–16:30
Last entry 15:30
Closed Tuesdays and over New Year.
From Umeda
≈20 min
Hankyu Takarazuka Line
Express to Ikeda, then about 5 minutes on foot.
One more thing: Ikeda's free lookout
Keep walking about 15 minutes north of Ikeda Station to Satsukiyama Park, the small mountain park locals use for their evening walks. Its observation deck looks out across the whole Osaka plain, and entry is free. The park is also home to the town zoo known for breeding wombats, but it is being rebuilt, so treat any animals you see as a bonus.
Satsukiyama Park, Ayaha 2-chome, Ikeda; about 15 min walk or 10 min by Hankyu bus from Ikeda Station north exit. The zoo has been closed for renovation since June 2024 with only limited openings. Sources: Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp), Ikeda City.

We searched the same two nights in December 2026 for one adult, total price including taxes, and only counted places within 1 km of Osaka Namba Station, an easy walk back from Dotonbori. Our verdict
We suggest: on a weeknight like the Wednesday we checked, ¥5,000 gets you a private room (with a shared toilet) or, for ¥15 more, a room with its own bathroom. On a Saturday like the one we checked, ¥5,000 buys a capsule, so take the capsule or move your Namba nights midweek. These were the two nights we sampled; prices change daily, so check your own dates.
One more thing: the mossy statue you splash
Two minutes from the capsule hotels is a quiet stone lane, Hozenji Yokocho, and at its end the Mizukake Fudo: a statue so covered in moss that you can't see its face, because people have splashed it with water for luck since just after the war. Scoop water from the well and throw it gently, three times on Fudo in the centre, once on each attendant, then once more on Fudo. It's free, open all day, and lovely late at night when the lane is lit.
Hozenji, Namba 1-2-16, Chuo-ku; about 5–10 min from Namba Station. Open all day, free. The lane is about 80 m of stone paving lined with old restaurants and bars. Sources: Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp), GLTJP (supervised by Hozenji).

## Four Friends in Osaka: One Apartment or Two Hotel Rooms?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-four-friends
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Four people in Osaka usually choose between three options: a private apartment, an apartment hotel, or two twin rooms in a regular hotel. None is always cheapest. What decides it is how many nights you're staying, how many bathrooms you need and how much you care about having someone at a front desk.
Checked 23 November 2026
The quick comparison
🏠 Private apartment
Good: one shared living space, a kitchen, a washing machine.Watch: often one bathroom for four, cleaning fees, self check-in, and some have a minimum stay.
🏨 Apartment hotel
Good: real beds for four, a kitchenette, a laundry machine, and staff if something goes wrong.Watch: popular with groups, so they book out early.
🛏️ Two twin rooms
Good: two bathrooms, daily cleaning, easy cancellation, often right by the station.Watch: rooms are compact and there's no common space to hang out.
Our suggestion: for 2–3 nights, two twin rooms near the station are usually the easiest. For 4 nights or more, an apartment hotel often wins, because laundry and a living room start to matter.
Before you book an apartment
How to check a rental is legal
Short-term rentals in Japan need a registration or a special-zone certification, and legal hosts must record your passport at check-in. Osaka City stopped taking new special-zone applications on 29 May 2026 and has been inspecting rentals more closely, so unlicensed listings are more likely to be cancelled at short notice.
Step 1
№
Find the number
The listing should show a registration or certification number. No number, no booking.
Step 2
ID
Expect a passport check
A host who never asks for ID is a warning sign.
Step 3
Σ
Compare the total
Add cleaning fees and taxes for all nights before comparing with hotel rooms.
Where we'd look for fourNamba: easy to split up during the day and meet up for dinner.
Food at every budget on foot
Direct airport train
Lots of apartment hotels and twin rooms close together
See places for 4 in Namba →Opens Booking.com, searched for 4 adults. Check the bed layout in the photos.
One more thing: a takoyaki party in your apartment
If you take the apartment, do what Osaka families do at home and throw a takoyaki party. A three-minute walk from Namba, Sennichimae Doguyasuji is a 150 m covered street of shops that supply Osaka's restaurants, and several sell takoyaki pans in every size. Buy one there, pick up octopus and batter mix at a supermarket, and four people turning dough balls with picks is a better night than any restaurant.
Sennichimae Doguyasuji Shotengai, Namba-Sennichimae; about 3 min from Namba Station. Hours vary by shop (many roughly 9:00–18:30). Some shops also run food-sample-making workshops. Check that your apartment has a hob the pan works on. Sources: Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp), Mapple.

## Where to Stay in Osaka If You're Out Late
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-night-owls
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Osaka stays up late, but its trains don't. Most subway lines stop around midnight, and a taxi across the city adds up fast. If late dinners and bar hopping are part of the plan, we suggest picking your hotel by where you'll be at 1am, not where you'll be at noon.
Checked 23 November 2026 against Osaka Metro timetables
Our pick · Most nights out
Namba
walk home from everything
The south side of Osaka is where the night happens. Stay within a few minutes of Namba Station and the canal, the side streets and the late food are all on foot.
On foot
3–5 min
Dotonbori
Neon, takoyaki and late ramen along the canal.
On foot
5–10 min
Ura-Namba
Back streets of standing bars and small izakaya between Namba Station and Nipponbashi. Mostly locals.
On foot
3–5 min
Hozenji Yokocho
A quiet stone alley of old restaurants, lovely after dark.
Osaka's south side after dark: the back lanes stay busy late.
Room tip: Namba is loud until late. Ask for a higher floor or a room facing away from the main street.
See hotels near Namba →Opens Booking.com, already searched. Pick your dates.
For a local night · North side
Tenma and Umeda
izakaya alleys
If you would rather drink with office workers than tourists, stay around JR Tenma. The Ura-Tenma alleys sit just north of the station, under hundreds of lanterns. Umeda, one stop away, has the izakaya basements of the Osaka Ekimae Buildings.

≈5 min

Small izakaya and standing bars, packed after work.

1 stop
Tenma to Osaka Station
Handy for an early train the next morning.

If you do stay elsewhere
Check the last train first
Most Osaka Metro lines stop around midnight, and some outer stations earlier. The time is posted at every station.
Know your way back
Missed it? Taxis queue outside Namba and Umeda. Save your hotel's address in Japanese on your phone to show the driver.
First night out in Osaka?A bar-hopping tour takes you into the small places that are hard to walk into alone.
Bar-hopping tours
One more thing: if you miss the last train anyway
If the night runs past the last subway, there's a very Osaka plan B: Spa World in Shinsekai, a huge hot-spring complex themed on bathing cultures from around the world, which is open around the clock. Pay the overnight surcharge, soak, and sleep in the rest areas until the first train. The men's and women's floors swap every month, so you see a different "country" on your next visit.
Spa World, 3-4-24 Ebisu-higashi, Naniwa-ku; about 1 min from Dobutsuen-mae Station Exit 5 (Sakaisuji / Midosuji lines) or JR Shin-Imamiya. 24 hours, with an extra charge overnight; check current fees and the tattoo policy on the official site. Sources: Headout, Expedia, osaka-info.jp.

## Where to Stay in Osaka to Live Like a Local
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-live-like-a-local
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Namba and Umeda are the easy choices, and for a first trip we still suggest them. But if you want to buy dinner where locals buy it, drink where office workers drink and wake up to a quiet street, these two neighbourhoods give you that without making the sights hard to reach.
Times checked 23 November 2026 · train times are approximate
Our pick · Tenma and Tenjinbashisuji
Tenma
1 stop from Osaka Station
Tenma sits around JR Tenma Station and Ogimachi, north of the city centre. Japan's longest covered shopping street runs straight through it, and the back alleys north of the station, known as Ura-Tenma, are packed with tiny izakaya under hundreds of lanterns. At night it is lively, but it is local-lively: office workers and neighbours, not tour groups.
Tenjinbashisuji: about 2.6 km of local shops under one roof.

To Osaka Station
For Kyoto trains, the airport express and Universal Studios connections.

Sakaisuji Line
≈10 min
South to Nipponbashi
Ten minutes to the Namba side for Dotonbori and Kuromon.
Why we suggest it: you get the local life on foot and the big sights by train, and dinner and drinks usually cost less than on the main tourist strips.

Small lanes and small bars: Tenma after dark.
For food lovers · Tsuruhashi
Tsuruhashi
direct to Namba and Nara
Osaka's Korean neighbourhood, famous for yakiniku. The market lanes start right outside the station, and Miyuki-dori Koreatown is a 10 to 15 minute walk south. Three lines meet here, which makes it a smart base if Nara is on your list.

Who it suits, honestly
Go local if…
it's your second trip, you love food, you want quieter mornings, or you're staying four nights or more.
Stay central if…
it's your first trip and you have two or three nights. Namba or Umeda saves you time. See where to stay in Osaka.
Local Osaka after dark: small lanes, small bars, neighbours rather than tour groups.
One more thing: the free ferries locals commute on
Osaka still runs eight free city ferries across its rivers, and people use them to get to work, school and the shops. Ride one, for example the Senbonmatsu ferry in Taisho, which leaves about every 15 minutes, and you are standing among bikes and commuters, not tourists. The ride takes a few minutes, costs nothing, and shows you the water-city side of Osaka that most visitors never see.
Osaka City ferries: 8 routes, free for pedestrians and bicycles; most run from early morning to about 19:00–21:30, no service on 1 January, and they stop in bad weather. Sources: Osaka City Construction Bureau, Taisho Ward Office.

## Local Markets in Osaka Beyond Kuromon
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-local-markets
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

If you have already walked Kuromon, or you'd rather skip the crowds, we suggest one of these three. Each one is a short subway or loop-line ride from Namba or Umeda, and each has a different feel: a chef's wholesale market, a post-war maze of Korean food stalls, and a 2.6 km covered street that locals use every day.
Hours and access checked 23 November 2026 against osaka-info.jp and the markets' own sites
Market 1 · For a seafood breakfast
Kizu Wholesale Market
3 min from Daikokucho
A private wholesale market with more than 300 years of history, where restaurant chefs buy fish, vegetables and dried goods. Visitors can walk in and buy too. It is quieter and less polished than Kuromon, which is exactly the point.
Walk
3 min
From Daikokucho Exit 1
Osaka Metro Midosuji or Yotsubashi Line. One stop south of Namba.
Best time
8:30–10:30
Go early
Stalls open around dawn for chefs and many close by late morning.
Closed
Sun + hols
Check the calendar
Also some Wednesdays and 31 Dec to 4 Jan. The calendar is on kizu-ichiba.com.
Our suggestion: skip hotel breakfast once. Take the subway one stop from Namba to Daikokucho and eat a seafood bowl at the market, then walk back toward Namba.
Market 2 · For grilled meat and kimchi
Tsuruhashi Market
right outside the station
A maze of narrow covered lanes that grew out of a post-war street market around Tsuruhashi Station. Today it is six markets and shopping streets full of yakiniku restaurants, Korean grocers, fish stalls and clothing shops. Walk 10 to 15 minutes south and you reach Miyuki-dori, Japan's largest Koreatown.
Station
0 min
Tsuruhashi Station
JR Osaka Loop Line, Kintetsu and the Osaka Metro Sennichimae Line all stop here.
From Namba
1 line
Direct from Namba
The Sennichimae Line runs straight from Namba to Tsuruhashi. Kintetsu trains from Osaka-Namba stop here too.
On foot
10–15 min
Miyuki-dori Koreatown
About 150 Korean grocers, restaurants and shops along one street.
Our suggestion: come hungry in the evening for yakiniku, or late morning to walk the food lanes. Many small shops prefer cash.
Market 3 · For an everyday Osaka walk
Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
2.6 km, covered
Said to be the longest shopping street in Japan, running about 2.6 km north from Tenjinbashi. Around 600 shops, from fish and pickles to croquettes and old coffee shops. It grew up as the approach to Osaka Tenmangu Shrine and takes about 40 minutes to walk end to end.
Length
2.6 km
Covered all the way
A good rainy-day walk. Start at Minamimorimachi and head north.
Stations
4
Easy to join anywhere
Minamimorimachi, Ogimachi and Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome (Osaka Metro), and JR Tenma.
Shrine
2-chome
Osaka Tenmangu
The shrine the street grew around. Home of the Tenjin Festival every 24–25 July.
Bonus · For the curious
Osaka Central Wholesale Market
≈10 min from JR Noda
Osaka's main city market, the second-largest market complex in Japan by trading volume after Tokyo's Toyosu. It is not a shopping market and you can't join the auctions, but the restaurants inside are open to everyone and guided tours run on weekday mornings if you book by phone.
Want markets on your doorstep?Stay near Namba. Kizu is one subway stop away and Tsuruhashi is one line away.
Kuromon and Kizu both within reach before breakfast

The airport train stops at Namba
See hotels near Namba →Opens Booking.com, already searched for Namba. Pick your dates.
Prefer a guide?A local food guide can take you through the market stalls and explain what you're eating.
Market food tours
One more thing: sushi inside the wholesale market
For one more market, go to Endo, a sushi counter inside Osaka's Central Wholesale Market in Fukushima, open since 1907. It serves "tsukami-zushi": warm, loosely pressed rice under fish bought in the market that morning, five pieces to a plate, and you brush on your own soy sauce. It was named one of Tabelog's top 100 sushi restaurants in west Japan, and it opens early, so going for breakfast beats the lunch queue.
Chuo Ichiba Endo, inside Osaka Central Wholesale Market (Noda 1-1-86, Fukushima-ku); about 620 m from Tamagawa Station. Opens early morning; credit cards not accepted. Sources: Tabelog (Sushi WEST Hyakumeiten 2021), Retty, GIGAZINE.

## Tenma & Tenjinbashisuji: Where Osaka Locals Actually Eat
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tenma-tenjinbashisuji-local-guide
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Key facts:
- Where: JR Tenma is one stop from Osaka Station on the Osaka Loop Line (JR Pass valid); the Sakaisuji Line stops at Minamimorimachi, Ogimachi and Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome.
- Tenjinbashisuji: about 2.6 km of covered shopping street, said to be Japan's longest.
- Harukoma sushi: plates from about ¥100, open 11:00–21:30, closed Tuesdays; go mid-afternoon for the shortest queue.
- Evenings: the standing bars of Ura-Tenma, north of JR Tenma, fill up after six.

Most visitors eat in Dotonbori and never see this side of Osaka. One stop from Osaka Station, Tenma is where office workers drink after work and families do their daily shopping, under a roof that runs for about 2.6 km. If you have one free evening in Osaka and you care about food, we'd spend it here.
About a 4-minute read · facts checked 23 November 2026
Who Tenma suits, and who it doesn't
Good fit
Food-first travellers who want local prices and fewer tour groups
Couples and friends who want a night out without a long ride home
Anyone using Osaka Station for day trips: it's one stop away
Rainy days: the main street is covered end to end
Think twice
Light sleepers: the lanes north of JR Tenma stay loud late
Big-name luxury hotels: those are in Umeda
Very young kids at night: the busiest bars are small, smoky and standing-only
Getting there
JR Tenma Station is one stop from Osaka Station on the Osaka Loop Line, and a JR Pass covers it. By subway, the Sakaisuji Line stops at Minamimorimachi, Ogimachi and Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome, all on the shopping street. Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome is also on the Tanimachi Line, and some Hankyu trains from Kyoto run straight through to it, so check the departure board if you're coming that way.
Eat like a local
Tenjinbashisuji is said to be Japan's longest shopping street: about 2.6 km, roughly 40 minutes end to end if you never stop, which you will. Most shops are small, family-run and priced for people who live here.
Counter sushi is the local lunch on this street.
Harukoma (sushi): the oldest sushi shop on the street and the one with the queue. Pieces are big and plates start at around ¥100. At the tables you write your order on a slip of paper, and the chefs work fast. It's open 11:00 to 21:30 and closed on Tuesdays. Go mid-afternoon for the shortest line. Sushi Masa, almost opposite, is the local alternative when the queue is too long.
Croquettes from the butchers: meat shops along the arcade fry korokke at the counter for a few hundred yen. This is the real walking snack here, more than takoyaki.
Standing bars (tachinomi) north of JR Tenma: the lanes called Ura-Tenma fill up after six. Order a drink and two or three small plates, then move on. Hopping is the point.
Takoyaki: yes, it's here too, usually cheaper and with shorter lines than in Dotonbori.
Fresh-fried croquettes: the snack locals actually buy here.
Cash tip: many small stalls and standing bars still prefer cash. Carry coins and ¥1,000 notes.
After six, the alleys off Tenma Station turn into one long bar crawl.
🍶 First time bar-hopping in Japan? Several small-group food walks start at JR Tenma in the evening and take you through three or four standing bars in about three hours, so you learn how to order instead of pointing at a menu.Let a local walk you through Ura-Tenma →
A half-day walking route
10:00 Start at Osaka Tenmangu Shrine, the shrine that gave Tenma its name. It's quiet in the morning and a short walk from Minamimorimachi Station.
10:30 Walk north up the arcade and snack as you go: croquettes, rice crackers, fruit.
12:00 Lunch at Harukoma, or any busy set-meal shop with locals waiting outside.
13:30 Keep going towards 6-chome, where the arcade gets calmer and more residential.
15:00 Back to your hotel for a rest. Tenma is at its best after dark.
18:30 Ura-Tenma, north of JR Tenma: two or three standing bars, then a late bowl of ramen.
Late morning: snack your way up the arcade
Afternoon: the side lanes get quieter
After dark: Ura-Tenma fills up
Where to stay: three good bases
For food and nights out
JR Tenma / Ogimachi
Walk home from the bars
Osaka Station is one stop away. The lanes right by the north exit are loud, so pick a hotel on the south or Ogimachi side.
Stay where Osaka's nightlife is a two-minute stroll →
For day trips
6-chome Tenjinbashisuji
Quieter streets, trains at the door
Two subway lines and through Hankyu trains, and the food is still five minutes away. The easiest base here for a day in Kyoto.
Wake up quiet, be in Kyoto by mid-morning →
For sightseeing
Minami­morimachi
By the shrine
The south end of the arcade: the shortest trip from here to Osaka Castle and Nakanoshima, with the arcade still on your doorstep.
Start your mornings at the shrine gate →
📅 Good to know before you book
Cherry blossom week (mid-April): the Japan Mint, about 15 minutes' walk from Temmabashi Station, opens its roughly 560 m cherry blossom lane for about one week. Entry is free but you must reserve online in advance (in 2026 it ran 9 to 15 April, with booking from mid-March). Osaka hotels get much more expensive that week; most offer free cancellation, so booking early costs nothing.
Tenjin Matsuri (24 and 25 July): one of Japan's biggest festivals, centred on Osaka Tenmangu. Hotels near the shrine fill first.
Osaka Museum of Housing and Living: its life-size 1830s Osaka street is closed for renovation until 31 December 2026, and it normally closes on Tuesdays. Check the reopening date before you plan around it.
Pick a sakura-week stay you'll remember for years →
Mid-April in Osaka: the week everyone wants, and the week hotels know it.
Nearby, if you have more time
Osaka Castle: a few subway stops south-east and an easy morning add-on. Sort your castle tickets before you go →
Nakanoshima: riverside museums and a rose garden, a pleasant walk south of the arcade.
Kema Sakuranomiya Park: a long riverside cherry-blossom walk beside the Mint, where locals have their hanami picnics.
One more thing: write your sushi order down
At Harukoma's tables you don't need Japanese: you write your order on a slip of paper (at the counter you just tell the chef). Take a photo of the menu board while you queue, decide in the line, and you'll be eating within minutes of sitting down while everyone else is still reading.
Source: Ekiten and Retty reviews of Harukoma, checked 23 November 2026.

## Narita or Haneda: Which Train Gets You to Your Tokyo Hotel Fastest?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-airport-which-train
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

From Haneda, take Keikyu if you stay in Shinagawa, Asakusa or Yokohama, and the Tokyo Monorail for Hamamatsucho, Tokyo Station and the east side. From Narita, take the Skyliner (about ¥2,470) for Ueno and Asakusa, and the Narita Express (¥3,140–3,330) for Tokyo Station, Shibuya and Shinjuku. The Limousine Bus wins with heavy bags to a hotel it stops at, and after the last train.
Times and fares from the operators' official pages, checked 23 November 2026 · adult fares
Answer A · Landing at Haneda
Keikyu or Tokyo Monorail
11–34 min to most bases
Keikyu runs from Terminal 3 to Shinagawa in 11 minutes, Yokohama in 23 and, with through trains onto the Toei Asakusa Line, to Asakusa in 34 minutes without a change (about ¥599 by IC card). For Shinjuku, change at Shinagawa to JR: about 45 minutes and ¥580 in all. The last train toward Shinagawa leaves Terminal 3 at 00:08 and the first at 05:26.
The Tokyo Monorail reaches Hamamatsucho in 13 minutes on the fastest service (¥519 by IC card), then it is about 7 minutes to Tokyo Station on the JR Yamanote Line. On weekends and holidays its Monorail & Yamanote Line Discount Ticket covers any Haneda terminal to any Yamanote station for ¥590.
To Shinagawa
11 min
Keikyu
Last train from Terminal 3 at 00:08.
To Asakusa
34 min
Keikyu, no change
About ¥599 by IC card.
Hamamatsucho
13 min
Monorail
¥519 by IC card; Yamanote onward.
Keikyu suits Shinagawa, Ginza (Higashi-ginza 23 min), Asakusa and Yokohama hotels. The Monorail suits Hamamatsucho, Tokyo Station and Odaiba-side stays.
Keikyu's red trains run from Haneda straight into the city.
Answer B · Landing at Narita
Narita Express or Keisei Skyliner
¥2,470–3,330
The Skyliner runs from Terminal 2·3 to Nippori in about 36–50 minutes and Keisei Ueno in about 41–57 minutes (Terminal 1 adds about 3 minutes), for ¥2,470. Ueno is 5 minutes from Asakusa on the Ginza Line. Keisei also sells a discounted Skyliner ticket online for visitors. Heading to Asakusa directly with no reserved seat? The Access Express runs there without a change for about ¥1,276 by IC card, but slower.
The Narita Express (N'EX) reaches Tokyo Station in 53 minutes at its fastest (¥3,140 reserved), then continues to Shinagawa, Shibuya and Shinjuku (¥3,330). Visitors with a non-Japanese passport can buy the N'EX Tokyo Round Trip Ticket: ¥5,200 for the trip in and out within 14 days, including JR trains in the Tokyo area to your hotel station.
Skyliner
¥2,470
Nippori / Ueno
About 36–57 min from Terminal 2·3.
N'EX round trip
¥5,200
Both ways, 14 days
Non-Japanese passports only.
Skyliner suits Ueno, Asakusa and Yanaka stays. N'EX suits Tokyo Station, Shinjuku and Shibuya, and is the better deal if you fly in and out of Narita.
On the Narita Express, Tokyo Station is the first big stop.
Answer C · Big bags, late arrivals, groups
Airport Limousine Bus, or a taxi
door drop-off
The Limousine Bus stops at the doors of big hotels, so there are no stairs or transfers with luggage. Haneda to Shinjuku is ¥1,400 and about 40–55 minutes in daytime traffic, with stops at hotels such as Keio Plaza, Hilton Tokyo and Park Hyatt; the last regular bus leaves Terminal 3 at 23:40. After the trains stop, late-night buses leave Terminal 3 at 00:20, 01:00, 01:40 and 02:20 for Shinjuku and Ikebukuro (¥2,800). From Narita the bus to Shinjuku costs ¥3,600 and takes about 2 hours, so it only beats the train if your hotel is on its list.
Taxis: Haneda has fixed fares to central wards, about ¥8,300 to Shinjuku in the daytime plus tolls and more from 22:00 to 5:00, which is reasonable for three or four people after midnight. Narita's fixed fares are ¥29,000–32,500 to central Tokyo plus tolls, a group-only choice.
Suits: travellers with large suitcases whose hotel is a bus stop, and anyone landing at Haneda after midnight. Not for Narita arrivals in a hurry: the bus is slower than N'EX or Skyliner.
The limousine bus trades speed for a door-to-door ride.
Our verdict
We suggest: fly into Haneda if you can, because Keikyu or the Monorail gets you to most bases in under 45 minutes for under ¥600. From Narita, pair the line with the area in our first-trip area guide: Skyliner for Asakusa and Ueno, N'EX for Tokyo Station and Shinjuku (round trip ticket if you also fly out of Narita). Take the Limousine Bus when your hotel is on its route with heavy bags, and after 00:08 at Haneda; a taxi only makes sense at night with three or four people sharing.
See N'EX and Skyliner tickets →Opens Klook. Book in English and pay in your own currency; check how to collect on each listing.
Arriving late with a group? A pre-booked car through Welcome Pickups meets you in arrivals with a name sign. Pay with an IC card on the train: see IC card or subway pass?
One more thing: a temple town 10 minutes from Narita
If you land at Narita with a few hours to spare, or you're flying out late, ride one or two stops to Narita Station instead of going straight to Tokyo. From there, an 800 m street of old wooden shops grilling eel leads to Naritasan Shinshoji, a temple founded in 940. Have unaju (eel on rice) on the way; it is what this town is known for.
About 10–15 min by Keisei or JR from the airport to Keisei-Narita / JR Narita, then about 10 min on foot along Omotesando. The temple is free. Sources: JAL Guide to Japan, JNTO (japan.travel), All About Japan.

## Getting Around Tokyo: IC Card, JR or Metro, and Is the Subway Pass Worth It?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-ic-card-or-subway-pass
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

Get a Suica or PASMO on arrival (Welcome Suica, TOURIST PASMO, or Apple Wallet on an iPhone) and tap it on every train, subway and bus. Add the Tokyo Subway Ticket (¥1,000 for 24 hours up to ¥2,000 for 72 hours since March 2026) only if you will ride Tokyo Metro and Toei about three or more times a day, because it does not cover JR.
Fares from JR East, Tokyo Metro and Toei official pages, checked 23 November 2026 · adult IC fares
Answer A · The card everyone should have
Suica or PASMO, card or phone
no deposit for visitor cards
The card shortage is over: regular Suica and PASMO went back on sale on 1 March 2025, with a ¥500 deposit. Visitors have no-deposit options. Welcome Suica comes loaded with ¥1,000 to ¥10,000, works for 28 days, and is sold at JR East Travel Service Centers (Narita, Haneda Terminal 3, Tokyo, Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ueno and more) and Welcome Suica machines at the airport stations; leftover balance is not refunded and top-ups are cash only. The TOURIST PASMO (since May 2026) is sold at airport stations, also for 28 days. On an iPhone, add Suica or PASMO directly in Apple Wallet and top up with your own card; JR East's Welcome Suica Mobile app lasts 180 days.
Welcome Suica
28 days
No deposit
Balance not refunded, so load modestly.
Cheaper by IC
¥178 vs ¥180
Subway minimum
IC fares are slightly below paper tickets.
Covers JR, subways, private railways and buses, plus many convenience stores and vending machines. Android phones need Osaifu-Keitai (usually phones sold in Japan), so most Android users should carry a physical card.
Tap and go: IC cards open every gate in Tokyo.
Answer B · Why prices differ
JR lines vs Tokyo Metro and Toei
three companies, three fares
Tokyo's trains belong to different companies, and each charges its own fare. The green JR Yamanote Line is the backbone: a loop of 30 stations taking about an hour, linking Shinjuku, Shibuya, Tokyo, Ueno and Shinagawa. Since JR East's fare revision on 14 March 2026 its minimum fare is ¥155 by IC card; Tokyo Metro and Toei start at ¥178. The same trip can differ: Shinjuku to Tokyo Station is ¥253 on JR (14 minutes) but ¥209 on the Marunouchi Line (18 minutes). Shinjuku to Asakusa is about ¥272 on Toei lines but ¥387 if you mix JR and the Ginza Line.
Same trip
¥209 vs ¥253
Shinjuku to Tokyo
Metro is cheaper; JR is 4 min faster.
Yamanote
30 stations
About an hour round
Not covered by the subway pass.
Rule of thumb: staying on one company end to end is usually cheapest. With an IC card you never need to work this out at a ticket machine; the gates charge the right fare.
The Yamanote loop is JR, so a subway pass doesn't cover it.
Answer C · The visitor pass
Tokyo Subway Ticket (24 / 48 / 72 h)
¥1,000 / ¥1,500 / ¥2,000
Prices rose on 14 March 2026 to ¥1,000, ¥1,500 and ¥2,000 (children half). It covers every Tokyo Metro and Toei subway line, not JR, and is sold to visitors from abroad and people living outside the Kanto area, at Narita and Haneda airports, Toei tourist information centres, many hotels and electronics stores, and online. The maths: the 72-hour ticket works out at about ¥667 a day. With typical subway rides of ¥209–¥272, three rides a day roughly breaks even and four clearly wins. The 24-hour ticket needs about four or five rides in a day.
72 h per day
≈¥667
Pays off at
About 3 subway rides a day.
24 h
¥1,000
Pays off at
About 4–5 rides that day.
Suits: visitors based in Asakusa, Ginza or Ueno who hop between sights by subway. Does not suit a Shinjuku or Shibuya base where most trips are on JR, or slow days with one or two rides.
Metro and Toei lines are where the Subway Ticket pays off.
Our verdict
We suggest: everyone taps an IC card; it is slightly cheaper than paper tickets and works on every line. Add the 72-hour Tokyo Subway Ticket only if you are staying on a subway line (Asakusa, Ginza, Ueno) and plan three or more subway rides a day, roughly a full sightseeing day across town. Skip it if your hotel is by a JR station and your days run along the Yamanote Line, or if you plan day trips out of Tokyo on those days.
See the Tokyo Subway Ticket →Opens Klook. Book in English; check where to collect on the listing.
Data on your phone helps with route planning from the first minute: an Airalo Japan eSIM can be installed before you fly.
One more thing: Tokyo's last tram
Your IC card also works on the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line), the only one of Tokyo's old city tram lines still running. It rattles 12.2 km through backstreets between Minowabashi and Waseda, past Oji and Asukayama, for a flat fare. You tap on as you board at the front and get off at the back, and it shows you a side of Tokyo the subway never will.
Flat fare ¥170 (IC ¥168), children ¥90 (IC ¥84); Toden 1-Day Pass ¥400. 30 stops; services every few minutes. Source: Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation (Toei).

## First Trip to Tokyo: Which Area Should You Stay In?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/tokyo-where-to-stay-first-trip
City: Tokyo · Facts checked: 2026-11-23

For most first trips we suggest Shinjuku: it has the most lines, the Narita Express and late food, and a well-rated double for two started around ¥12,500 on our sample weeknight. Pick Tokyo Station if you will take the Shinkansen two or more times. Pick Asakusa if your budget for two is under about ¥16,000 a night or you land at Narita and ride the Skyliner.
Booking.com prices for 2 adults, Wed 16–Thu 17 Dec 2026, hotels rated 7+, checked 23 November 2026 · train times from Ekitan and JR East
Answer A · For nightlife, shopping and the most trains
Shinjuku (or Shibuya)
middle ≈¥18,000 for two
Shinjuku is the world's busiest station by Guinness World Records' count (about 2.7 million passengers a day in 2022), and that is the point: JR, Keio, Odakyu, Tokyo Metro and Toei all meet here, so most of the city is one ride away. Tokyo Station is 14 minutes on the JR Chuo Rapid Line (¥253 by IC card) and the Narita Express stops here. On our date the first 20 well-rated hotels started at about ¥12,500 and the middle price was about ¥18,100, for example Rosenheim Tokyo Shinjuku (rated 9.2) at ¥15,145 and Villa Fontaine Tokyo Shinjuku (8.5) at ¥18,434. Shibuya ran higher on the same night.
To Tokyo Stn
14 min
JR Chuo Rapid
¥253 by IC card, no change.
To Asakusa
26–28 min
One change
Toei lines about ¥272, or JR + Ginza Line.
Suits: first-timers who want evenings out and simple day trips west. Not ideal if crowds wear you down: the station's size is real. Which side of the station matters too, see "Shinjuku" on the booking: which station? For Shibuya with quieter nights, see a quieter base near Shibuya.
Shinjuku after dark: trains at the door, dinner on every corner.
Answer B · For Shinkansen day trips and quieter evenings
Tokyo Station / Ginza / Nihonbashi
middle ≈¥22,000 for two
Six Shinkansen lines start at Tokyo Station (Tokaido toward Kyoto and Osaka, Tohoku, Hokkaido, Akita, Yamagata, Joetsu and Hokuriku), so a 7 a.m. train to Kyoto is a short walk, not a cross-town ride. The fastest Narita Express reaches Tokyo Station in 53 minutes, and Ueno is 8 minutes away on JR. The catch is price: within 1 km of the station the middle price was about ¥22,000, and about ¥25,000 in Ginza. The better-value finds were a little out, such as Tosei Hotel Cocone Kanda (rated 8.5, 900 m) at about ¥14,000 with tax.
Shinkansen
6 lines
Start here
Including the Tokaido line to Kyoto and Osaka.
To Ueno
8 min
JR Keihin-Tohoku
¥199 by IC card; 9 min on the Yamanote.
Suits: travellers with two or more day trips (Kyoto, Nikko, Karuizawa) or an early Narita Express, and couples who prefer calm evenings. Does not suit late-night plans: office districts go quiet after dinner.
Tokyo Station's Marunouchi side, where the Shinkansen lines start.
Answer C · For lower prices and the Skyliner
Asakusa (or Ueno)
middle ≈¥15,800 in Asakusa
Asakusa was the cheapest of the three on our date: the middle price was about ¥15,800, with Tosei Hotel Cocone Asakusa Kuramae (rated 8.6) at ¥13,860 and The Kanzashi Tokyo Asakusa (8.8) at ¥15,048. Ueno was not cheaper than Shinjuku on the same night (middle about ¥18,400 within 1 km), but it is where the Keisei Skyliner from Narita ends, about 41–57 minutes from the airport. Ueno to Asakusa is 5 minutes on the Ginza Line, and Shibuya is 34 minutes direct from Asakusa.
Asakusa saving
≈¥2,300 /night
vs Shinjuku middle
Same date, same filters, two adults.
To Shinjuku
26–28 min
One change
Allow more for western sights.
Suits: budget-minded first-timers, Narita arrivals on the Skyliner, and anyone who wants Senso-ji at quiet hours (morning or evening?). Does not suit a trip built around Shibuya and Shinjuku nights. To pay less still, look across the river from Asakusa.
Asakusa: Senso-ji's gate, a short walk from the cheaper rooms.
Our verdict
We suggest: Shinjuku for a mixed first trip, because nearly every line and the Narita Express are at the door and well-rated rooms started around ¥12,500 for two. Switch to Tokyo Station as soon as you have two or more Shinkansen day trips, since you save a cross-town ride each early morning. Switch to Asakusa when your limit for two is under about ¥16,000 a night on your dates, or when you arrive at Narita and want the Skyliner to Ueno.
See hotels in Shinjuku →Opens Booking.com. Check the walk to the station on each listing.
Prefer the other bases? Tokyo Station area · Asakusa. Prices on Booking.com are the same as booking direct; it simply lets you book in English with free cancellation where the listing says so.
One more thing: Tokyo's kitchen street
If you stay on the Asakusa/Ueno side, spend an hour on Kappabashi, an 800 m street of about 170 shops that supply Tokyo's restaurants. You'll find chefs' knives, lacquerware, noren curtains and the plastic food samples you see in every restaurant window. People come for the range rather than low prices. Go on a weekday: more than half the shops close on Sundays.
Kappabashi Dougu Street, Matsugaya / Nishi-Asakusa, Taito-ku; about 5 min from Tawaramachi (Ginza line). Most shops roughly 10:00–17:00 Mon–Sat. Some sample shops run hands-on workshops by reservation. Sources: GO TOKYO, LIVE JAPAN, GLTJP, NAVITIME.

## Where to stay in Osaka: Namba, Umeda or Tennoji?
URL: https://japanbystation.com/osaka-where-to-stay
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-22

Osaka is easy. All three of these areas sit on the same red subway line, so wherever you sleep, the other two are under 15 minutes away. The real question is what you want outside your door.
Times checked 22 November 2026

Namba
Food, neon and the airport train at your door.
1What it's like
This is the Osaka on postcards: neon over the canal, takoyaki on every corner and streets that stay busy late. The airport train from Kansai ends right here, so you can be eating dinner within an hour of landing.

A 12-metre lion head said to swallow bad luck. Free to visit.

Area 2 of 3

Umeda
Kyoto in 29 minutes, straight from the station.
1What it's like
Umeda is modern Osaka, built around JR Osaka Station, the city's biggest hub. Think department stores, rooftop views and underground food halls. If Kyoto, Nara or Universal Studios are on your list, this is the easiest base: direct trains leave from here. Not sure which "Umeda" station or which side? See Osaka Station vs Umeda.

Area 3 of 3
Photo: Sarmat Batagov / Pexels
Tennoji
30 minutes from the airport, no change.
1What it's like
Tennoji is where old Osaka meets a 300-metre skyscraper. One side of the station has Abeno Harukas and big malls. Walk the other way and you are in Shinsekai, a retro maze of fried-skewer bars under Tsutenkaku Tower. Hotels here usually cost a little less than in Namba or Umeda.
2What's nearby
2–3 minon foot
Abeno Harukas
A 300 m tower with an observation deck and a huge department store.
5–10 minon foot
Tennoji Zoo
One of Japan's oldest zoos. Adults pay ¥500.
≈15 minon foot
Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku
Loud signs, cheap eats and kushikatsu, the deep-fried skewers Osaka is known for.

Also worth knowing
Shin-OsakaThe bullet train station. Kyoto in 13–15 minutes, but little to do around it. Good for one night before the Shinkansen.
Universal CityHotels 5 minutes from the park gate. Worth it for two park days; for one, Umeda is 15 minutes away.
One more thing: a 1920s street under a skyscraper
If you stay in Umeda, go down to the basement of the Umeda Sky Building to Takimi Koji, a food alley built to look like an Osaka street from the early Showa era, with cobblestones, tiled roofs, old posters and a small shrine. Around 20 restaurants serve okonomiyaki, kushikatsu and other Osaka staples, and you can wander it for free after the sunset from the rooftop.
Takimi Koji, Umeda Sky Building B1F, 1-1-88 Oyodonaka, Kita-ku; about 7–9 min from JR Osaka Station. Hours vary by restaurant. Sources: Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp), GLTJP. Checked 23 November 2026.

## Things to do around Namba, all within a 15-minute walk
URL: https://japanbystation.com/namba
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-22

Namba is the easiest part of Osaka to explore on foot. Leave Namba Station by Exit 14 and the canal, the food streets and the shopping arcades are all within a few minutes. Here is how it fits together.
Walking times from Osaka Metro Namba Station · checked 22 November 2026
Part 1 · The canal
Dotonbori
3–5 min on foot
The canal is the heart of Namba. Giant 3D signs hang over the restaurants, the Glico running man glows above Ebisu Bridge, and the whole strip gets brighter after dark.
3–5 minon foot
Dotonbori canal
Walk the riverside path at night when the signs reflect in the water.
3–5 minon foot
The giant signs
A moving crab, a giant octopus and more. Half the fun is spotting them all.
Every
30 min
Tombori River Cruise
A short boat ride under the bridges. Departures on the hour and half hour, 11:00 to 21:00.
Best timeCome once in daylight for the shops and once after 7 pm for the neon. It's the same street, but it feels like a different city.
Part 2 · Eat
Street food and markets
Osaka calls itself Japan's kitchen, and Namba is where you taste it. Eat standing up, try small portions, and move on to the next stall.
≈8 minon foot
Kuromon Market
Covered market with about 150 shops. Grilled seafood, wagyu skewers, fruit. Best before noon.
3–5 minon foot
Takoyaki
Osaka's octopus balls, cooked to order all along Dotonbori. Let them cool a minute.
5–6 minby subway
Kushikatsu in Shinsekai
For deep-fried skewers, ride two stops south. One rule: don't double dip.
Part 3 · Shop and explore
Arcades and side streets
Namba's covered arcades keep you dry in any weather, and the quieter corners are only a few steps off the main street.
600 mcovered arcade
Shinsaibashi-suji
Fashion, drugstores and snacks under one roof, starting at the canal.
≈8 minon foot
Namba Yasaka Shrine
A 12-metre lion head that swallows bad luck. Free, and quiet in the morning.
On foot
3–5 min
Hozenji Yokocho
A narrow stone alley of old restaurants around a small, moss-covered temple statue.
On foot
3 min
Doguyasuji
The kitchen-supply street. Knives, plastic food samples and every pot you can imagine.
Liked everything on this page?Then sleep in the middle of it. Everything above is a short walk away.
Dotonbori, Kuromon and the arcades on foot
The Kansai Airport train stops at Namba Station
Late-night food on every corner
See what's still free in Namba →Opens Booking.com, already searched for Namba. Pick your dates.
Only one evening here?Let a local walk you through the food stalls. You eat, they explain.
Food tours
One more thing: the lion that swallows bad luck
Ten minutes west of the Namba crowds, in a quiet residential street, is Namba Yasaka Shrine, the local guardian shrine of Namba. Its stage is a 12 m lion's head with a gaping mouth, and the lion is said to swallow evil spirits and bring luck, which is why students and shop owners come to pray here. It's free, and early morning is the quiet time to see it.
Namba Yasaka Shrine, 2-9-19 Motomachi, Naniwa-ku; about 6–10 min from Namba Station. Open daily from early morning to about 17:00, free. Sources: JR West (New Golden Route), GLTJP (supervised by the shrine), Japan Cheapo.

## Kansai Airport to Osaka: which train for your hotel
URL: https://japanbystation.com/kansai-airport-to-osaka
City: Osaka · Facts checked: 2026-11-22

The short version: Nankai trains go to Namba. JR trains go to Tennoji, Osaka Station and Shin-Osaka. Both leave from Kansai Airport Station, across the walkway from Terminal 1 (Terminal 2 passengers take a shuttle bus first). Choose by where you're sleeping.
Times from Kansai Airport's official access page · checked 22 November 2026
Which train for your hotel
To NambaNankai Rapi:t
34–39 min
Reserved seats, big luggage space, the fastest way to Namba.
¥970 + seat chargeNankai lists the seat charge at ¥700. Older guides still say ¥520.
To NambaNankai Airport Express
43 min
No reservation, just tap in. Only a few minutes slower than Rapi:t.
about ¥970The best value if you're travelling light.
To TennojiJR Haruka
30 min
Reserved and unreserved cars. Also stops at Osaka Station and Shin-Osaka.
about ¥1,840Base fare plus the unreserved express charge.
To Osaka Station (Umeda)JR Haruka
45–50 min
Direct, no change. Haruka now stops at Osaka Station, on the underground platforms by the West Gate: which side of the station for your hotel.
check fareJR fares vary by ticket type. Confirm before you buy.
To Osaka Station (Umeda)JR Airport Rapid
65 min
Slower but cheaper, no seat charge. 45 minutes to Tennoji on the way.
about ¥1,180
To Shin-OsakaJR Haruka
50 min
For a bullet train connection, stay on Haruka to the end of its Osaka stops.
check fare
Going straight to Universal Studios?Take the JR Airport Rapid to Nishikujo and change to the line for Universal City, 65–75 minutes in total. Or take the direct airport bus, about 50–70 minutes.

Still choosing a hotel?See which area fits your trip, with walking times to the sights.
Where to stay in Osaka
One more thing: a sunset one stop from the airport
Flying out late? Get off one stop before the airport, at Rinku Town (every train except the Haruka stops there), and walk about five minutes to Rinku Park. It faces Kansai Airport across the water, so you watch planes take off over Osaka Bay, and its Marble Beach sunset is on Japan's list of 100 best sunsets. It's free, open 24 hours, and a better last hour than the departure lounge.
Rinku Park, 1-271 Rinku Orai-kita, Izumisano; about 300 m (4–5 min) from Nankai/JR Rinku Town Station. Open 24 hours, free. Sources: Osaka Convention & Tourism Bureau (osaka-info.jp), Nankai Railway, GLTJP.
